...by the increase of the disease-causing cause, but rather from an abundance of good nourishment and healthy juice <term>enchymi</term><note>original: "enchymi" — refers to well-digested, nutritive juices or chyme in the body</note>. So it was that evil would most certainly arise from the very source where others prophesied good would come<gloss>1</gloss>, those who mocked me with secret laughter. And when I strove to wash away and strengthen my assertion with wine—namely, that a moderate drink of wine would fortify a patient, whom an excess of that same wine would otherwise make prone to much spitting. But since they would not fall at a single stroke of the weapon <note>A metaphorical way of saying his opponents would not concede the argument easily</note>, I descended to the experience of the Lent and the Easter just
<margin>72.</margin> passed. I noted that, to be sure, from Easter onwards the patient would spit more copiously and snore more distressingly. But during fasts, he would have been scarcely, or at least little, mindful of these things. Therefore, for the decision of the question, I said there was need of proof, and that at least as much should be deferred to me as to the other unsuccessful helpers thus far. Wherefore, under a more sparse and harder diet (which would indeed satisfy a hungry stomach in digestion, although not providing the desired abundance of <term>vital blood</term><note>original: "cruoris"</note>), immediately the <term>upright-breathing</term><note>original: "orthopnoea" — a condition where a patient can only breathe comfortably when sitting or standing straight up</note> was diminished; which then, by a continued moderation of abstinence, gave quiet nights. For just as when the lung is ill-affected, more waste-like phlegm is produced: so the more copious the matter present, the more that same waste abounds. Because this does not happen except from matter closely disposed to it. For neither that phlegm—whether it be thin and watery, or finally thicker or more tenacious—comes from anything except a mass of matter more related and disposed to it. Which being lacking, the vital blood itself is transmuted and migrates into waste of this kind. There is, to be sure, a watery <term>fluid</term><note>original: "latex" — Van Helmont’s term for a neutral, watery liquor in the body that is not yet blood</note> in the body wandering through all the veins, taking on various masks of watery waste and putting on their forms: no differently than water in which linden bark or comfrey root have soaked mimics the appearance of phlegm. Even the white of an egg is milky on the first day, which soon, by a spontaneous motion, takes on the thickness of glue.

<column-break/>

This is seen more clearly in a <term>Head Cold</term><note>original: "Corizza"</note>; 
<margin>73.</margin> where the fluid that drips in the first days is like salty water: then in the following days it becomes mucous. In <term>Consumption</term><note>original: "Phthisis" — a wasting disease of the lungs, often tuberculosis</note>, however, while the spit begins to turn mucous from the blood, at first the mucus appears yellow and thick, which then turns ashen, and finally verges more toward black. Because then they are the wastes of transmuted blood, no longer merely mixtures of the body's watery fluid. In this way, of course, both <term>Guardians</term><note>original: "custos" — the vital spirit or Archaeus governing an organ</note>—who first manufacture thick mucus from the fluid—then, when the Guardian wanders in error, it immediately turns into a watery flood, and is thickened again as soon as the Guardian's error is corrected. For the Guardian, of both the Brain and the Lung, is subjected to various injuries and inclemencies of the air, and therefore calls for fluid from everywhere, swollen with error, so that he forces it to go back or depart into waste equal to his own suffering. Therefore, from the mass of the fluid, mucous wastes of this kind are formed, upon which mass a certain harmful stain of error is sometimes impressed, so that the more liquid and immature blood is transmuted together into mucus. Violently, to be sure, by both erring Guardians—in both the Lung and the head—the blood itself is alienated into mucus, no differently than blood in an ulcer assumes the form of pus or bloody discharge. And so, besides the aforementioned alterations of both Guardians: a frequent impression is branded upon individual parts, by which the digestion of each member is powerfully harmed or turned inward. In which case, I call such a bad impression the "tormentor of the member," the "hinderer of digestion," and the "depraver of the final nourishment." Around which, truly, the whole aim and pivot of healing ought to turn. The Guardian of the larynx, therefore, is provoked from above by the injuries of the air, as well as from below, by the internal indisposition of its own Lung. So let these things be regarding the mass dedicated to the Guardians, and regarding the mass sprinkled for the final nourishment of the limbs. In which, whatever is corrupted by a defect of integrity...

...vitiated: this also grows into the occasions of many infirmities. And the worse the mass or immediate material from which it flows, the more powerful is the stimulus for the diseases born from it. Consequently, abstinence and the satiety of many nutritious foods <term>enchymi</term><note>original: "enchymi" — refers to the healthy, well-digested juices or "chyme" of the body</note> are fertile means for both healing and causing sickness. Therefore, every fluid <term>Latex</term><note>In Van Helmont’s system, "Latex" is a specific internal fluid distinct from blood and urine that can become diseased and cause swelling or phlegm</note> does not rush headlong from the head, even if it presents itself to us in the form of mucus, egg-white, discharge, pus, or honey-like cysts. For by the error of digestions and other impressions, sins and vices of the organs occur, manifesting in diverse forms. This must certainly be noted diligently and with a "steel pen" <note>an idiom meaning to record something permanently and unforgettably</note> where the healings and remedies of infirmities are intended.

<margin>74.</margin>
The error of Cauteries <note>the practice of burning the skin or creating artificial sores to "drain" bad humors</note> is confirmed here. For fontanelles <note>artificial weeping sores kept open by a physician</note> help in some places, not indeed because they evacuate the material of a Catarrh descending from above, or because they divert, draw out, or pull it elsewhere: but insofar as they diminish the total mass of both the *Latex* and the nutritive blood <term>cruoris</term>. Meanwhile, these fontanelles do nothing to remove or even consider the error of the organs or the disease characterized therein. This is because they do not remove or moderate the "domestic destroyer" or the morbid indisposition. And therefore, Catarrhs do not fall downwards; rather, defects are simply created by that destroyer in the part where it lives, or where it has its object and rule.

<margin>75.</margin>
At this stage, we consider barley waters <term>ptisanæ</term>, sarsaparilla <term>zarzæ</term>, China root, and the like, which, besides providing an elemental drink, are far removed from true nutrition and substantial, seed-like nutritious food. Therefore, they cannot help but take away from the mass of the body's absorption. For this is the "dryness" which Physicians intend to bring about with the aforementioned drink and decoctions. Not insofar as they dry out descending humors or phlegm (for among philosophers, moist things do not dry out humors), but insofar as they diminish the nutritive mass of the blood, which

<column-break/>

they then restore with plenty of nutritious food <term>enchymo</term> brought in from elsewhere, and thus make themselves look ridiculous by the effect that usually follows. Surely, moderation in food could achieve more than any tearing of the skin, or cruel burning by fires, or the drinking of barbarous woods and roots. These things which I have said, therefore, are supplementary to the treatises on the *Latex*, on Cauteries, on the Erring Guardian, and on Catarrhs.

<margin>76.</margin>
Meanwhile, I wonder greatly that they thought to help the lungs with sweets, electuaries <term>eclegmatis</term><note>original: "eclegmatis" — thick, syrupy medicines intended to be licked or swallowed slowly</note>, and ointments. They fixated on "fox lung" <note>a traditional remedy based on the idea that because foxes have great endurance, their lungs must cure breathing problems</note>, because they knew the fox runs until tired; and they would institute healings with cooked or macerated coltsfoot <term>tussilagine</term>, drunk or licked in various ways. These are means that are not admitted immediately to the affected place, and mediately, they are robbed of their original strength. But the Schools <note>traditional university medical authorities</note> never considered that if the patient himself crushed the remedies daily while his nostrils were blocked, he could draw certain remedies to the lung itself by breathing in a very fine powder of the crushed materials. By this method, he could apply his balms immediately to the affected place. But this was in vain: therefore, syrupy medicines are even more useless, as they are not even delivered to the lung. Likewise, they have neglected

<margin>77.</margin>
a profitable method used until now, through which they might immediately connect the smoke of sulfur to a drink; this smoke then gradually unfolds itself together with the drink into all the veins: not as a form of nourishment, but only as a seasoning, just as that same smoke frees and preserves a cask of wine from corruption. For nothing has been thought of until now regarding the way and the "companion of the paths" by which they might make a remedy penetrate, which otherwise is not admitted very deeply on its own. And although they saw through their syrups and electuaries that they had accomplished nothing in thousands of cases, except for filling their own purses; yet without further investigation, they have always persisted in that same muddy rut until now.

<margin>1.</margin> <image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'A' showing a scholar in a robe within an ornate frame.</image-desc>As I am about to speak of the *Latex* <note>Van Helmont uses "Latex" to describe a specific internal water distinct from blood and urine, which he believes traditional medicine ignored</note>, a unique and hitherto neglected fluid, I must first prove whether it exists, or what it is. Then, I must discuss its use and necessities, or the ends and purposes it serves. Before all these things, however, it is helpful to briefly explain what I mean by that unusual name. Truly, besides the single nutritional liquid openly and publicly known, which they call *cruor* <note>original: "cruorem" — the thick, red part of the blood</note>, there floats in it a certain watery liquid, which is not only the material substrate for saliva, tears, sweat, thin mucus, and swelling,

<column-break/>

<margin>2.</margin> but is also notable for various uses. The Schools <note>The "Schools" refers to the established medical universities following the ancient Greek traditions of Galen</note> have indeed mentioned it under the name of "whey of the blood" (*serum sanguinis*), and they have made it common to both urine and sweat. But I shall surely show that this same fluid is far different in its matter and its uses; and consequently, it should not be counted among the excrements, but among the useful juices. I call it the *Latex*, rather than a <margin>3.</margin> "humor," so that the abuse of names might be removed. I have already demonstrated clearly enough through my books that the quaternary of "humors" <note>The four humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note>—which the Schools have expanded upon through repeated centuries of commentaries and introduced like actors into the tragedies of all diseases—never existed in human nature. That book is titled *The Passive Deception of the Humorist Schools*, to distinguish it from "active" deception, lest I seem to accuse them of the malice of stubbornness rather than a failure to realize the truth. For this reason, <margin>4.</margin> a backward ignorance of the essence of the blood-mass has darkened the entire map of healing. Thus, they wish a part of the urine to be left in the blood-mass, even after the urine has been separated, and they call both the urine and this kind of residue of it the "serum of the blood." I have seriously grieved over this lack of distinction, because it has been a wretched nurse to human calamity. For they have called the urine and its residue, which breaks out through sweat, by the single <margin>5.</margin> name of "serum of the blood." Yet they have overlooked its chief purposes. For they soon deflect from that hypothesis of theirs: as soon as anything floats on top of the blood drawn from a vein, they no longer call it "serum," but "bile," "choler," or "gall," and name it one of the four constitutive parts of the blood. They have repeatedly called it a fictional thing—bitter, sharp, and very hot—which in no way conforms in us to the qualities of <margin>6.</margin> serum or urine. But what is to be concluded from such fundamental confusion by the Schools in matters of such great importance?

->FLUID HUMOR<-

...I have measured at length and with professional expertise in the aforementioned book. For Paracelsus was the first to attack those theories, treating them as the culprits of a pillaged inheritance. But the Schools, though warned, refused to be wise, even though they were urged to realize they had applied the torch of human destruction to burn more readily. And first of all, I have sufficiently demonstrated that neither of the two biles <note>The "Schools" of traditional medicine believed in Yellow Bile and Black Bile.</note> nor phlegm exist in nature. Now, furthermore, I have resolved to show that it is not enough for the Schools to have been ignorant of the Latex and its particular purpose, but that they have also utterly erred in its constitution. They have wandered far from the established boundaries of the Latex, having been 
<margin>7.</margin> deceived by the likeness of milk. For whey is never separated from milk except after the corruption of its own milk; thus, they compare a "corpse" <note>He means a spoiled or dead fluid.</note> to the Latex. Finally, whey, which only arises and appears from the curdling of milk, was part of the native constitution of the milk; however, urine or sweat are not part of the matter of the blood. Therefore, they at least admit this: if that which floats in blood drawn from a vein is serum, and of the same species as the watery body of urine, then the serum already differs formally from bile. For what can be absent from a permanent thing is not part of its 
<margin>8.</margin> essential nature. Thus, they plainly imply a contradiction: that it is part of the internal constitution and essence of the blood, and yet also that it is not part of the intrinsic constitution of the blood. Therefore, without absurdity, the Latex floating in living blood cannot rightly be called the "serum of the blood," much less "gall-like bile" or its "fiery part." The Schools have therefore commanded that the part of the 
<margin>9.</margin> blood which they call serum, or urine, remained in the blood more due to the neglect of a separator than out of an inexcusable necessity of essence. Indeed, it is not rare to see blood drawn from a vein without serum. And therefore, they teach that serum is left in the blood only for the sake of an easier passage through the tiny fibers of the liver's veins, namely by giving the blood a more diluted consistency. And so they say: once these thin reeds have been passed, nature immediately planned the separation of the serum, and ordered it to be carried down into the final chamber of the urine <note>The bladder</note>. By leaving a remainder of it

<column-break/>

allied with the blood, it might also more easily penetrate through the thin tubes of the outermost small veins. By this doctrine, which is purely "excremental," they pollute the purity of digestions. They were ignorant of the principal purposes of the Latex and invented childish uses for the "whey" of the blood. I, however, through a reliable and indubitable path, have always confessed that the Parent of Nature <note>God or the creative force</note> cannot be frustrated in His conceived ends, nor has He permitted any urine to be left in the blood by an ordinary error of nature. Finally, whatever liquid is in the substance of the blood is not itself part of the constitution of the blood, nor is it its excrement; rather, it is the Latex, useful for its own ends. For the Latex is not a part of urine, just as it is not a part of sweat. For first, the salt of sweat is distinct in its properties from the salt of urine. And the Latex is still clearly devoid of salt. This is not surprising. Indeed, urine, insofar as it is imbued with the "stercoraceous ferment" <note>original: "fermento stercoreo" — a transformative power associated with waste or dung</note> of the kidneys, is also 
<margin>10.</margin> transmuted by it. For urine is made in its own workshops and is completed with its own formal properties, useful for its own functions and goals. Therefore, urine differs not only from sweat but also from itself, as long as it has not yet shared in the ferment of the kidneys and the liquid dung of the intestines. And this is surely no different than how the dung of the colon differs from the "cream" of the stomach <note>chyme or digested food</note>, or how chyle differs from blood. Therefore, a "part of urine" is not present in the blood, nor is a currently corrupted excrement (which would corrupt other things) committed to a food that has already been purified. For that error would be too daily and direct; to avoid this, nature has everywhere labored so diligently that it works harder at nothing than to proscribe troublesome waste as swiftly as possible. Since all and every excrement has already been alienated from its former self by the impression of the stercoraceous ferment, it could not help but further decay every good thing it was admitted to. Truly, the Latex 
<margin>11.</margin> wanders through the blood by permission, not indeed as a part of the blood, or as a residual waste of urine, but as something useful for various purposes. Therefore, I have called it the Latex, or a peculiar humor...

->NEGLECTED TOPICS<-

<margin>12.</margin> ...a substance distinct from the **thick blood** <note>original: *cruore*</note>. It is indeed almost tasteless in itself, and for its primary purpose, it tempers the acidity of the blood so as to keep it in check. This is most necessary after labor, heat, sweating, baths, and so on; for during such high levels of perspiration, the blood would become greatly thickened unless it had this watery part mixed in to provide for the sweat.
<margin>13.</margin> A second purpose of the **Latex** was this: since in all crude <term>Chyle</term> <note>The milky fluid produced by digestion in the stomach.</note>, cream, and blood there is some waste, and since the blood reserves an "excrementitious salt" while being digested (even as it is converted into pure nourishment), the Latex was a convenient companion to receive this salt and sweep it away.
<margin>14.</margin> A third purpose for the Latex was added: to act as the material cause that prevents any residue of a denser composition from remaining during the final evaporation of nourishment. Instead, it is expelled at the same time through <term>insensible perspiration</term> <note>original: *diapnæam*</note> by means of the **arterial ferment** (as mentioned above regarding the human <term>Blas</term> <note>Helmont’s term for the vital "spirit of motion" or "force" within the body.</note>), or it is washed out by means of sweat. For sweat is materially nothing other than the Latex to which superfluous salt has been added.
<margin>15.</margin> This is evident. For from a drink of water or thin beer, a copious sweat soon flows in summer. It is not, however, that a "false" watery latex of sweat is carried through the body as a vapor, picking up salt and something oily beneath the skin.
<margin>16.</margin> Rather, sweat is expelled in the form of water (as in health), or it is poured out spontaneously like water in those who are fearful, fainting, or dying. Here, I note in passing a seemingly irrelevant point:
<margin>17.</margin> That the sweat of the dying is not so much the Latex in its own nature as it is the **nutritional dew** <note>original: *ros alimentarius*</note> being broken down, which death commands. This is clear, for the body's condition immediately collapses, just as in a faint. Furthermore, that sweat possesses wonderful powers for killing hemorrhoids and growths. Moreover, it is clear that sweat is not carried by heat in the form of vapor.
<margin>18.</margin> For since vapor occupies a place a hundred times larger than water, the body would swell a hundred times more while sweating than its own extension otherwise allows. There is no empty space beneath the skin to receive vapor; likewise, a pot of boiling water has no vapor inside itself—it only exhales what it emits from the surface.

<column-break/>

Therefore, vapor does not wander beneath the skin; it is propelled only in the form of a liquid.
<margin>19.</margin> Sweat, then, is materially the Latex which, as it travels, scours or washes away filth from the **kitchens** <note>A metaphor for the metabolic or digestive sites within various organs.</note> of the parts. For this reason, it is usually smelly, and more so in the sick than the healthy. Thus, in a "Crisis," it often terminates diseases, insofar as it carries away filth according to its ordinary purpose. The **Schools** have admired the dissection of corpses, but they have not yet looked into the anatomy of sweat through its digestions, residues, selections, mixtures, resolutions, or expulsions.
<margin>20.</margin> The fifth purpose of the Latex was more intimate. Indeed, since the eye needs liquid so its eyelid may move without harm, and the tongue requires saliva to temper chewed food with moisture—and it would be absurd for all food to be moistened by the mass of the thick blood—therefore, the Latex is carried through the veins so that saliva, tears, etc., might be formed. For when more saliva than is proper flows during quinsy <note>A severe sore throat or tonsillitis.</note> or the infamous **salivation caused by Mercury**, the bowels themselves become drier.
<margin>21.</margin> Therefore, the Latex wanders harmlessly in the mass of blood, being carried to the appropriate places and promptly obeying the **distributive faculty**. If it should happen to seize the "salt of the brain" (as in a cold or catarrh), the Latex is not by its nature harmful, nor should it be blamed for what is unseasonably associated with it by accident. Likewise, although it may abound in diseases and inflate swollen legs <note>original: *œdematosa crura*</note>, that happens by chance. For nature, with a general effort, gives birth to a guest it hates and stuffs it with the waste it wishes to drive away. On a very cold night, I find a linen sheet in the morning stretched and frozen from the night's breath, of which at least four times more water has exhaled. Breath on summer days is no less watery, but much more vaporous. Therefore, several ounces of tasteless liquor are exhaled from the lung alone. But that water is not the waste of the lung, nor the matter of resolved blood. Therefore, it is sought from the Latex, whether it be sent by the distributive power of the <term>Archeus</term> <note>The internal "vital director" or "master chemist" that Helmont believed governed the body's functions.</note>, or whether the lung attracts it to itself. At the very least, it is continuously supplied, and the glands provide service elsewhere.

# ASTHMA

The lung's tissue <note>original: *parenchyma*</note> performs this same function. <margin>22.</margin> Therefore, the purpose of the **Latex** <note>Helmont's term for a clear, watery bodily fluid distinct from the four humors</note> is, as it were, a goal: that it might restrain the lungs with its moisture, lest they split open from the dryness of the inhaled air. It is also a misuse of teaching to claim that the Latex is "raw" and "undigested" at the start of a cold <note>original: *Corizzæ*</note>, and that over a number of days it is thickened by heat at the end of its "ripened" maturity. For once it is expelled, it does not wait to be "cooked," nor does it wait for its own coagulation to thicken. Nor could the Latex ever have waited for its own thickening within an empty skull at the start of a cold.

<margin>23.</margin> Therefore, ignorance of the Latex has stirred up many "dreams" or delusions in the treatment of <term>catarrhs</term> <note>excessive buildup of mucus</note> and <term>edemas</term> <note>swelling caused by fluid trapped in body tissues</note>. When legs are swollen late in the day, retaining a small pit from a finger’s pressure, and these swellings vanish by morning, the cause was thought to be <term>pituita</term> <note>phlegm, one of the four traditional humors</note>, which was supposedly turned into blood by nocturnal digestion. Thus, ignorance of this compliant Latex gave birth to the fables of what is called **rheumatism**.

<margin>24.</margin> But if they had ever sat down to do the math, they would have seen that late in the day, both legs were perhaps burdened by four pounds of weight from the swelling. If that had been (as they say) a "rawer blood" or "phlegmy" substance—since the legs are not the sewers for phlegm known by the Schools—there would be no reason why the phlegm should settle in the legs rather than any of the other three remaining humors, or why that phlegm should not fall into the belly, thighs, or loins instead. Surely, a just distribution would require perhaps 40 pounds daily to be consumed in the loss of "unripened" blood. Often basins and urinals are filled with saliva in a single night, and blankets and shirts drip with moisture; unless these are sought from the **Latex**, and not from the mass of living blood, everything believed about food, digestion, and blood-making collapses. Indeed, arithmetic itself and the weighing scales mock these "little doctors" <note>original: *medicastros*</note> in their fictions about phlegm. But what person with any sense <note>original: *nasutus*</note> would ever believe that saliva, tears, sweat, and copious urine are drawn from the heritage of the blood itself without instant harm to life? Especially since the same thing persists even in chronic cases! Let us imagine a small

<column-break/>

dinner, where the stomach and the <term>pylorus</term> <note>the opening from the stomach into the small intestine</note> have performed their duty well, <margin>25.</margin> yet there is copious salivation in a case of fierce quinsy <note>original: *anguina*; an inflammation of the throat</note> and exquisite inflammations of the tonsils. Certainly, that thicker and continuous mucus does not flow down from the brain (the passage of the throat being already obstructed), and much less does it ascend from an empty stomach while the throat is blocked. Therefore, let the ordinary duty of the tongue and throat be the production of saliva, the matter of which is sought from the **Latex**; this Latex changes into various "masks" according to the variety of its **ferment**. For there are watery, slimy, salty, acidic, bitter, and tenacious salivas, like a thread.

<margin>26.</margin> Therefore, a daily abundance of Latex in the veins was necessary, along with its prompt obedience to the calling of the <term>Archeus</term> <note>the internal "master workman" or vital force governing the body's functions</note>. For even if the Latex is unfit for nourishment, it is still suited for its own uses. Indeed, food could be reduced to juice (as mice and grasshoppers show) without drinking, had there not been a need for the Latex for greater services.

<margin>27.</margin> Thirst is therefore the herald of a deficiency in the **Latex**, not a lack of the "constitution" or balance <note>original: *crasis*</note> of the blood (as the Schools otherwise command). The thirst of those with fevers, which persists even after drinking, announces that the Latex has been made unfit for its duties by a foreign contagion.

<margin>28.</margin> Indeed, whenever bitterness, saltiness, or a foul smell infects the saliva, the stomach is weary with <term>apepsia</term> <note>indigestion or failure of the digestive power</note>, and the tongue (otherwise painless and having no evil in itself) is split by dryness. This signifies that the Latex does not pass to the veins equipped with its proper "provisions" because it became unfit for its duty in the "inn" of the stomach or its vicinity. Therefore, the dryness of the tongue and its encrusted filth in fevers is not an effect or sign of "exhalations" carried upward from the stomach (even when it is not digesting drink), but is a defect of the Latex, either defiled or impoverished by scarcity.

<margin>29.</margin> It is not enough to have spoken of the Latex and some of its uses and duties through the necessity of its distribution. It is also helpful to uncover its paths and to have recounted its "exorbitations" <note>deviations or errors from its natural course</note>. For the law and necessity of its uses have introduced just as many "sins" or malfunctions—if not two for each side. Since the Latex is not of the substance...

is not the essence of the blood; but a foolish, harmless liquid, a companion running along the same paths. For that reason, it is carried through the veins together with the blood. with **scabies** <note>mange or the "itch"</note> without any defect of the liver whatsoever. Two things, therefore, are chiefly to be looked at here: that the Latex is not moved so much by its own accord as it is called by the surface, which it is otherwise destined to help; and also that the sweats of those parts testify to a defect in the same. <margin>37.</margin> Therefore, blankets thrown over someone promote sweat, because the external...

But truly, a manifest error is present in this stated use. For the significant glands behind the ears would be in vain, where there is no fear of tearing, just as there is none internally: furthermore, the fleshy membrane itself is not stretched, and thus the glands could not have been placed there except in vain, with a vanishing use and purpose. That is, either the Arbiter of Nature erred in the use of the glands, or the Schools err. Since in no place previously mentioned where the glands are located can the vessels move away from each other. A thin ligament would have preserved a vessel from rupture better and more conveniently than a fragile and tender gland. I everywhere notice the perpetual neglect of the Schools in <margin>41.</margin> investigating the truth. For they do not notice that the aforementioned glands are nothing

This is visibly <margin>42.</margin> manifest in the tongue, where the glands produce saliva and therefore draw the Latex to themselves. Under the armpits and in the groin, however, they bring forth sweats. They do not, however, provide against the tearing of vessels. For the former is a daily duty; the latter, truly, is nothing but unusual, rare, and rather ridiculous. For stagnant Latex burdens the veins by oppression, and if they are freed from the same, the **Archeus** <note>the internal "chief" or vital spirit that directs the body's functions</note>, as if taking a breath, resumes new strengths for himself unexpectedly. Therefore, ignorance of the Latex invented and sustained the use of **cauteries**; it feigned the existence of **Catarrhs**, and caused men to dream up unharmonious remedies or universal protections. For nothing solid has been considered against diseases. As I shall show in its proper place, the beginnings of diseases <margin>43.</margin> remain hidden and unknown even today: and therefore remedies are but vain attempts, containing nothing certain unless they are endowed with a **specific property** for certain diseases. Otherwise, a conjectural uncertainty will prepare retreats for itself, and the credulity of the sick has fortified those who practice medicine. Because a given remedy, even if it were said to be appropriated to a disease, does not help everyone. Indeed, not even **purgatives**, although they undoubtedly loosen the bowels, comfort the sick on account of the diversity of **complexions** <note>the traditional balance of the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile)</note> and stubborn, fictitious humors. For they suppose that such a person, for instance, sins by way of the humors, and they look afterward at what is drawn out through the purgative: yet they see that nothing of the disease's ferocity has been diminished. Therefore, when they ought to acknowledge their ignorance founded upon the humors and purgatives, they turn themselves back to the variety of complexions and the uncertain and unknown differences of "imbalances." Which surely, if they are viewed with a fair mind, will end in no other way than in the full knowledge of the ignorance and overthrow of the principles of healing used until now. For which reason, I exhort and humbly <margin>44.</margin> pray those who practice medicine that they might timely learn the unheard-of beginnings, themes, and unusual axioms of Medicine.

<margin>45.</margin>
For this reason, I thought it opportune to wander a little from the path in this place. Indeed, just as I have seen **Atrophy** <note>a wasting away of the body</note> occasionally sustained by the **Latex** <note>the clear, watery fluid Van Helmont identifies as distinct from blood and humors</note>, so also fatness, or obesity, was driven away in my sight in a single two-month period by a **diuretic drink** <note>a substance that promotes urination</note> used in place of beer. However, foreign drugs such as **Cinchona** <note>original: *chinę*; the bark used to treat malaria</note>, **Sarsaparilla** <note>original: *zarzę*</note>, **Guaiacum** <note>original: *Guajaci*; a South American "holy wood" used to treat syphilis</note>, and others, because they pour out the Latex through sweats, have acquired the name of "drying agents" under a false and deceptive title. Truly, I have already demonstrated that every visible body, and everything believed to be forged from a mixture of elements, is made materially from the single element of water. This water, in all established things, primarily conducts itself in the manner of the **Latex**, and it is enough to have assumed that here, as it has been sufficiently proven once before. Furthermore, there is an axiom of Philosophy: *That bodies are not changed into one another unless they are first reduced into their first and following matter.* For however much they wish this to be applied to metallic transmutations <note>the alchemical changing of lead to gold</note>, it is nevertheless taken from the observed transmutations of all sublunary things. However, they do not mean that bodies must be reduced into the "first matter" of **Aristotle** <note>the abstract "prime matter" of ancient philosophy</note>, nor even into the first separation of elements (for they do not think food must return to its basic elements so that blood may be made from it). Rather, they mean that a body to be changed must recede into its **proximate matter** <note>the substance most closely preceding its current form</note>, or the subject of its prior life, before it can fix any hope on the goal of acquiring a new transformation. To what end, let it be certain: Food and drink in the stomach take on the nature of **Chyle** <note>milky fluid of digested food</note> while retaining the qualities of the "middle life" of those foods. The former matter of the foods is indeed destroyed and brought closer to the matter of the Latex, or closer to the element of water. This is accomplished, of course, by the **specific ferment** <note>a vital, enzyme-like force</note> of the stomach, just as the ferment of the liver transforms chyle into **blood** <note>original: *cruorem*; specifically the thick or clotted part of the blood</note>, of which the Latex is a companion and associate, but not a part. Moreover, the gifts of the ferments in nature exist as something so distinct and singular.

<column-break/>

So much so, that certain living things make for themselves blood, flesh, etc., and even oily **fat** <note>original: *axungiam*; specifically animal fat or grease</note> from water alone. For in the stomach of the **Salmon**, fishermen say that food is never found. Furthermore, there are tiny aquatic creatures in salty waters, in which almost nothing is born, which communicate a certain "seed" to the water they drink, from which they increase and sustain their little bodies. Thus, when other fish eat these types of animalcules, the "seed" engendered in the waters is given over, passing into life and led toward a shared "middle life." Moreover, animalcules that immediately create blood and their entire physical equipment for themselves from water alone have an example in almost every **vegetable**. This is especially seen on rocky and sandy mountains, far removed from the manuring of men. On these mountains, perhaps sixty species of resin-bearing trees are noted; they are nourished and grow to a great height from only rainwater and snow, or from the **leffas** <note>a Helmontian term for the vital essence or "stethos" of minerals/rocks</note> of a stony odor. These trees become so fat with resin that they would be suffocated unless they poured it out all around them. The ferment of the stomach in man transforms food into chyle more easily than it transforms the fats of those foods, because **fat**
<margin>46.</margin>
is further removed from the Latex, or the "first matter," than the food itself is. This digestion of transmutation into watery juices is brought up here to make it clear that the Latex—once a foreign "seed" and the ferment of the limbs is easily conceived within us—is transformed into an "alien offspring." And so, from the Latex, it is most closely transplanted into **excrementitious mucus**, as I have already shown above, where I recalled that after taking a deep drink in the summer, **sputum** <note>phlegm or spit</note> (which was absent during dry thirst) is created as something mucilaginous immediately afterward. This is the new history of the Latex, to be referred to the treatise on **Catarrhs** <note>discharges of mucus</note>, because ignorance of it has given a singular confirmation to "conceived catarrhs," just as it has given recklessness to those who are about to conceive them.

<margin>1.</margin> For this reason, I have decided to declare the goals and effects of the cautery. First, then, cauteries are made by fire, by a glowing iron, by corrosive caustics, or even by the razor or forceps themselves, by cutting something away. It is enough: so long as the fleshy membrane is pierced by a wound. Others, however, prefer a wound prepared by fire or caustic over one opened by cutting. This is because they think that by actual heat and dryness, the flow

<margin>2.</margin> of humors is better prevented. As if, in a single moment, fire would burn anything beyond the scab <note>original: *eschara*; the crust of dead tissue formed by a burn</note> itself, or dry out anything else that they later imagine will flow toward the wound. <margin>3.</margin> Schools, they are making much of dreams. Indeed, the "little fountain" <note>original: *fontanella*; the common name for an induced draining sore</note> (for so they call the cauterized wound, so that the common people might believe diseases are

drained out as if through a fountain) helps nothing until the scab has been removed, and the trace of heat and dryness has first been taken away. This is because the establishment of a Cautery has as its object excretion <note>the discharge of waste</note>, which does not begin before the falling off of the scab; and less can ever evaporate through a scab than through otherwise healthy skin. Therefore, later doctors have judged it does not matter how the little fountain was made, so long as they have divided the continuity <note>broken the skin</note> and kept it divided. For what

<margin>4.</margin> God made whole so that it might be best, it seems better to the Schools if it is kept wounded. That is, they summon the catarrhs to appear personally at a place, according to the healer's whim. Quite charming, indeed, if it were equally true. Yet these wonders have progressed so far that cauteries are now made even for children before they are three years old <note>original: *trimatum*</note>. # THE CAUTERY #

...even assuming the downflow and prostration of humors, which they command, is by far the most absurd. For my foundation, however, let it suffice that there is no mission, or spontaneous downflow, of **Catarrh** <note>catarrh: the traditional medical belief that harmful fluids "flow down" from the brain to the rest of the body</note>. Since this negative reality stands, the foundation of **Cauteries** <note>cautery: here referring to an "issue" or "fontanelle," a small wound kept open intentionally by a physician to drain fluids</note> becomes vain. For the **Schools** <note>The Schools: the traditional medical universities following Galen and Arabic authorities</note> teach that through these **fontanelles** <note>literally "little fountains"</note>, evil, even deadly humors are drawn out, which would otherwise either be sent elsewhere or flow down of their own accord. 

<margin>7.</margin> How delightful indeed, that nature, with a loose rein, should await the judgment of the Healer and the opening of the Skin, so that it may deposit the burden there, which it would otherwise divert into a more noble member. As if nature, in the act of sending, were threatening: "Unless you maintain a wound open for me in the fleshy membrane where it seems best to you, so that you might appease my fury through **revulsion** <note>revulsion: the medical theory of drawing a disease from one part of the body to another</note> and turn me away from the intent of dismissing these fluids, woe to you! For what I would otherwise purge beneath the skin, I shall pull back toward a noble organ in vengeance." 

But tell me, please: from what center, or from what bubbling spring of a fountain, is that evil humor prepared? Is it in the liver, the workshop of the four humors (as they claim)? 

<margin>8.</margin> But truly, it is a difficult, long, and rugged path for that evil humor to be carried from the liver through the *vena cava* <note>the main vein carrying blood to the heart</note>, and thus through the heart, to the furthest skin of the arm, leg, or neck, without contaminating the **blood** <note>original: "cruorem"</note>—yet remaining itself a pure, evil humor. It is a cruel **emunctory** <term>emunctory: an organ or canal that carries off waste</term> indeed, which leads evil humor across the very fountain of life <note>the heart</note>. And thus the Physician is cruel, and the Schools more cruel still, who command that noxious humor be carried through the Heart. 

But if that evil humor, still unknown today, has its source in the Brain: where, I ask? Is that evil humor born in every sink-hole of the head? In its borders? Or in the basin? Certainly, a daily collection and nest of that malignant humor could not occur in the ventricles of the brain without an immediate fear of death. But if the evil is made in the basin—having previously been good—it would then flow down of its own accord through the nostrils and the palate, as is usual, and would not need a Cautery. Or who is that Corrupter who, in some part of the head,

<column-break/>

purposely vitiates a humor that was previously good, so that it might then carry the malignancy to some part beneath the skin which the Physician has ordered to be struck? How obedient indeed is that evil humor (which is surely now a dead excrement) that it would allow itself to be twisted and sent elsewhere—one which otherwise, no longer concerned with the economy of life, obeys only the law of its own weight and position! 

Moreover, as for the claim that the evil humor to be drained by the cautery is a vapor transferred from the stomach into the head, through the brain, the **meninges** <note>the membranes covering the brain</note>, and the skull, and there collected and dismissed between the external muscles and the skin: that theory was previously and peremptorily exploded in the section on Catarrhs. Finally, even if these things were granted, it would lack the essence and the very etymology of a "humor," and consequently of an "evil humor"—namely **phlegm** <note>original: "pituitæ"</note>, one of the four. For whatever has once been raised from the stomach as a vapor and has thickened into drops is neither thick nor tenacious, nor is it any longer one of the four humors made in the liver; rather, it would be a posthumous, distilled liquor. 

Therefore, if the evil humor—the final cause for the cautery—is not generated in the liver, the brain, or the stomach, what then shall be the workshop of evil humors for catarrhs? Or what part is the "sender" and the "high place" from which they might be carried downward to the Cautery? 

<margin>9.</margin> Indeed, in such a narrow strait of trifles, the Schools are forced to confess that no evil humor is actually sent to the hole of the cautery; rather, the blood degenerates in the wound itself and in its ill-disposed edges. 

<margin>10.</margin> For this is natural to all wounds that lack **balsam** <note>balsam: the body’s natural healing fluid, according to Van Helmont</note>. Truly, if the Schools were to examine the **Aphorism** <note>referring to Hippocrates' Aphorisms</note>: *While pus is being made, there is greater pain, labor, and fever, than when the pus is already formed,* they would recognize that **pus** is produced materially from the blood through the labor of the [body's] faculties, and consequently, in a fontanelle, pus is desired for those same ends. 

This being the case, the thesis falls which supposes that evil humors are drawn out through cauteries. 
2. The drawing out of pus made in a wound is not from the center of the body. 
3. It is not the excrement of a flowing catarrh. 
4. Cauteries do not purge evil humors, but rather...

# THE CAUTERY #

...prepare the blood into excrement, with great effort by the digestive faculty. 5. Cauteries do nothing to prevent a malignant humor that forms locally within the very lips of the wound. 6. Pus and **sanies** <note>sanies: a thin, greenish or bloody discharge from a wound</note> cannot move backward through the opening of the ulcer and slip into a **noble part** <note>noble part: a vital internal organ like the heart or liver</note>, and much less can the good blood from which pus is made. 7. If the blood were already a "bad humor" before it reached the **fontanelle** <note>fontanelle: a small, intentionally created wound kept open to drain fluids; also called an "issue"</note>, then nature would be aiming a bad part of the blood mass specifically at the wounded part just to nourish it—or this would be its ordinary habit in every individual part. In that case, all of nature would be laboring under the vice of foolishness. 8. It is a stupid thing to say: "Because it has produced much pus, the Cautery has purged well." For that pus actually represents the corruption of good blood. Indeed, while a man is quite ill, the fontanelle "weeps" **ichor** <note>ichor: a watery, thin discharge, often seen as a sign of poor healing compared to "laudable" thick white pus</note> instead of pus. 9. If the Cautery truly worked to evacuate evil humors, a person ought to feel better while the ichor flows than when pus is formed. But in theory <note>original: "in thesi"</note> this is false. From this, it is correctly inferred that it is not some "selected" bad humor or a dangerous waste product (which would otherwise fall elsewhere) that is evacuated through the fontanelle. Rather, all of this—whether it be pus or a thin virus—is nothing other than pure blood intended for the nourishment of the cauterized part, which is corrupted there by the defect of the wound. Therefore, the corruption of the blood itself measures the quality or the malignancy of the **digestion** <note>digestion: in this context, the physiological process by which a specific body part transforms nutrients into its own substance</note> at the site of the fontanelle. And consequently, while the **total Archeus** <note>Archeus: the "internal chemist" or vital spirit that Van Helmont believed directed all life processes and healing</note> is struggling in any way, there is also a greater failure of digestion in the fontanelle, and the pus is closer to putrefaction. Up to this point, the fontanelle "weeps" ichor because of a more powerful than usual disturbance of digestion. The desire of the **Schools** <note>The Schools: the traditional medical universities following the ancient teachings of Galen</note> is therefore that a great deal of white pus be made from innocent blood.

<margin>11.</margin> And they call this "having purged well," if a great deal of blood is corrupted in the **final digestion** <note>final digestion: the last stage of nutrition where blood is turned into solid tissue</note>. If this is considered correctly, it will now become clear that a Cautery is not applied to purge a malignant humor, nor does such a bad humor even exist; rather, it is used only to

<column-break/>

diminish an abundance of blood. Thus, it is done solely in view of **Plethora** <note>Plethora: a medical condition characterized by an excess of blood in the circulatory system</note>. From which it <margin>12</margin> follows that it is not suitable for adolescents, nor for those who are emaciated, nor for those depressed by some disease—nor indeed for those living orderly lives, and least of all for abstemious religious practitioners. But they have not yet distinguished <margin>13</margin> whether the pus in a fontanelle comes from blood alone (one of the four "fictional" humors), or truly from a mixture of all four. If the first is true, then pus would not come from a "bad humor," but from the best of the four humors; therefore, the fontanelle would be useless, and the "best" pus (the intended effect of the fontanelle) would be the worst thing possible, since it would be nothing but the corruption of the best blood. If they prefer to invent a story—namely, that the blood is not bad beforehand, but becomes bad when it is separated from its three companions—at the very least, the three remaining humors in that secretion would be even worse than the blood. In any event, the fontanelle would be created only for a bad end: to corrupt good and innocent blood. But if they want the pus to be made from a mixture of all four humors, then the Cautery fails in its goal. For the Cautery would be effective not <margin>14</margin> for purging harmful humors, but for corrupting the good ones sent daily by a non-erring nature for nourishment. Finally, the Cautery cannot be considered an established precaution against **Catarrh** <note>Catarrh: the supposed "down-flow" of waste fluids from the brain</note>; otherwise, the matter of Catarrh would not be a vapor, nor even phlegm, but the blood itself, which the fontanelle corrupts within itself. For pus is not made from phlegm, but from blood alone, as is sufficiently taught in the Schools. Therefore, once the essence of pus is well-investigated in its matter and its cause, the purposes of Cauteries—the purging of catarrhs and bad humors—cease to exist. Indeed, once any symptom of the wound is removed in Cauteries and health is assumed, it is necessary that the **breach of continuity** <note>breach of continuity: a classic medical term for a wound or physical break in the body's tissues</note> in the fontanelle produces pus, and that this does not flow down from elsewhere, but is generated in the part itself. The **Archeus**, too, proportionally dispenses as much blood to the parts daily as they have need of for their nourishment.

# THE CAUTERY #

<margin>15.</margin>
Therefore, pus is simply blood that has been spoiled in the area where the wound is located; it is the result of a corrupted digestion in that specific place. To have damaged the integrity, continuity, and digestion of the body's parts, and finally to have converted the blood into pus—this is exactly what is regarded in the **Schools** <note>original: "Scholis"; the academic medical establishment of the time</note> as having countered **Catarrhs** <note>original: "Catarrhis"; from the Greek "to flow down," a medical theory that many illnesses were caused by mucus flowing from the brain to other organs</note>. They claim they have extracted an excrement-like humor through the opening of the cautery—humor which was otherwise threatening to settle in a **noble part** <note>a vital organ like the heart or liver</note>—either from the head (where they believe all catarrhs originally seek their source) or elsewhere. They maintain this whether or not there is a "consensus" <note>a sympathetic connection</note> between the head and the wounded part; it is all the same to them, provided the wounded skin is kept open. Whether that excrement-like humor is blood, or becomes pus, or is **sanies** <note>a thin, foul-smelling discharge</note>, it is all the same, so long as the world is deceived by the well-worn vocabulary of Catarrh, precaution, derivation, revulsion, and the **fontanelle** <note>original: "fontanellæ"; an "issue" or artificial wound kept open to drain fluids</note>. 

For I observe a year-old infant, currently teething, suffering from fever, foaming at the mouth, and constant saliva. And finally, there are griping pains and stools that are greenish-yellow. Surely that tooth is a part of the head; therefore, the diarrhea must be a "catarrh of the head" <note>Van Helmont is being sarcastic here to show the absurdity of the "Schools" logic</note>. But what is the "consensus" of a tooth about to erupt, or of a swollen gum, with the intestine? What power does the tooth have to create and send a catarrh from the infant’s stomach to the head, and from there into the **ileum** <note>original: "Ileon"; the final section of the small intestine</note>? By what law does a vapor distilled from the stomach become "aeruginous" <note>rust-colored or copper-green</note> bile in the head? Has the workshop of the bile perhaps migrated to the head from the very beginning of life? Could a cautery (if an infant could tolerate it) drive away that leek-green diarrhea into itself? Could a few drops of pus compensate for several pounds of leek-green bile? Why does the infant's stomach manufacture a catarrh because of a toothache? Why is it sent to the intestine and not to the aching tooth? Does the reader not yet see that diarrhea is not a catarrh? Rather, it is the **Archeus** <note>original: "Archeum"; Van Helmont's term for the internal "master builder" or vital spirit that governs the body’s chemistry</note>, indignant and provoked anywhere in the body, which is ready in the intestine to transform the nutritional "cream" into excrement—which the Schools then think is bile, phlegm, and so on. If, therefore, diarrhea is not a catarrh, and if the indignant **Archeus**—

<column-break/>

—is able to transform anything into a hostile liquid if only the gum is afflicted, can it not then discharge itself in any direction through the established **emunctories** <note>natural disposal organs/routes like sweat or urine</note>? Does it really need to wait for a piece of skin to be opened by a caustic? Ah, what cruel dullness has made the Schools so ferocious against their own fellow mortals?

<margin>16.</margin>
For they do not even consider that in women and the obese, there is a fleshy membrane around the ordinary locations for a cautery—mere **axungia** <note>soft body fat or lard</note> to a thickness of at least two fingers—yet these are the very persons for whom cauteries are more frequently and "profitably" urged. Consequently, the bottom of the fontanelle will barely reach the middle of that fat. 

<margin>17.</margin>
There is, therefore, no path by which the evil, fictional humor of the outlawed **Catarrh** can rush from the brain, or between the skull and the skin, through the middle of that fat. For what, in the end, is that "solitary humor," which, having been outlawed by its own sin from the part that sent it, descends unmixed through the substance of the fat and degenerates into pus? If it is an exhalation of vapors from the stomach, why is it not more frequent in younger people and those with "hot" stomachs, rather than in the weak, the old, and the "cold"? In what way does that water, distilled from vapor, take on the form of pus? How will it hurry through the brain, the **meninges** <note>original: "menynges"; the membranes covering the brain</note>, and the skull to find the hole made by the cautery, so that it might flow out and be purged there alone? Why does the vapor not fly out into the air a hundred times over before it reaches the place so conveniently designated for the cautery? How can water rising from the stomach already be blood and the mother of pus? How can blood (which is the material of pus, according to **Galen** <note>the famous 2nd-century Roman physician whose theories Van Helmont is attacking</note>) be the material of "Catarrh"? Why should blood be reduced to the rank of "bad humors" when it is not yet contaminated and is being dispensed by nature to the wounded site? Why, once a wound is made, would nature stop casting down the condemned matter through and into its accustomed places? If the skin is opened at the doctor's whim, will nature suddenly lose its way? Or did it perhaps struggle so much just to find an exit somewhere, and now that the hole is made, will it henceforth become the servant of the one who wounded it? Therefore, these four things are false: namely,

# THE CAUTERY #

namely, that pus is the matter of **Catarrh** <note>original: "Catarrhi"; the old medical theory that illness was caused by "flows" of cold mucus from the brain</note>; that Catarrh is materially made from the vapor of the stomach; that catarrhal matter is excreted through the **fontanelle** <note>original: "fontanellam"; an "issue" or artificial ulcer kept open to drain fluids</note>; and that this matter would be diverted into a **noble part** <note>a vital organ like the heart or liver</note> unless it is drawn elsewhere through the opening. The **Schools** <note>the traditional academic medical establishment</note> have at least one refuge for their 
<margin>18.</margin> boldness. Namely, that Cauteries, in chronic diseases, as well as in the more corpulent and **plethoric** <note>original: "plethoricis"; those with an excess of blood</note>, have not infrequently been beneficial. Therefore, they say, it is necessary that at least the 
<margin>19.</margin> bad humor is purged once the wound is made, and the body is unburdened. To which subterfuge, I say: the matter of Catarrh, its essence, its manner, the paths of its derivation, and its effect—likewise the "bad humor" and the goals of the Cautery—are all fictitious dreams, veils for shameful laziness and ignorance. Moreover, examples of successful 
<margin>20.</margin> outcomes are not enough to destroy the fine points of truth. What if Cauteries have helped sometimes? That would at least not be from the root and essence of Catarrh, which in itself is nothing at all. Therefore, if they have been beneficial, let the Schools admit that Cauteries help through means and ends unknown to them: and that they extol with such great praise a conjectural remedy, which is uncertain and works only by accident. For they have rightly wondered that Cauteries were beneficial by the outcome; for if some ailment was going to perish and cease on its own, or shortly by the maturity of days, do they therefore think a right is born for them to miserably torture two hundred people in vain, just because for one person, by accident, the 
<margin>21.</margin> cautery was not unlucky? What if, on the contrary, the histories of many were compared for whom cauteries turned out badly? Immediately they say, "We are not moved by the smoke of **empirics** <note>original: "empyrici"; healers who relied on experience rather than the 'rational' theory of the Schools</note>, nor by examples." For the Schools claim to be rational, and they lean furthermore on the authorities of the Ancients. And they thunder this so loudly whenever they are destitute of reasons and convicted by experiences; they cease to be most expert masters, nor do they wish to be swayed by experiences contrary to their own. They flee to the reasons of those who came before, which I have shown to be pale, lazy, false, and stumbling at the very first entrance. 
<margin>22.</margin> Indeed, when the Schools had discovered that some, by a stroke of luck, felt relief after a cautery, soon a **seton** <note>original: "seton"; a cord or thread passed through a fold of skin to keep a wound open</note>—or a cord drawn through the skin of the neck on both sides—is believed to be

a remedy for **Ophthalmia** <note>eye inflammation</note>, bleary eyes, and even for cataracts themselves, and for the ruined digestion of the eyes. A cautery on the opposite leg was believed to be a 
<margin>23.</margin> cure for **Sciatica** <note>original: "Ischiadico"; nerve pain in the leg</note>. They tried various Cauteries, and the blacksmiths made a long inventory of tools; they even instituted "Arabic burnings" (using nothing but goat dung, fried in a pan) on the big toe from a distance, for those with sciatica and **arthritis** <note>original: "arthriticis"</note>. They have everywhere sold stage-actor-like trifles and dreams as the truth in their healing. But the Schools finally wondered why **Arthritis** alone, though assigned to Catarrhs, laughed at all their theorems and Cauteries. 
<margin>24.</margin> That is to say, it showed as false the idea that **Gout** <note>original: "Podagra"</note> happened because of a flowing Catarrh, and that the Cautery was a useless invention for the "derivation" and "revulsion" of a settling humor. 
<margin>25.</margin> I also wonder at the "delirious" Cauteries used in **tabes** <note>wasting disease or consumption</note>, defects of the lungs, the head, the eyes, and the kidneys—namely, for those empty "catarrhal" defects. They promise that the "epileptic fumes" will exit from the brain that way—not so that they might at least lessen the duration of a seizure, but so that they might often suspend them for the future. But the sick endure these things in a "deaf hope" of health, yet without precedent. Nor do they ever weigh the fact that these dreamed-up vapors do not affect the brain for lack of an exit; but on the contrary, the storms of the disease stir up the cause before they can even reach the skin of the scalp. Therefore, the work and help of the Cautery is pale and vain, as it begins from the "rear end" of things in healing diseases. 
<margin>27.</margin> For it has not yet been determined by the Schools which ailments Cauteries are suitable for, because they help only rarely and by accident. # THE DISEASE OF THOSE WHO LIVE PLEASANTLY
<note>original: "VOLUPE VIVENTIUM MORBUS"; a reference to gout's reputation as a disease of luxury and "high living."</note>

<margin>1.</margin>
Arthritis—the joint disease understood by the name of **Gout** <note>original: "Podagræ"; literally "foot-trap"</note>—is attributed to **Catarrhs** <note>waste fluids or "dripping" humors</note> because many European nations call it "The Drop" <note>original: "Gutta"</note> by way of **antonomasia** <note>a figure of speech where a descriptive phrase replaces a proper name</note>. Patients agree with this etymology, lending their support to such great human blindness. This is because they seem to feel a certain "dropping" or sliding between the connections of their bones. For the **Schools** <note>the traditional academic medical establishment based on Galenic theory</note>, which presume to teach the whole world, delight in learning from the indistinct senses of the common people. Moving along without any real investigation, they themselves have become "catarrhal" in their thinking. But since I have already overturned the entire fable of the **Catarrh**, I shall also expose the error of common perception regarding Gout. I judged that this could not be done otherwise than by explaining the scene of Gout from its very "egg" <note>from its very beginning</note>.

<margin>2.</margin>
Gout remained unknown in the first ages of the world, even though the human race fell into every kind of luxury from its very cradle. But as hardship gradually grew into human weakness, it was at least so rare among the first writers that it was hardly considered worthy of their pens. However, as the decay of mortals increased further, it first attacked those most dissolved in luxury. For this reason, it was believed to be the plague of those enslaved to **Venus and Bacchus** <note>the gods of sex and wine/alcohol</note>, a belief that persists to our day. Nevertheless, since it now frequently infests laborers and even the most abstinent **Capuchins** <note>an order of friars known for their strict poverty and fasting</note>, I have made a prophecy: Gout will soon flourish everywhere as a popular plague, unless God, pitying us, prevents this disaster which is partly hereditary and partly acquired.

<margin>3.</margin>
Finally, from this I have also predicted that Gout will be the sign that distinguishes between the "chosen" doctors and the "imaginary" ones <note>original: "medicastros"; medicasters or quacks</note>, just as **Quartan fever** <note>a type of malaria</note> does. For once it has taken root, it not only remains as a companion for life, but is sometimes transferred inexorably to distant descendants. Indeed, it will so multiply its fertility for the future that it will serve to set apart the medicasters who deserve to be scorned. For there are many things that this "Prince of Diseases" keeps unique to itself.

<margin>4.</margin>
For besides its stubbornness, it not only succeeds through the parents' lineage into several 

<column-break/>

generations, but furthermore, it waits patiently for thirty years or more before it comes forward. Indeed, a father <note>original: "Generans"; the one begetting</note> who is not yet gouty often establishes an heir to his Gout in almost the same year that he himself—after the act of generation—is about to suffer the first beginnings of the disease. Therefore, silent in the parent, the plague not yet born begets its kind before the proper maturity of its seed, a thing denied to other seeds in nature. It is as if the ruined field of human nature now grows Gout of its own accord. I pass over the fact that it produces "stones," "chalk," or "lime" <note>referring to the stony deposits, or tophi, found in gouty joints</note>, which have origins different from **Duelech** <term>Duelech: Van Helmont's specific term for the "spirit" or stony matter that forms kidney and bladder stones</term>. This stony monster, appearing outside its usual and proper place, deforms a man into a monster, mutilated in his limbs and a mere trunk, from such a proud structure.

<margin>5.</margin>
The **Schools** indeed grant, beyond controversy, that Gout comes from "defluxions" <note>fluids flowing downward</note>; but they have not yet defined whether that Catarrh is raised from the stomach like others, or whether this irregular Catarrh is led from the liver through the narrow and highly obstructed vessels of the veins. They do not claim it travels the straight path where the mouths of the veins end, but by unusual ways known only to nature, coming to rest between the joints and ligaments. I, however, being little concerned with fables, let both opinions fight it out. It is shameful, meanwhile, that the causes of diseases have been discussed only as "problems" and left as debatable. Meanwhile, I know for certain that Gout—whether it glides into heirs through the parents' seeds, or is finally contracted by one's own errors in living—is of one and the same species with all the properties that accompany it. It matters nothing whether it attacks with "heat" and hurts immensely, or is judged to be slower and milder with "cold."

<margin>6.</margin>
For those are merely the "banners" of the degrees with which the matter is marked; they do not, however, vary its essence.

<margin>7.</margin>
I know then, and have learned above all: that at least hereditary Gout is not derived from a Catarrh, if it has lain hidden and imperceptible in the seed, and in the constitution of that seed, for thirty years. For truly, since it is in the seed,

->### THOUGHT OF OLD.<-

In the **seed** <note>original: "semine"; referring to the hereditary material of both parents</note>, nothing external can be contained without that very thing destroying the fertility of reproduction. Let it be certain: nothing of a **catarrhal** nature <note>referring to the waste fluids of traditional Galenic theory</note> remains in the seed, and there is no place there for any hostile matter. It is therefore established that in the seed, nothing remains except the **character** or **seal** <note>original: "characterem sigillumve"; a formative blueprint or spiritual imprint</note> of things to be done in a set order. Indeed, that seal is not so disruptive that it shakes the fertility from the seed, even if a hereditary disease is destined to rise again from it in a son or grandson. Finally, that seal cannot defile the fetus with a monstrous deformity in the seed, even though other characters of the seeds, according to their nature, might shape the seed. Therefore, even if the **seal of Gout** <note>original: "Podagræ sigillum"</note> is truly present in the seed, it nonetheless sleeps, remains silent, and hides during the course of the body's formation, until at last it unfolds itself when the opportunity of created matter and maturity arises.

<margin>8.</margin>
The character of Gout is therefore in the seed like a "first life" with a command of silence, so that it sleeps until the first **paroxysm** <note>a sudden attack or fit of the disease</note>, just as a swallow sleeps through the whole winter. ->## THE DISEASE OF THE PLEASURE-SEEKERS<-

[This] will be agreed upon by those who are free, and not yet contaminated by any prejudice.

<margin>14.</margin> First of all, once the **gouty character** <note>original: "character podagricus"; the hereditary blueprint or spiritual imprint of the disease</note> of the family has been established—whether it has grown from the seed of the parents or was acquired through an immoderate way of life—it is necessary, according to the law of fate and the cycle of things, that it has prescribed limits for its duration, both in its emergence and its continuation. Therefore, as the beginning of this gouty movement draws near, the **vital spirit** <note>the internal life-force that governs the body's functions</note>, acting as a servant obeying the corruptive character, immediately puts on a **fermentative acidity** <note>original: "aciditatem fermentalem"; an acidic state triggered by a biological "ferment" or catalyst</note>, which is entirely hostile to itself and foreign to us. Finally, since all acidity, whether in the blood or the flesh, has been shown to contain the beginning and evidence of putrefaction: it follows that nature, sensing that acidity in the spirit (which it conceived from the seed or the gouty character), immediately stirs up a **short-lived fever** <note>original: "febrim ephimeram"</note> before the onset of the Gout itself. Soon, in that specific place, or "womb" (namely, where two bones touch each other), a pain is felt: quite light at first, but then like a burning drop. As it increases, it subsequently triggers pains, burning sensations, and finally, often, swellings. For then the sourness conceived in the spirit, through a spiritual fermentation and an active alteration, defiles the **spermatic glue** <note>original: "gluten spermaticum"; the protein-rich fluid Helmont believes maintains the tissues</note> that exists between the ligaments and the meeting of the bones. I have already shown before that the gouty character is by its nature born to infect and be transferred with the **seed** <note>original: "semine"; reproductive material</note>—just as Mercury infects the bones and teeth, or the saliva of a rabid dog infects the brain—as if in a lodging house in which it often lies hidden for a long series of years.

<margin>15.</margin> Therefore, by the power of this symbolic connection, it is fitting that the gouty character primarily concerns the seeds. Nevertheless, since all of Nature is anxious about sex and is a diligent preserver and savior of the species, she takes particular care, as much as she can, so that the character does not infect

<column-break/>

the species, nor settle into the testicles. For this reason, she could not at least prevent it from immediately infecting, according to its nature, the liquid adjacent to the seed, which **Paracelsus** <note>A famous 16th-century Swiss physician and alchemist</note> calls **synonia** <term>Synonia: An early term for synovial fluid, the lubricating liquid found in the joint cavities.</term>, which is poured out abundantly between the capsules of the ligaments and the contacts of the bones. But at that moment of sexual union,

<margin>16.</margin> the character of Gout—otherwise sleeping in the **Archeus** <note>the "internal chemist" or governing spirit of the body</note>—is awakened under such great agitation of lust. Together with the spirit, it is mixed into the seed in a clearly irregular way; nature, then unable to hold the reins of control, could not prevent the poison of the character from infectiously fermenting the lustful seed. Thus, since the seed, or character of Gout, regularly contaminates the spermatic materials, it most readily affects the **Synonia**, which is found nowhere else in isolation except where two bones touch each other. Hence the place or "nest" of Gout is in the joints. Since these effects must follow once the causes are established, Nature, lacking the means for its own preservation, does not allow the "characterized" spirit to infect the synonia except in the regions far removed from the heart. It is from this that the names **Podagra** <note>Gout of the foot</note> and **Chiragra** <note>Gout of the hand</note> are borrowed.

<margin>17.</margin> But eventually, when the disease has acquired strength by its progression and nature has lost its own, Gout also infests the closer parts of the body.

<margin>18.</margin> Thus, the sourness of Gout conceived in the spirit exists **potentially** in the seed, without being **actual** sourness. Just as, for instance, the seed of a pear does not manifest the taste of the fruit. But when the time of maturity is at hand, the acidity is activated in the spirit and contaminates it; this spirit then, in a short space of time, contaminates the Synonia with its ferment.

<margin>19.</margin> In the same way, the smell of a sour jar soon curdles fresh milk poured into it. Meanwhile, while these things are happening within, the entire Archeus of the body is altered within itself. Indeed, many sufferers of Gout know how to predict an approaching attack from a change in the **excrement** <note>referring here to skin secretions or "toe-cheese"</note> growing between the toes. This is certainly not a flowing down of a physical humor, but rather an alteration of the sweat and liquid itself—
