### IT IS DEMONSTRATED ###

The Adamic nature is horrid in the sight of the Lord, who indeed promises that he will raise up on the last day as many as have reverently received the Eucharist. For all people shall indeed rise by the "finger of God"—that is, by supernatural power. Therefore, whoever shall be changed in the act of rising are considered resurrected by the Lord Jesus; insofar as they rise in the body, which they acquired from the *wine that brings forth virgins* <note>original: "vino germinante virgines"; a reference to Zechariah 9:17, traditionally interpreted as the Eucharist providing the strength for chastity.</note>, they shall rise as sharers of the immaculate virginity of Jesus: *I will raise them up on the last day.* What else, I ask, does that promise signify, except that the elect will rise changed and resurrected by the Lord—not indeed in the flesh of sin, but in the Lord's flesh, which they shared through Baptism and the Eucharist. Therefore, the horrid and damned flesh of sin, not without the stain of unmerited impurity, sprinkles those who touch it.

There is, therefore, a distinct diversity of virginal purity: 
**First**, that which was found in Adam before the fall, which therefore contained a certain immortality by the favor of the tree of life. 
**Second**, the purity of those who were sanctified in their mother's womb: which is in itself twofold. For although such sanctification dismissed original sin and restored the integrity of lost purity, because they were nonetheless conceived from the "will of man and from bloods" <note>A reference to John 1:13, describing natural human procreation.</note> or from the flesh of sin, they were still mortal. 
But the most holy Mother-Virgin, immediately from the seminal mixing of her parents, was preserved from the bond and harm of original sin, before her <term>haecceity</term> <note>original: "hæccitatem"; a philosophical term referring to the specific "this-ness" or individual identity of a person.</note> or the arrival of the soul. Jeremiah and John [the Baptist], however, obtained the same, but after <term>ensoulment</term> <note>original: "empsychosin"; the moment the soul enters the body.</note>. In these two, there was indeed the remission of committed sin; but in the Virgin Mother of God, there was a prevention, before sin could touch her soul, and therefore she was assumed into heaven with her body; but not John, or Jeremiah. 
**Third**, purity is found in the rebirth from water and the Holy Spirit; which also arrives in two ways: to infants and to adults. For in adults, regeneration remits not only original sin,

<column-break/>

but also any grave sin. In little ones, however, it remits only original sin, because it finds no other. In both cases, however, it leaves behind death and the flesh hurrying toward the state of a corpse, because it was raised from the Adamic union. 
**4.** The purity of those who have "made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of God" <note>Matthew 19:12.</note> is considered: and that in a twofold path. For either they have devoted their virginity to the Lamb from childhood and observe it—and therefore they also follow him wherever he goes and sing the hymn, etc. <note>A reference to the 144,000 virgins in Revelation 14:4.</note>—but all of that is after death. For otherwise they are of the flesh of sin, and therefore necessarily also liable to death and decay. But those who lost their purity by their own error, and thereafter rising up, vowed or observed chastity; these, although chaste, are not to be counted among the virgins. Indeed, after matrimonial generation was established by the Lord, regeneration from the Holy Spirit and water does not pre-require virginity. 
**5.** The apex of all purity and chastity is the Lord JESUS himself, who, not being conceived from sexual union, was truly immortal (and the first who therefore rose from the dead by his own power) unless the loving mission, for which he had come, made him choose to be born in the "form of a servant." 

Therefore, the question which drove many, anxious about the immaculate conception of the Mother of God, into bitter quarrels, seems to me now decided. Furthermore, not only is regeneration through Baptism enjoined: but also, <margin>56a</margin> unless we eat of the *supersubstantial bread* <note>original: "pane supersubstantiali"; a term from the Vulgate version of the Lord's Prayer (Matthew 6:11), often interpreted as the Eucharist.</note>, we shall not have life in us. This benefit of vital purity is the supreme pledge given for the life of the world—that is, for the falling, Adamic, miserable, and mortal life. For that heavenly bread which came down from Heaven (which is the "wine that brings forth virgins," and the same in its underlying reality) by its own free property removes the stain contracted from Adam and the shattered virginity of Eve; because the merits of the Passion in that shared pledge of unsullied virginity...

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the Eucharist, specifically how participation in the Body of Christ grants the believer a share in His virginal nature and the merits of the Passion, transitioning into a physical analogy involving alchemy.</meta>

### THESIS. ###

...with the divinity of the Lord’s body. Thus, the communion of that most chaste body unites us to His mystical body and makes us partakers of His incomprehensible and loving Incarnation, insofar as by being born again, we participatively put on His virginity (in which we must be saved). For Christ was born so that He might be crucified for us. His death, therefore, was intended to give us life, and this in a universal sense for the entire human race. Individually, however, as often as the bread becomes the body of the Lord, Christ is, in a sense, born again—not indeed to be crucified once more, but to grant to that human individual who eats the reborn Lamb the intended goal of His Incarnation, that is, the merits of His passion. There are, without doubt, two principal ends of the most holy Eucharist: namely, that the virginal nature of Christ and the merits of His passion may be united to us through communion. Indeed, baptized children will rise in a glorified body, yet one that is less luminous in proportion to how far they were removed from the union with the beatific body. And even if visible signs of such a great effect do not appear now—such as those I mentioned earlier regarding baptism—they are nonetheless truly communicated to the immortal mind. For it is the mind that will eventually lead its own body back into the form of a spirit. Otherwise, the regeneration that did not pre-exist by being born again in this world would not grow anew in the resurrection. Nor is faith concerned with fictional non-entities, but with things that are primarily true, even if they are not immediately visible, because they work primarily upon the immortal mind, which is invisible.

<margin>57.</margin>
Therefore, although the symbol of union with God through the Eucharist is entirely inscrutable, and its fruits are invisible to us, this mystical and real rebirth is nevertheless considered in the discourse to Nicodemus <note>A reference to the Gospel of John, Chapter 3, where Jesus explains being "born again" to the Pharisee Nicodemus.</note> as something still earthly and, as it were, natural. It is under this title that I have transferred this free gift of purity into these physical considerations; namely, so that under the doctrine of long life, I might also speak of the immortal life, insofar as it is understood by

<column-break/>

true Christians and actually put into true practice. For I contemplate that the regeneration and participation in life of those to be saved, occurring in the communion of the Eucharist, is counted among earthly things because something similar to it is found elsewhere among earthly matters;

<margin>58.</margin>
Almost exactly as in the "projection" <note>The final stage of the alchemical process, where the Philosopher's Stone is cast upon a base metal to transmute it.</note> of the stone of <term>chrysopoeia</term> <note>The art of making gold from base metals.</note>. Indeed, I have several times handled that stone with my own hands and seen with my own eyes the real transmutation of commercial mercury, which surpassed by weight the <term>chrysopoeic powder</term> <note>The "red powder" or "Philosopher's Stone" used in alchemical transformation.</note> by several thousand times. It was, in fact, the color of saffron in its powdered state, heavy, and glinting like crushed glass when it was less finely ground. Once, I was given one-fourth part of a single grain. (I define a "grain" as the six-hundredth part of an ounce). I wrapped this powder in wax scraped from a letter, lest in casting it into the crucible it should be scattered by the soot of the coals. Then, I cast that little ball of wax upon a pound of boiling mercury, recently purchased, in a triangular crucible. Immediately, all the <term>hydrargyrus</term> <note>Another name for mercury or quicksilver.</note> stopped flowing with a slight sound and settled like a mass of dough. The heat of that mercury was great enough to prevent molten lead from re-solidifying. Soon after, the fire was increased with bellows and the metal melted; after overturning the melting pot, I found that it weighed eight ounces of the purest gold. Thus, by calculation, one grain of that powder converts 19,200 grains of impure and volatile metal (which can be destroyed by fire) into true gold. Indeed, that powder, by uniting itself to the aforementioned mercury, preserved it in a single instant from eternal rust, decay, death, and the torture of fire—no matter how violent—and insofar as it made it immortal against any strength or industry of art and fire, it transferred it into the virginal purity of gold. At least one moderate fire of coals is required for this. In the same way, provided there is a just fervor in the faithful, a tiny amount of this mystical and Divine super-celestial bread regenerates, restores, and renews an immense number of the elect.

This was surely the unique goal of so great a Sacrament. And for this reason it is said: *With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you.* <note>Luke 22:15</note> May the theologian who is about to write concerning the life of the world forgive me if I have drawn a demonstration from earthly things through a likeness—following the Lord’s persuasion of Nicodemus <note>A reference to John 3, where Jesus explains being "born again" to the Pharisee Nicodemus using earthly metaphors.</note>—to confirm the real and heavenly regeneration of purity and the restoration of human fallenness, using an argument taken from the terrestrial. Moreover, the same Lord who gave His own life to the righteous person who eats, in place of the *Adamic life of the world*, will raise up on the last day the one who is thus regenerated and preserved against fire and death. In this way, the union of the Lord’s loving Incarnation makes us participants in His integrity, insofar as we participatively acquire the virginity of Christ—in which we must be saved—through regeneration. This is the most proper paraphrase of those words: *The wine that brings forth virgins.* <note>original: "Vinum germinans virgines," from Zechariah 9:17. In the mystical tradition, this "wine" is often identified with the blood of Christ in the Eucharist.</note> And without this remedy, some will rise again unchanged in the former and heavy body of Adam, with only the desired necessity of death taken away from them. I return to the privileges of that purity, so that it may be clear how closely it approaches the heavenly beings and the primitive state of innocence; thus we may also learn from this that the Creator's intention

<margin>59.</margin>
was for celibacy. For occasionally there comes to my mind that voice of Truth which, for those to be saved under the threat of infernal punishment, demands the state of little children: and we must despair of salvation unless we become like them. Yet in children I find sudden, swift, indiscreet, and frequent anger, blows, kicking, lies, disobedience, murmuring, insults, deceit and falsehood ready in their play, insatiable gluttony, immodesty, nuisances, aversions, inconstancy, and a dull innocence—finally, no acts of devotion, attention, or contribution. However, those are not the qualities in children that are required for those to be saved under the penalty of eternal loss. Finally, children are not lacking in their own pride of life, and the despising of others, and especially

<column-break/>

the hatred of the poor, as well as a frequent desire for revenge, cruelty, an itch for acquiring things, and the <term>concupiscence of the eyes</term> <note>A biblical term for the lustful or greedy desire for what one sees.</note>; they are entirely and perpetually devoted to and submerged in <term>autophilia</term> <note>Self-love or narcissism.</note>. But neither are these the things required in those to be saved under God’s indignation. They lack only the <term>concupiscence of the flesh</term> <note>Sexual lust or carnal desire.</note>. This is surely the mark that is required in such high tones for those to be saved. For this was the primitive intention in the act of creation. And therefore, I argue from the opposite sense that the principal crime of the Fall—the eating of the apple—concerns the breaking of that chaste modesty. That is to say, that original sin is located in the breaking of virginity, the act of lust, and the propagation of seed; and not merely in the act of disobedience and the scorning of the warning and the distrust of the truth of the Divine word. For even Saint Hildegard, in the third book of her life, seems to testify to the same.

<margin>60.</margin>
A matron (the author says), a Sybil from the city of Lausanne across the Alps, *who requested her help through a messenger, was delivered from a long-lasting flow of blood by the letters sent to her. You shall place these words between the breast and the navel, in the name of Him who disposes all things rightly:*
> *In the blood of Adam death arose; in the blood of Christ death was extinguished. In that same blood of Christ, I command you, O blood, to contain your flow.* 

And the matron was healed by these written words; a thing which others have experienced many times. Therefore, death is extinguished through the shedding of Christ’s blood and participation in it through being born again—that is, through the offering of pure chastity to God the Father, on behalf of those to be born again in His blood.

<margin>61.</margin>
Indeed, if we pay close attention, it is recognized that God loved women more than men in their sex, on account of their innate modesty. For this reason, He gave devotion to this sex as a free gift of nature, so that there might be in it a certain natural force and a virtue proper to the sex, acting as a mediatrix for salvation. For the first female Apostle, <note>The Samaritan woman at the well (John 4).</note> before the arrival of the <term>Paraclete</term> <note>The Holy Spirit.</note>, converted Samaria—the head of the Israelite kingdom (and otherwise most stubborn)—with a single sermon. Only the women followed from Galilee into death and sub-

...despite all the disgrace, they remained faithfully, albeit shamefully in the eyes of others, attached to Christ. They stayed even when the Disciples—who had witnessed so many miracles—had abandoned Him at the first gust of adversity. For these humble women <note>original: "mulierculæ"</note> rejoiced in insults, provided they could follow Christ as He carried the cross. Mary Magdalene was also the first to preach the Gospel of the resurrection to those who did not believe, and she strengthened the wavering in their faith. She deserved to be the first to see Christ after His death because she sought Him with the fervor of the greatest devotion. 

God, I say, has burdened this sex with many diseases, adversities, and subjections, so that it might be even more similar and closer to His Son. The world, however, scorns women and gives precedence to males; but in most things, the judgments of God are opposite to the judgments of the world. Just as the world scorns the poor—of whom Christ calls Himself the father, but not the father of the rich. 

<margin>62.</margin> Then, finally, Christ frequently calls Himself the "Son of Man." Since He did not have a human father, He therefore calls the Virgin woman "Man" <note>original: "hominem"</note> through a figure of speech <term>Antonomasia|the substitution of a title or epithet for a proper name, or vice versa</term>, a name of absolute dignity and worthy of the female sex. It is as if, because of that name ("Man"), she should henceforth be the counterpart to sin, standing for "woman" in its most noble sense. This shows at least that the Virgin Mother was the only human since the sin of Adam who was such as the Divinity had betrothed to Himself in the creation of the universe, intended to fill the places deserted by the Evil Spirit <note>original: "Cacodæmone"; a reference to the medieval tradition that humanity was created to replace the fallen angels who left heaven vacant</note>. And what Eve ceased to be through the breaking of her chastity, Mary, the most glorious virgin, truly became: the unique mother of those to be saved in the regeneration of purity. 

Nor have I merely undertaken a panegyric of that sex. It is enough to have shown that God loved the female sex for the love of chastity. <margin>63.</margin> For the virgin thinks on the things that belong to her God. <margin>64.</margin> The Apostle also commanded that widows who are truly widows are to be honored. And under the ancient law, all who had known their wives (even in marriage) were considered impure unless they were seriously washed; <margin>65.</margin> they were also to be kept away from the temple unless they were first properly cleansed. 

<column-break/>

Death also came suddenly to the one who, being impure in such a manner (though with good zeal), put his hand to the wobbling cart on which the Ark of the Covenant—an image of the Virgin Mother of God—was being carried <note>This refers to the biblical story of Uzzah from 2 Samuel 6, who was struck dead for touching the Ark to steady it</note>. In both cases, the consistent truth detests and bears witness to the foulness of the impure generation of Adam. For the impurity which is contracted from any natural flow of menstruation or seed, and even from touch, is considered equal to that which creeps in from contact with corpses, and it must be purified by the same rite. This is so the text might consistently denote that death began from the concupiscence <term>concupiscence|intense desire or lust, often seen in theology as the "fuel" of sin following the Fall</term> of the flesh lurking in the fruit of the apple. 

Therefore, the only remedy for such great impurity contracted from touch consisted in washing, an image by which the faith and hope that shone forth in Baptism <margin>66.</margin> are strengthened. For Adam knew that from fratricide <note>the killing of a brother, referring to the murder of Abel by Cain</note>—since he had generated the firstborn of mortals in the concupiscence of the flesh—an innocent and just brother had been killed. Foreseeing from this the heinous errors of mortals yet to come, and feeling within himself his own hardships, he knew for certain that all these calamities had come to him from the concupiscence of the flesh drawn from the apple, and that they would inevitably flow down to his descendants. 

He thought it best for himself, therefore, to abstain entirely thereafter from the wife whom he had violated, and he mourned in chastity and sorrow for one hundred full years <note>This tradition of Adam and Eve’s century of penance and separation is found in apocryphal texts like the *Life of Adam and Eve*</note>. He foolishly hoped that by the merit of that abstinence, as an opposite to the concupiscence of the flesh, he would return once more to his former majesty of purity. But when the penance of one century was completed, the mystery of the Lord's Incarnation was likely revealed to him. He learned that man can never hope to return to the brightness of original purity by his own power, and much less can he restore his own descendants from destruction. Therefore, marriage is well-pleasing and was granted to him by God soon after the fall, because God had determined to satisfy His justice in the fullness of time. Through this, the human race, for the glory of His name...

...and so that the confusion of Satan might lift humanity to a more eminent state of blessedness. Nevertheless, marriage was admitted in this way because of the lack of other means of propagation, and because the "otherness" <note>The author suggests that a different, divine way of multiplying was impossible after the Fall</note> of the primitive Divine generation was otherwise impossible.
<margin>67.</margin> Marriage is thus accepted as a Sacrament for the faithful; however, because it was eventually granted as if by a "turning of the blind eye" out of necessity, the Church—dictated by the Paraclete <note>The Holy Spirit</note>—established a rule against the Greeks. This rule states that the Priest (by whose office the body of the Lord is made flesh in the sacrifice of the Mass) must be entirely estranged from the act through which death and the impurity of nature were introduced. For the necessity of propagation once excused the "fault of otherness" in procreating. For, as Augustine testifies, *if the propagation of humans could happen in any other way, the conjugal act would be illicit.* <note>original: "si alio modo hominum propagatio posset fieri, actus conjugalis esset illicitus"</note> Therefore, it is not without merit that a man who has married twice is barred from the Bishopric, just as active marriage is barred from the Subdeaconate. For however much it may be a Sacrament, it is nevertheless unbefitting for the Sacrament of the Altar, through which the chastity of the first creation and the intention of the Creator are restored. For God refused to have blood offered to Him, even in burnt offerings, and forbade man to eat blood, remembering that blood (in which the sensitive soul resides)
<margin>68.</margin> had issued forth from the eating of the apple. Furthermore, brute animals feel fear, anger, flattery, grief, compassion, and they set ambushes; man possesses these passions from the "sensitive soul" <term>sensitive soul|In Aristotelian thought, the part of the soul shared by humans and animals that governs perception and movement</term> which he has in common with the beasts. Indeed, even elephants feel shame if they are reproached for doing something less than noble. But no animal feels shame from sexual union. From this it is manifest that the lust <note>original: "concupiscentia"</note> of the flesh is Diabolical in man alone, whereas in beasts it is earthly and natural. If, therefore, both parents were ashamed immediately after eating the apple, and covered only their shameful parts for that reason, then that shame presupposes and accuses them of something committed against justice, the

<column-break/>

intention of the Creator, and against their own nature. Consequently, Adamic generation <note>human reproduction through sex</note> is not part of the primitive constitution of his nature, nor of the primordial intent of the Creator. Therefore, when God predicts that *the earth shall produce thistles and thorns*, and that *man shall eat his bread in the sweat of his brow*, as already proven above, these were not curses, but warnings. They were warnings that such things would be encountered on earth: that beasts would bring forth in pain, plow in sweat, and eat their food with labor and fear—and that the earth would produce many things beyond the farmer's intent. Thus, those who had begun to procreate in the manner of beasts should also be nourished like beasts. Then, if the text is considered more deeply,
<margin>69.</margin> it is announced to Eve after her transgression that she would bring forth her offspring in pain. Undoubtedly, it follows from this that before sin she would have given birth without pain; that is, just as she had conceived with a closed womb, so too would she have given birth. What, then, does the pain of childbirth have in common with the eating of an apple, unless the apple had some effect upon conception or the lust of the flesh? And consequently, unless the apple had incited that union? And had the Creator not intended to discourage that union by forbidding the eating of the apple? For why are the genital members of the woman punished with the pains of birth, if the eye sinned by seeing the apple, the hand by plucking it, and the mouth by eating it? Would it not have been enough to punish life with death and health with many diseases? Why, furthermore, is the womb (which is innocent of the eating) afflicted with the pain of birth in a brutal manner, if conception—which is permitted to beasts—had not been forbidden to man? After the fall, therefore, their eyes were opened, and they were ashamed. This signifies that from the filth of lust they recognized that the coupling of the flesh had been forbidden to them in the most innocent chastity of nature; they were suffused with shame while they beheld the committed disgrace with the open
<margin>70.</margin> eyes of their intellect. But upon the serpent and the Evil Demon <note>original: "Cacodæmonem"</note> alone was placed the head of the whole curse, just as [it was placed upon] the woman’s...

the woman's privilege and the mysterious prerogative of blessing upon the earth. Namely, that the woman (and not the man, although he was already established as the head of the woman) would one day crush the head of the serpent. And so, it is not possible that giving birth in pain was merely a curse, since from the same mouth of the Lord, the woman's blessing and victory over hell were immediately pronounced. Furthermore, being subject to her husband was not enjoined upon the woman as a form of execration <note>original: "exsecrationis," meaning a formal curse or exclusion</note>. For the Son of Man humbled himself even unto death. He also called for one to be exalted through being extinguished by an ignominious death. Therefore, while the Lord presses the woman down under the power of the man, he simultaneously exalted her before Himself and made her more similar to Himself <note>referring to the Christian paradox where the humble and suffering are raised highest</note>. Otherwise, the fact that the serpent would henceforth crawl upon the earth was not from a curse, but was proper to it as a created reptile, as the very name of "serpent" proves; and this was well enough known to Adam. For in this, the curse fell not so much upon the serpent as upon the Evil Demon <note>original: "Cacodæmoni"</note>, because that lying impostor had hidden himself within the lowliest reptile. It was his head, therefore, and not that of some mere reptile, which the woman crushed. 
<margin>71.</margin> 
Furthermore, certain beasts were once judged as "impure," and were forbidden from kitchens and human use, specifically those that generate through prolonged copulation (among which reptiles are not in the last place), etc. Our thesis contains and in turn confirms this mystery: namely, that the impurity of our nature takes its origin from the concupiscence of the flesh. Therefore, the mating of beasts is seen by God as marked, distinct, and contaminated by impurity. 
<margin>72.</margin> 
Finally, even in the law concerning menstruation, the woman—and anything touching her—was judged to bring about impurity. Otherwise, this would have to be seen as entirely innocent, being turned toward a secondary and natural cause; unless the menstrual flow, in its natural course, derived from the same causes from which death

<column-break/>

<margin>73.</margin> 
Moreover, the fact that only the woman suffers menstruation, unlike the beasts, certainly attests to no prerogative of our race, but rather an all-encompassing defect. Specifically, it is related to the punishment of lost modesty <note>original: "cassæ pudicitiæ"</note> and to secondary causes, according to the notable mystery of our thesis. Nor does it stand in the way of this that chaste virgins are subject to menstruation, or that it is a monstrous thing for a woman not to be "menstruous" when the opportunity arises. This is because the Adamic generation <note>the lineage of humans descended from Adam after the Fall</note> is compelled to carry the inconveniences of its nature no less than death itself. Indeed, since chastity does not excuse a virgin 
<margin>74.</margin>

This is no different than how death itself began from secondary causes inserted by the "diffused apple" <note>original: "pomo diffuaso," referring to the eating of the forbidden fruit</note>, although these were previously unknown and unconsidered. Therefore, menstruation—occurring in the woman alone and not in beasts—proves that the transgression of the fatherly warning occurred in the very parts of shame <note>original: "pudendis," the genitals</note>. For this reason, they are branded with a perpetual sign, like an impure, bloody seal. These things surely would have no place if sexual union for the propagation of man had not inverted the intention of the Creator more than it did in the beasts. 
<margin>75.</margin> 
At this point, a paradoxical and incidental consideration occurs, inserted as if by a parenthesis: that since Adam was created in the possession of immortality, God did not intend for man to be an animal, nor to be born, conceive, or live as an animal. For he was created into a "living soul" <note>original: "animam viventem"</note>, so that he might be the closest image of God. He was therefore as far removed from the animal nature as the immortal is from the mortal, and as a God-like creature is from a beast; which is surely more than an entire category of being. It is most admirable, and should be considered a source of indignation, that the Schools of Christ <note>theologians and scholars</note> believe and confess these things, yet still define the essence of man as being derived from an animal nature...

And so, just as the sensitive soul arose in man beyond the intention of the Creator and nature: so it is of no brutal species, nor can it subsist, unless it be continually bound to the mind, from which it is sustained in life. And the offspring of Adam would likewise have perished immediately, had God not consented to marriage for him. They confess, finally, that the conditions of being, living, and sensing in man are perhaps entirely distant from the animal nature, because they follow the force of the rational form or the immortal Mind. But they shamefully believe that man, as much in his first constitution as now regenerated divinely through the Sacraments, is an "essential animal." Oh, let it be a shame to be ignorant that man, the Evil Demon, and all nature together cannot in any way change the essence given to them from the eternal foreknowledge of the Creator, but that he would continually remain such as he was created: although in the meantime he has put on foreign properties for himself, as if they were natural, through the vice of his own will. For just as it is not without absurdity to count a glorified man among the animals because he is not without sensation: so to be sensitive does not dictate the inseparable essence of an animal. And since otherwise the definition of any thing is from the essence of the thing itself (as they will have it), and man truly according to his essence was made in full possession of immortality and subsequent eternal duration according to his soul: the Schools could not believe man to be essentially an animal on account of the sensitive soul alone: especially while they believed his essence to depend on eternal duration and an incorruptible soul or form. All of which absurdities I acknowledge have crept into and remained in the Schools because the truth of our thesis was unknown.

Augustine argued that because Christ was not conceived through lust, He did not inherit "sinful flesh."</note> As if to say: *Whatever is born of sexual union, even if it had been born in Paradise and before sin, would have been and is the flesh of sin.* Since only that which is not born of sexual union is not <margin>Chapter 24.</margin> the flesh of sin. *Whatever offspring is born from <term>concupiscence</term><note>Strong desire or lust, which theologians argued was the "carrier" of original sin.</note>, or from the flesh of sin, is bound by original sin, unless it is reborn in Him whom a <margin>Augustine, *Against Julian*, Book 5, Ch. 15.</margin> Virgin conceived without concupiscence. The flesh of Christ drew mortality from the mortality of the maternal body: because it did not encounter the concupiscence of one lying together.* Indeed, just as original sin is not passed down to posterity in any other way than through the concupiscence of the flesh: so it is necessary that concupiscence was enclosed in the apple, from which the human stock, by generating, <margin>Augustine, *Against Julian*, Book 5, Ch. 12.</margin> degenerated and was corrupted. For if offspring could be generated in any other way than through a carnal union, <margin>77.</margin> the matrimonial act would be illicit. This dilemma serves that point: *That act, before the eating of the apple, was either illicit and unthought of; or it was licit.* If it was illicit, our thesis is already proven. But if it was licit, then whatever I described above from Augustine is false. Therefore, when they had actually felt the effect of the eaten apple—that is, the concupiscence of the flesh—in their members while still in Paradise, they were immediately ashamed that their members, which they could previously rule at a nod of the head, were then moved by the incentive of their own lust. Finally, how much virginity has always pleased the Bridegroom of the soul is clearly enough apparent from various histories of the Saints. And indeed, in Cana of Galilee, the bridegroom followed the Lord

<column-break/>

Jesus, leaving the bride behind; and he is that disciple whom Jesus loved so much for that reason. <note>A common medieval tradition held that the bridegroom at the Wedding of Cana was John the Evangelist, who left his bride to remain a virgin and follow Christ.</note> The same is familiar in the stories of <term>Alexius</term>, <term>Giles</term>, <note>Saint Alexius and Saint Giles (Aegidius) were popular figures in hagiography known for abandoning worldly lives or marriage for asceticism.</note> and many others, especially among young virgin women. <margin>78.</margin> Indeed, infinite goodness, by its own movement of pleasure, created and loved man with such great love from eternity that it determined to connect its Divinity to him and illuminate him with the light that illuminates every man coming into this world; and to adopt him as a son of God, giving him the power to become a son of God through <term>rebirth</term><note>renafcentia; here referring to spiritual regeneration or baptism</note>, which rebirth was not necessary before sin. Wherefore he aspired to overcome God (whom he had not yet seen) and cast Him down from the seat of Majesty. Then, soon after, being even more fiercely indignant while he paid the penalties for his sins, he saw that Eve, a virgin without any merit and out of the sole goodness of God, had been freely destined as the aforementioned instrument of that adoption and the mother of men. He therefore tried to hinder Divine love through the eating of the apple. For he saw that lewdness and concupiscence of the flesh were implanted in it, diametrically opposed to the Divine intention. Therefore, the eating of the apple was not forbidden to man by law, but by paternal admonition. Nor is original sin derived from the transgression of a Law or from the eating of the apple simply as a forbidden food, but because of the effect arising from the apple and the properties inserted into it. Otherwise, the transgression or eating would only have been a sin in a voluntary act [of the parents]: it would not have affected posterity, except naturally, through the secondary causes of the brutal intercourse following from it. (Which would have been otherwise impossible in the First Parents) and would have inverted the intention of Divine generation.

...it remains. Indeed, original sin did not fall upon innocent descendants so much as a legal charge, but rather as a physical effect of reproduction. This process gave birth to a generation that was adulterous, beast-like, diabolical, and utterly incapable of entering the kingdom of heaven or achieving divine union and enjoyment. Because of this resemblance to those born of <term>adultery</term><note>The author uses "adultery" here in a spiritual and biological sense, suggesting the human lineage became "illegitimate" in the eyes of God after the Fall.</note>, they were excluded from participation in heaven. 

<margin>79.</margin>
Let us imagine the opposite: that the law of the forbidden fruit was given to the parents while they were fully aware of it by God, the creator of the universe. If they were held as such, and death was predicted for themselves and all their descendants—and would undoubtedly come—then at least such an enormous sin, such a bold crime, so impious and atrocious, could not be dismissed across all posterity without a great sign of contrition. Nor would God, however merciful and good, have so suddenly blessed that man with fertility and placed all other living things beneath his feet. leaves. I conclude from this that on that same day, not only did mortality enter through <term>concupiscence</term><note>Disordered desire or lust, often cited by medieval and early modern theologians as the biological "carrier" of original sin.</note>, but it also immediately entered into the very act of reproduction that was soon conceived. It was in respect to this that they were driven out of Paradise on that same day. Therefore, original sin was effectively born from the lust of the flesh; the eating of the apple and the scorned warning were merely the *occasional* cause <note>In philosophy, an "occasional cause" is the trigger for an event, but not the force that actually produces the effect.</note>. However, the poison of lust was located in the tree of warning (or rather, the tree that was advised against), and it was radically inserted and implanted within it as its own property.

When Satan saw that—contrary to his expectations and despite the defilement of the virgin—man was not removed from the world according to the warning (for Satan was unaware that the Son of God had established Himself as a guarantor before the Father on man's behalf), he looked into human nature and saw it was indeed corrupted and degenerate. Since the power of uniting oneself with a God of infinite majesty had been taken away, he rejoiced greatly; but he felt pain once he knew that marriage was now 

<column-break/>

granted. He realized that Divine goodness still leaned toward man, and thus his own Satanic fallacies, deceits, and calculations were being mocked. From this, he conjectured that the Son of God would restore every defect of the stain, and therefore perhaps would even become <term>incarnate</term><note>The doctrine of the Incarnation: that God became human in the form of Jesus Christ.</note>. He searched to see if he could so contaminate the lineage rising from marriage with a mortal soul that he might render God’s entire plan vain. For this reason, he not only stirred up his fratricides and criminals, so that there would be much evil at all times, but he also ensured that <term>atheism</term> would arise, taking root and growing stronger day by day alongside paganism. By this, he hoped that if he could not prevent the connection of the immortal mind with the sensitive soul, he might at least—by destroying man under the law of nature—drag him away with himself into infernal punishment. 

But most of all, he meditated on how he might gradually erase the immortal mind from the future lineage. He therefore stirred up wicked sexual acts among his atheist libertines. He saw that the union of men with women was far more successful, and by this method, the generation of men continued equally and constantly. It was not enough for the infernal enemy to have rendered man incapable of heaven; he further attempted to prevent any remaining hope of restoration—that is, to hinder the Incarnation of the Son of God. He therefore attempted to see if, through the application of active substances, he could manufacture "male seed" according to his own wicked whim. 

When he found this attempt was useless and impossible for him, he tried again to see if a "witch-sow" <note>original: "scrofa saga." When even this did not yield a result that matched his intention, and he observed elsewhere that a mule is born from a donkey and a beast of burden (resembling the mother more than the father), and that from a rabbit and a dormouse-father a true rabbit is born (distinguished from the mother only by the dormouse’s tail), he shifted his tricks. Indeed, remembering these things, the old law still shudders at such comminglings of species...

...produced things horrible to God: although today among Christians these things are so admitted that the Primates of the Church ride upon monsters <note>original: "monstris"</note> horrible to God. <margin>§ 1.</margin> Therefore, Satan established a connection between male seed (having first been warmed for a short time) and the womb of a young witch <note>original: "sagæ"</note>. And from this there came forth a certain adulterous generation of Fauns, Satyrs, Sylphs, Gnomes, Nymphs, Dryads, Nereids, and other monsters, according to the various conditions the male seed underwent. And since the Fauns and forest Nymphs excelled the others in beauty, they subsequently produced offspring among themselves; the descendants of these again contracted concubinage among themselves, and at last established marriages with men. They lied, claiming that in this way they would obtain an immortal soul (as the credulous <term>Paracelsus</term><note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a physician and alchemist who wrote extensively on elemental beings.</note> testifies) for themselves and the children to be born from that union. Moreover, they told these lies at the Devil's persuasion, so that men, thinking they were performing a pious work, might admit those monsters to carnal copulation. Those who were ignorant were easily persuaded of this, as if the creation of the immortal soul and its connection to the perishing soul depended on human free will and seed. I will show below that this is false, both from the Holy Scriptures and from the account of St. Anthony in the *Life of Paul the First Hermit* <note>original: "Anachoretæ"</note> described by Jerome. For this reason, such Nymphs were called "succubae" in ancient times. However, so that Satan might make the wickedness even worse, he frequently transforms himself into the simulated personas of both sexes, acting as both <term>incubus</term><note>A male demon believed to have sexual intercourse with sleeping women.</note> and <term>succubus</term><note>A female demon believed to have sexual intercourse with sleeping men.</note> at once. But none conceived true offspring from males except the Nymphs; and when the "sons of God" (that is, men) had indiscriminately and everywhere taken these as wives, God was forced to destroy the entire race born of such wicked marriages through the flood of waters, so that the intent of the <term>Evil Demon</term><note>original: "Cacodæmonis"</note> might be frustrated. <margin>§ 2.</margin> A certain wine merchant, a countryman of 

<column-break/>

ours and an honest man, who sailed several times to the Canary or "Fortunate" Islands, asked me for a serious judgment regarding certain creatures which the boys there would bring home from the mountains whenever they wished. They called them *Tudesquilli* or "Little Germans." For they were dried-out corpses, barely three feet long, which any of the boys could easily carry with one hand <note>original: "uno palmo," literally "with one palm."</note>. They were of human form, but the entire corpse was transparent like parchment, and the bones were flexible, like cartilage. When held against the Sun, their internal organs and intestines could be seen. Since I later learned from Spaniards born there that these things were true, I considered that the lineage of <term>Pygmies</term><note>Commonly used in early modern texts to describe diminutive legendary races or "elementals."</note> has been destroyed there today. For the Almighty wished to render the vain and useless expectations of the Evil Demon, built upon the human race, null and void. <margin>§ 3.</margin> Now, however, I shall propose several doubts against our thesis. For those who are not merely abstaining, but are chaste by a certain pre-election, seem to be sanctified and even promoted to a further degree of perfection. Therefore, they follow the Lamb wherever He goes.

### IT IS DEMONSTRATED

Indeed, just as those who act rightly assume a hope of reward, so too do those virgins who practice abstinence and endurance keep themselves within the bounds of love and <margin>84.</margin> humility. Nor does it argue to the contrary that in the first chapter of Genesis <note>original: "i. c. Gen. 27" – the text likely intends Genesis 1:27</note>, God created male and female; or that in Genesis 1:28, He blessed them so that they might increase and multiply and fill the earth. It is often argued as if marriage had been established by the Creator's original institution and primary intention. However, Genesis Chapter 1 completes the entire history of creation succinctly. In contrast, Chapters 2 and 3 follow with the specific creation of the woman in Paradise, as well as the story of sin, and so forth. Therefore, the blessing of generation <note>the power to reproduce</note> was not described in Genesis 1:28 as though it were given at the very beginning of creation, nor was it given in Paradise even after the woman was formed. Rather, it followed from sin and the banishment from Paradise to the earth. For it is said that they should "fill the earth" with offspring, but not Paradise. Furthermore, they were given full dominion over the beasts of the earth. In this, the goodness of the Creator is manifested: that He blessed a guilty creature, who had not yet repented, with offspring—even though those offspring would be corrupt and impure. He did this, of course, because He foreknew the restoration for which His own Son had stood as a surety <note>original: "vadem"</note> before the justice of the Father. Otherwise, on the very day they tasted the apple, they would have actually and necessarily perished, had not the Father accepted the death of His Son for the remission of sin. <margin>85.</margin> Thirdly, an objection could be raised: "God made nothing in vain." Since He fashioned sexual organs for the parents from the beginning, which denote a necessity of purpose, it would seem God sufficiently exposed His intention and the modern mode of generating within their very bodies from the start. I respond by conceding that the Creator bestowed these members upon them along with the freedom of will. Otherwise, the freedom to sin through the lust of the flesh <note>original: "concupiſcentiam carnis"</note> would have been granted in vain if they had lacked the organs to do so. Just as God’s intention for a future regeneration <note>spiritual rebirth</note> is not rightly turned into a license for the will to sin, so much less is that same intention correctly inferred from the

<column-break/>

structure of the organs. For this argument is similar to saying: "GOD made remedies against disease and death, therefore God made death and disease." The conclusion is false, and therefore the premise is as well. For from eternity, the Almighty foresaw the fall of Adam; He was not content with Paradise alone but created the earth in addition, and from the earth, Medicine against death and disease. In the same way, He made the genitals for our first parents. It was enough for Adam that he never felt any stimulus from his own members, nor from the sight of the woman’s nakedness; and likewise for the woman in the company of the man. This state of "insensibility" is called the state of innocence. Otherwise, one could equally conclude: "God created man to live happily in Paradise, therefore He created the earth in vain before the transgression," especially since sin was a contingent result of free will. Both of the aforementioned arguments stem from a failure to premeditate the end of contingent events; therefore, they contain an implicit blasphemy. For GOD did not create the earth only for Himself and the beasts; likewise, the sexual organs denote a foreknowledge of future events, but <margin>86.</margin> not the divine intention in the act of creating. Finally, the Atheists struggle, wishing to claim the text is fabulous and ridiculous because the effects or the disobedience of eating an apple would pass to all descendants. <margin>87.</margin> That argument has already been sufficiently countered. They also argue: "If shame <note>original: "pudor"</note> comes from original sin, then since sin touches all equally, so too should shame affect children, adults, Black people, Americans <note>indigenous peoples of the Americas</note>, Egyptians, Abyssinians <note>Ethiopians</note>, and so on. Yet, even the Christian priests of the Abyssinians have not been ashamed until now; therefore, shame does not come from eating the apple, nor from the sin of disobedience, nor from the unusual novelty of generating or the lust of the flesh." But these Sophists <note>deceptive reasoners</note> do not know that shame was gradually forgotten among Barbarians, and the loss of modesty arose through scurrilous habit and a prior lack of clothing. Lest the people of Israel should likewise lose this shame (being for a large part...

# THESIS.

...the wicked one) **GOD** did not permit the clothes of the people to wear out during their 40 years in the desert. By that continuous miracle, **God** prevented the loss of modesty, and by that sign, He showed that nothing would be as hateful to Him as the loss of modesty. From this, it becomes clear that the modesty acquired through the eating of the fruit was not troublesome to **GOD** nor forbidden: rather, beneath the term "modesty" <note>original: "pudoris etymo"</note> lies the chaste language of the Sacred Scriptures, which was used to cover the forbidden concupiscence <note>intense sexual desire</note> of the flesh. Finally, as many as set aside their barbarism also reclaim the modesty they had previously lost. Indeed, it is no wonder that nations lost their modesty through the advice of that scoundrel <note>likely referring to a specific critic or the Devil</note> who teaches that modesty is found in the "knowledge of evil."

<margin>88.</margin> Finally, the **Atheists** attack, claiming it is a ridiculous fable if one believes the serpent spoke with a human voice to persuade **Adam**. They argue that Adam, who had given the animals their proper names, could not have been ignorant of the fact that a serpent lacks the power of speech; for **Adam** ought to have been stunned, rather than believing such a persuader. But these wretched men are mistaken. The serpent counterfeited the face of a man; it is no wonder if **Adam** had not yet given a name to such a monstrous portent. And if he had been required to name it from its essence (as with other beasts), he would have called that serpent a "rational, scholarly, and speaking animal." This is not unlike what appeared to **Blessed Anthony** in the desert. First, a four-legged monster came to meet him, which, when it began to speak, spoke imperfectly and fled. And then another, in the form of a satyr <note>a mythological creature, half-man and half-goat</note>, which spoke the native languages perfectly. One should not think that this monster was the **Devil** (since the Devil never asks for prayers to **God** for himself), and therefore, by the same authority of the **Church** by which **Paul**, the first of the **Hermits**, was recorded among the number of the **Saints**, it is called an animal. It is not called a **Devil** or a **Spirit**; and it is depicted by **St. Jerome** with the characteristics borrowed from **Blessed Anthony**. **Adam**, therefore, could speak to the serpent just as **Anthony** spoke to the Satyr. The present text of

<column-break/>

**Genesis** has hitherto had no "heresiarch" <note>a leader of a heretical sect</note> as an opponent, following **Origen** and the **Atheists**, because it relates a true and literal history.

<margin>89.</margin> I will add a final point, as if by a digression <note>original: "per impertinens"</note>. Indeed, I have said that fish do generate, but not through sexual union, even though they possess genital organs. Above all, I believe the generation of egg-laying fish to be univocal <note>producing offspring of the same species and nature</note>. The example of one will suffice; for it was not possible for me to investigate every species of fish beneath the waters. There is a certain rock-dwelling fish, a meat-eater, and easily the swiftest of all fish, called the trout <note>original: "truta"</note> by our people. Near a stream where the **Tiber** falls perpendicularly from a high cliff, it is seen climbing the entire height of the cliff—at least five hundred feet—in a straight line. It swims upward against the rushing whirlpool three times faster than the headlong water falls downward.

<margin>90.</margin> Here, the dogma of the Schools <note>the traditional academic philosophy of the time</note> is proven false—specifically that water always falls in a circular shape. For in that place, every little drop of water can be seen with a point at the rear, and the point is sharper the further it falls. This is proven by the resistance of the air. For even if they want water to imitate a circle because a sphere is the most capable of shapes, by that same logic of its size, it cleaves the air with great difficulty, which consequently hinders the speed of its fall.

<margin>91.</margin> Furthermore, the female trout, as the eggs grow large inside her, feels the birthing membrane break and gradually open, in which the eggs are housed as if in a pouch. Soon she exerts herself and deposits the eggs on a sandy bottom. Indeed, the very imagination of the trout loses the eggs <note>this suggests the mother's mental state or instinct triggers the release</note>. For if it has only a stony bottom (as I have observed in our fountains cemented with lime), they do not produce their eggs; but if the bottom is strewn with sand, they bring forth the eggs. The male then sprinkles the eggs produced by the female, and broods over the eggs from the outside like a spider's web. And finally, thus shielded, the eggs transform into little fish. In this species, therefore, there is no carnal union; such a union would be useless, as it could not reach even a thousandth part of the eggs internally.

<margin>98.</margin>
But since before the flood there was no promise of celibacy or chastity, and the Monastic vow had not yet entered the mind as long as multiplication remained a mandate and a blessing, I have suspected (under the humble judgment of the Church) that the "Sons of God" were descendants born from man and woman, possessing the true image of God. The "daughters of men," however, were daughters procreated from the sons of Adam and Nymphs, whose Satanic origin God has always utterly abhorred. Furthermore, there was an incredible multitude of these in the desert, one of whom was sent to Saint Anthony <note>referring to the famous encounter of St. Anthony the Great with a satyr in the desert</note>. Also, in the days of Constantine, a living Satyr was carried about, put on display, and then shown preserved in salt. Likewise, in former times, various talking monsters were drawn from the Ocean, equipped with various skills, and even rational; they even lived among our own people. Namely, they were rational animals, conceived from nefarious intercourse in both the waters and the deserts. Therefore, when the first monsters had generated female offspring from the sons of Adam, they distinguished the sons of Adam by the name "Sons of God," and called monsters of this kind "daughters of men." Afterward, since the flood, paganism has named these Nymphs, Dryads, Nereids, Naiads, etc. Since these were beautiful to look upon, and men had taken them for wives, God, abhorring such filthiness and the devastation of the human species (which the text calls "great malice at all times"), 

<column-break/>

decided to wash the world clean with a cataclysm <note>the Great Flood</note>. From that cohabitation of monsters and Nymphs, they fathered Giants, powerful and famous men of that age; whom the pagans consequently worshipped long ago as Gods and Heroes. Otherwise, the reasons for the flood seem frivolous according to the literal letter: namely, that men were joined with women in marriage, and these had generated Giants, strong and famous men of the age. Therefore, the text must encompass the indignation of God and a sufficient cause for the flood. There is monstrosity not only in figure and the formation of the body, as at the beginning of these degenerations; but gradually, as the deformity was removed or diminished, the monstrosity remained in the sensitive soul <term>In medieval philosophy, the 'sensitive soul' provided movement and perception common to animals, but lacked the 'rational soul' or immortal mind unique to true humans</term>, which was not accompanied by an immortal Mind, even though they were externally animals using reason. Therefore, the law forbade different seeds to be sown in the same field, and forbade fabrics to be combined of linen and wool <note>original: "ex lino & lana"</note>. Truly, God was mindful of that vast and many-sided malice for which He had to destroy the world. From this, they lived basely in sin according to the habits of cattle, with the exception of the sons of God, who separated themselves from those same men and their lusts; from these Noah was born. This interpretation recognizes the "sons of God" in both sexes and clearly approves my reading of this text. Certainly, Satan had attempted by this means to destroy the human species and to hinder the immortal mind, so that there would be no source from which the Son of God could be born. Therefore, the Flood was necessary not only for the correction of sins, but for the salvation of the entire species. Otherwise, Ham <note>original: "Cham"; Noah's son, traditionally associated with the post-Flood spread of wickedness</note> would not have been saved through the Ark, for he was already entirely perverted by atheism.

Therefore (though under the humble judgment of the Church), I interpret the text thus: Namely, that the sons of God (who bore the image of God in an immortal soul and in the body) took the daughters of men (who showed only the human likeness in the rationality of the <term>sensitive soul</term> <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, the "sensitive soul" is the level of the soul responsible for sensation and movement, shared with animals, as opposed to the "rational soul" unique to humans</note> and in charming beauty) as wives because they were beautiful. **And from them they fathered giants, the strong and famous men of old.** For wickedness was great at all times, such that it repented God that He had created man, according to that saying: **All flesh had corrupted its way,** <note>Genesis 6:12</note> that is, every man had not only left the ways of the Lord, but had further corrupted the way which he had chosen for himself. For God had intended, through the overshadowing of the Holy Spirit, to generate man as the closest image of His own Deity and to join Himself intimately to him; but man preempted the divine intent. For which reason, God, being entirely good, later permitted marriage. Then again, man stained the generation of Adam, and had almost come to the destruction of the species, had the miracle of the Flood not intervened. And finally, the Devil would have again preempted God's intent through paganism, had the mercy of God not stood in the way in the fullness of time, sending the Son from His heart, to whom be all sanctification. Although God is no respecter of persons, and therefore not of sexes, it nevertheless pleased Him to burden the female sex with a narrower measure of tribulations <note>The author suggests women face more suffering as part of a divine mystery</note>

<column-break/>

owing to His unsearchable judgments. For even the hairs of the head are numbered, and a leaf does not fall from a tree unless permitted; much less is a woman or a girl born whom the finger of God has not fashioned. Therefore, I have inquired many times through the parishes following the knowledge of this paradox, and I have found everywhere in the books of those baptized annually that at least twice as many little daughters are born and baptized as males. Likewise, at least twice as many males are extinguished by diseases, travels, war, duels, shipwrecks, etc., than girls. From this it follows that God creates more daughters every year and allows more to grow up; and from this it finally becomes clear that such a full number of girls is not established by God except for the choice of virgins. Since He who forbade lust and adultery nevertheless creates and preserves a more copious supply of girls and a sparse catalog of males, He signifies by this that the constancy of celibacy in a woman is pleasing to Him: insofar as she approaches more closely to the purity and innocence of the first intention in creation. At the conclusion of this treatise, I shall bring forward what Saint Hildegard <note>St. Hildegard of Bingen (1098–1179), a German Benedictine abbess, mystic, and polymath</note> writes to the Gray Monks <note>Cistercians</note> on page 186:

> Virginity signifies the sun, which illuminates the whole world: because God joined virginity to Himself, which, having left man behind, brought forth her whom the ray of Divinity drenched, who also rules all things. For the King who rules all is God, and virginity is joined to Him, when God and man were born of a Virgin. Thus the Queen stood at his right hand, in a golden garment, surrounded by variety: because virginity stood resisting the Devil for the virtue of Divinity in a shining work, encompassed everywhere by a multitude of diverse virtues. For Divinity betrothed virginity to itself when the Angel first fell to the left side, and even now He chose for Himself the people of salvation in Adam, whom He named His right hand: from which people He joined virginity to Himself, which brought forth the greatest work. Because just as God created all things through His word, so also virginity, through the heat of the Holy Divinity, gave birth to the Son of God.

Therefore, some neglect this passage as if it were untouched; others, however, undertake to explain it through a certain rhythm. Namely, they suggest that rivers are drawn from the sea in the form of vapor, and then—through a scene of masked metamorphosis involving rain, snow, and storms—they eventually return to the sea. It is therefore necessary, first and foremost, to place before one's eyes the diversity of the grounds and the strata in the earth. For in one place, black earth occurs on the surface, abounding in dung and filth; elsewhere it is yellow, clayey, fatty, sterile, marshy, metallic, sandy, rocky, and adorned with various beauty, according to the temper of the soil and sky, the influence of the stars, and the adaptation of the rains: because these things are surely fruits, and not the element itself. If you pierce through this first "sole" of nature, in many places you will uncover rocks, metals again, or mineral juices; but in some places you find sand, and that sand here is yellow, elsewhere ash-colored, there blue, and then slightly green, according to the protean and multiform "un-yoked-ness" <note>original: "azygiarn"; likely a reference to substances that do not combine or are unique in their kind</note> of the latent spirit (for nature lies beneath the soil) and the destination of the subterranean Archeus <note>The "Archeus" is a Paracelsian term for the internal vital force or "master-chemist" that governs the formation of minerals and living things</note> received from the Creating Word.

# FIRST PARADOX.

<margin>6.</margin> beneath the unevenness of the sand and the beginnings of the rocks, that sand—I say, that most brilliant sand—is encountered. it is of a metallic quality and free from foreign contamination. This, I say, is the ultimate and impenetrable foundation of nature, yet it is not infrequently found on the surface of the earth. Indeed, being so indulgent of its own freedom, it laughs at our laws and spurns the barriers of our categories with its singular nature. Our people call this ultimate foundation of nature <term>Quelles</term> <note>original: "Quelles"; a Germanic term for a spring or source</note>, while the French call it <term>Sable bouillant</term> <note>literally "boiling sand," often referring to quicksand or highly pressurized water-bearing sand</note>; no shovel has yet passed through it. For no matter how much sand or water you deplete from it, more immediately flies to the spot in an unending and swift rush to fill the previous void. From this, therefore, I conclude:

<margin>7.</margin> That the aforesaid foundation, being the last in the order of nature, continues all the way to the center, unless perhaps Hell occupies some miles of the middle. It follows then that this sand is the very matter of the earth, not subject to change, but a perpetual and constant sieve through which nature filters the unending treasures of waters and the clearest springs into the common use of the Universe.

<margin>8.</margin> In this, I say, lies the vital vigor of the "boiling" water. For as long as the waters remain in this same foundation, they are "vivid" <note>vividæ; meaning "alive" or "full of life-force"</note>, not subject to considerations of being "above" or "below" in location, nor do they obey the laws of <term>Hydraulics</term> <note>the physical science of the motion of liquids</note>. Because they are alive, they preserve their vital property unharmed, just as the center itself does.

<margin>9.</margin> However, as soon as they flow out from there, they immediately die, no differently than blood outside a vein or a severed hand. For then, for the first time, they are forced to obey the laws of heavier bodies and the inconvenient positions of places and sites. Namely, they do not stop from that point on from rushing down slopes into the sea, as if seeking to return to their original home of rest.

<margin>10.</margin> Fourthly, it must be noted: that just as this foundation, when exposed to the air on the surface of the

<column-break/>

earth, expresses its native properties no less than that which lies hidden some hundreds of cubits below the earth's horizon; so also you must remember that the same sand ascends through the joints and wide gaps of the rocks to the greatest height of the mountains, and even to the very peak itself. From there, it turns into constant springs, which are not diminished in the least by summer heats.

<margin>11.</margin> In a human being, as long as the blood fluctuates within the veins, there is an equal regard for its position whether in the forehead or the feet; it knows neither "above" nor "below." But once it is outside the vein, it immediately takes on the fate of heavy things. So too in the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>the "Great World" or Universe, viewed as an analog to the human body</note>, as long as the water enjoys life in its first common hostelry, it hastens upward and downward without effort, because it does not know the difference. But once it has been shaken out of its vital hostelry, it does not cease to hurry until it recovers those blessed recesses of rest in the <term>Iliados</term> <note>original: "Iliado"; in Paracelsian philosophy, this refers to the primeval matter or the hidden spirit of the elements</note>. Thus, "a spirit nourishes the waters within, and a mind, diffused through the limbs, stirs the whole mass of the vast marble sea" <note>original: "Aquas itaque spiritus intus alit... mens agitat molem"; a paraphrase of Virgil’s Aeneid, Book VI, line 726, used here to describe the world-soul</note>. But from this, the sea—which waters the springs and vomits out the rivers, and toward which Scripture says they tirelessly hasten—is not yet sufficiently known.

<margin>12.</margin> For what Scripture calls "the sea" is the gathering of all waters into one continuous vessel. Of this collection,

<margin>13.</margin> this visible and external navigable sea is but the fruit, arranged like a canopy. Therefore,

<margin>14.</margin> that "boiling sand" contains the receptacle, congregation, root, and assembly of absolutely all waters. It is a thousand times richer and larger, and therefore contains that much more water than the Ocean. It fills almost the entire diameter of the earth, while the external sea fills a depth of only one or two leagues at most at the outermost edge.

<margin>15.</margin> For the <term>Archetype</term> <note>The Creator or Divine Model</note> separated the waters from the waters. He did not merely separate the sea from the rivers (or the sea would not be the gathering of all waters), nor did He just separate both of these from the clouds; rather, in the first days, He divided the *true and internal sea* from this external, navigable one.

# FIRST PARADOX.

<margin>16.</margin> This sea—the internal sea, I mean—is invisible (hitherto called the abyss) and vast. These are the waters upon which the Prophet <note>original: "Vates"; likely referring to the Psalmist or Moses</note> sang that the foundations of the world rest. Though they have thus far stood neglected, they are called "sea" by the Creator of things
<margin>17.</margin> in Genesis. From there, likewise, Ecclesiastes sought the sources and rivers,
<margin>18.</margin> destined to return thither. They flow out from this depth, and for fear of a vacuum, the external sea in turn penetrates the same sand as if by filtering, and it
<margin>19.</margin> soon separates its saltiness within the very first few steps. But because the springs and rivers, in their gradual course, have dispensed the seeds and matter of all minerals (which they previously guarded in their bosom, and which human life can hardly do without), they
<margin>20.</margin> hasten swiftly to the external sea. From there, they return again to the internal sea—the "Night of Orpheus" <note>a reference to the Orphic cosmogony where Night is a primordial source</note>, the "Darkness of Pluto" in Hippocrates, the "Oromasis of the Persians" <note>original: "Oromasim"; referring to Ahura Mazda, the Zoroastrian principle of light and creation</note>, and the <term>Iliadum</term> of Paracelsus <note>a Paracelsian term for the "First Matter" or a spiritual container of life-seeds</note> (where the Reasons and Gifts lie—that is, the mineral seeds not yet joined to bodies). They seek these fertile lodgings again so that the waters may once more be impregnated with seeds. Thus, the descent of waters into the Ocean is not an idle thing.

<column-break/>

Indeed, they are governed by intelligence; and as if they were endowed with intellect, they do not cease to perform their duties—testimonies of infinite Goodness and Providence. Certainly, as many as look upon the <term>Kabbalah</term> <note>the Jewish mystical tradition, often invoked by Renaissance natural philosophers to explain hidden workings of nature</note> will marvel at this, yet it is most true. It is necessary for those who are ignorant of many things to wonder at many things. And yet, it is consistent with what the
<margin>21.</margin> Ocean offers daily before our eyes in its double ebb and flow. I mean the rising "navel of the water," contrary to the laws of hydraulics, and the waves swelling according to the lunar alignment <note>original: "syzygia lunae"; the conjunction or opposition of the moon and sun</note>. For the sea lives, so to speak, by its own right: even when the wind is silent, it stirs up spontaneous tides, carefully observing a position analogous to the moon. Swollen with waves, it goes to meet the moon, and finally, through the variegated change of seasons, light, and motions, and the continuous mass of waters—now here, now elsewhere, through fixed intervals—it raises its overflows on high. Therefore, though you see portents of nature daily in the Ocean, cease to marvel at the vital and spring-like stirrings of the interior, true, and vivid sea—that far narrower abyss—dedicated to human uses.

# SECOND PARADOX.

<margin>1. *No springs from condensed air.* 2. *Elements do not change or perish.* 3. *Whatever is generated, is generated from seed; and whatever happens, happens in nature by the necessity of seed.* 4. *There are only two primitive elements, and two secondary.* 5. *Paradoxical explanation.* 6. *Mechanical proof.* 7. *Heaven and earth shall perish, but not water and air.* 8. *The art of distillation explains Physics.* 9. *What vapor is.* 10. *Proof against Aristotle.* 11. *Second mechanical proof.* 12. *What the "magnale" is, and of what kind.* 13. *Why droplets in vapor and snow do not fall, and when they do fall.* 14. *Proof against Aristotle.* 15. *Proof.* 16. 17. *Mechanics.*</margin>

<margin>1.</margin> **D**ealing with the gushing of springs, their immediate source of generation, and their birth, we have acted more briefly than a paradox requires, yet more tediously (I confess) than the doctrine of the people of Spa <note>original: "Spadanorum"; referring to the famous mineral springs of Spa in modern-day Belgium</note> would demand. It is difficult, indeed,

<column-break/>

to have maintained a middle ground in all things—specifically, regarding how the waters proceed from their most rich diversion to their destinations. Even if, in the meantime, some seek the air as soon as possible, and others occasionally run headlong through long journeys of earth and rocks and tubes before giving themselves to the light: the Reason, necessity, and end of the design was the same in both cases. Namely, the will of Him who created all things for our use. For the rest, it remains to ask for pardon, that the spirits of
<margin>2.</margin> Aristotle might indulge our freedom if I shall judge it a dream, impossible to nature, that springs are born from the condensation of air. For truly, this also is primarily true: that in no ages was air ever water, nor shall it be; just as water never takes the form of air.
