### SECOND PARADOX.

...will take on a form.
<margin>2.</margin> For the elements are the original "mothers" and the constant matrices of things; they have remained stable since the world’s founding and will persist until its end. However, whatever has submitted itself to the cycle of change through the various classes of generation—whether it appears to be earthy, stony, or liquid—all of it derives from the "mass of the three principles" <note>The Paracelsian principles of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury, which were believed to be the building blocks of all matter</note> dedicated to the stage of generation. It does not derive from the primary elements themselves, which enjoy a stable permanence. These primary elements hide their offspring back in their original storehouses until the seeds are ripe for the generation of a new child. These seeds then once again clothe and reassume those same principles of bodies, which have been transformed in the meantime through "digestions" <note>The chemical or natural process of maturing or refining matter</note>.
<margin>3.</margin> For all generation in the universe which is called "spontaneous" occurs from an invisible and bodiless seed that has taken up residence in the matrices of the elements and put on the principles of bodies. Others have called this a "flow from non-being into being" <note>original: "fluxum de nonente ad ens"</note>. To make this clearer, it should be noted that for the production of any thing, only two sexes—or at least one shared sex—must concur.
<margin>4.</margin> Furthermore, by that same law of worldly harmony, there are originally only two elements in the universe: namely, Air and Water. This is sufficiently suggested by the Sacred Text, which speaks of the Spirit floating over the abyss of waters at the world's cradle.
<margin>5.</margin> Earth, therefore, and Fire (or Heaven), if they are elements at all, should only be called "secondary," as they proceed from the first two.
<margin>6.</margin> For whatever exists of earths, stones, gems, sand, and so on, either flows out into a misty "outflow" <note>original: "aporrhœam"</note>, or it is first changed into ash, lime, or (at least by the addition of some other substance) into salt—which is the "offspring of water." Soon after, everything becomes airy and vaporous effluvia when the volatile part overcomes the fixed part, rushing with a hurried force back into water. And so, since everything that is earthy, hard, solid, and compact is reducible to a simpler, thinner, purer, and prior permanent substance (forgive the novelty of this idea, **MOST SERENE PRINCE**), it is

<column-break/>

necessary that it possesses no "elemental energy" at all, but is posterior to Air and Water.
<margin>7.</margin> We say the same regarding Heaven: that the heavens will be changed, grow old, and perish. Thus, heaven and earth will eventually pass away, but you will find no similar news of such destruction regarding Air and Water. Finally, in no age has Air or Water ever been able to be reduced into any prior body by either art or nature. This, then, is the appearance of the elements, this is their destiny, and this is finally their duty, combination, fate, and end: namely, that the unchanged essence and unmixed substance of these two simplest things provide a vital womb or support for seeds and fruits. This continues until the number of generatable things is fulfilled, at which point the mass of principles, along with the seeds, may establish their various families and colonies in a happier seat, in a separate bed.
<margin>8.</margin> Indeed, the mechanical art of Vulcan <note>The "art of Vulcan" refers to alchemy and chemistry, which use fire to transform matter</note> mocks with a laugh the many dreams by which the world has allowed itself to be deceived until now. Who would deny that water is easily changed into vapor? But vapor or breath is so far from being "Air" that it would be easier for the dust of marble or flint to be "Water." As we have shown.
<margin>9.</margin> For in reality, vapor is nothing else, materially and formally, than a collection of atoms of water raised on high. Our school demonstrates this more clearly than the noonday sun.
<margin>10.</margin> But Air, even when caught and compressed in either hot or cold glass vessels, will never yield water, except for the amount of vapor (that is, thinned-out water) it may have contained within itself.
<margin>11.</margin> Water is actually separated into tiny little droplets at the beginning of distillation; these are visible through the glass facing the sun as long as the walls are cold, while it flies out thinned into a breath by the force of the heat.
<margin>12.</margin> And this happens specifically through its own "Magnale" <note>Van Helmont's term for a subtle, ethereal vital spirit or "Gas" that acts as a medium between physical matter and spirit</note>. In mixed things, and even in water itself, this is "Ether"—rarer than air and separable from it. It sustains its own compression and dilation, hovering in the middle between "body" and "non-body," a stranger to its own birthplace...

<margin>16.</margin> Furthermore, even if vapor were air, generated from water through a formal transformation, and then from that same air water were to thicken again: you would now be disagreeing with yourself, as you would be allowing such a frequent and easy return from "privation" to "habit" <note>In Aristotelian logic, the return from a state of lacking a quality (privation) back to possessing it (habit) was considered philosophically problematic in certain transformations</note>. <margin>2.</margin> The closer a thing is to its first and seminal beings, whether in nature or by art, the more powerful, noble, and majestic it is. For this reason, those things that enter the world—being initially free from the dimensions of color, flavor, and even quantity (for exam-
<margin>3.</margin> ple: the same human seed sometimes produces a single fetus and sometimes multiple, determined solely by the simplicity or the number of the places where it is received; thus, in its first moments, it is not yet subject to the rule of numbers and quantities)—it is surely for this reason that on the highest cliffs, far from dross, and among rocks and sand, **acid springs** <note>original: "acidi fontes"; also known as "acidulae," these are mineral-rich springs</note> arise, which are more excellent than all others. They are so named, not because they display a sourness (for they are tasteless), but because, like acids, they are medicinal. They are more noble than ordinary mineral waters because they are more pleasant and potent, embracing the seed of the **hungry salt** <term>sal esurinum: a Paracelsian term for a sharp, "hungry" mineral essence capable of dissolving metals</term>, which is still free from the unfolding of flavors. Indeed, since these springs have struck a friendly covenant with our nature, they are drunk with pleasure by the palates of the drinkers and with the inner favor of the stomach, even in the greatest quantity. By this refreshing of nature, they emulate that **universal medicine** <note>The "panacea" or "Elixir of Life" sought by alchemists</note> by protecting health and propagating the vital powers, much like the **Homer's Moly** <term>Moly Homericum: a mythical magical herb from the Odyssey, used here to represent the pinnacle of medicinal efficacy</term>, appearing to have reached the very summit of medicine. **Paracelsus** <term>Theophrastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a famous physician and alchemist</term>, in his book *On Tartareous Diseases*, believed such a spring to flow in **Valtellina** <note>original: "Veltin"; a valley in the Alps</note> in the Swiss countryside, the likes of which the whole circuit of the world could scarcely contain another in a valley (for on the highest cliffs there are several).
<margin>5.</margin> Indeed, the Danube, the Rhine, the Rhone, the **Saône** <note>original: "Sanus"</note>, the Po, and others, possess such a spring at their
<margin>6.</margin> first source. I will add further: What if a guardian was appointed over the cave of **Gargano** <note>Monte Sant'Angelo sul Gargano, where the Archangel Michael is said to have appeared</note>, the Prince of the heavenly host? It would not be out of place to believe that some **Good Spirit** <note>original: "Eudaemonem"</note> is set over such springs; just as the ancients used to place their demigods at the origin of a river, turning their cups. However it may be, those springs are closest to the **Iliados** <term>Iliados: a Paracelsian term for the first matter of the elements or primordial chaos</term> and are filled with the first being of "hungry" substances. On the

<column-break/>

other hand, there are other springs with which a **petrifying juice** <note>original: "succus petrescens"; a fluid believed to turn objects into stone</note> is mixed. As the water gradually flows down, it sows rocks and flints both on the bottom and on the walls of the channel, and through hidden conduits of the veins, it spreads cliffs along the banks.
<margin>7.</margin> The **Meuse** <term>Mosa: a major European river flowing through France, Belgium, and the Netherlands</term> will serve as an example; for here, from its origin, its banks drink in this stone-making juice far and wide, laying down hills from there all the way to **Visé** <note>original: "Visetum"; a town in Belgium</note>. 
<margin>8.</margin> Once this juice is consumed and has finished its destined path, the Meuse henceforth sees no more cliffs. For it is not a simple stone; rather, it scatters coal in one place, iron mines in another, and even closer, sulfurous **marcasites** <note>Iron pyrite or similar metallic minerals</note> along the course of the banks. Elsewhere it exhibits lead ores, either pure or mixed with others in a "hermaphroditic" origin near the start of the springs. The **Adepts** <term>Adepti: those who have mastered the secrets of alchemy</term> distinguish this distribution of mines through the **Trival line** into their **Peroledo estates** <note>original: "per Trivalem lineam, in suos Peroledorum fundos"; likely technical alchemical or geological terms for specific mineral veins and their locations</note>.
<margin>9.</margin> Furthermore, there has been hesitation as to why they are called "acid springs," and from where that sourness is to be sought. I will speak briefly. For the seeds of all salts, as we have said, are situated in the waters; yet they have not yet taken on a flavor, unless they have found the agreeable principles of bodies and the proper wombs of the earth. For then, and not before, they express a saltiness and put on the garment of salt. Here they burst forth into alum, there into sea salt or spring salt, and elsewhere into nitre, etc.
<margin>10.</margin> Therefore, it should be noted that a certain **hermaphroditic salt of metals** exists, which, for lack of a name, has begun to be called "hungry" or "vinegary" in both reality and name. It is indeed general and adaptable to all metals; so that if one does not wish to think of it as their first and most remote matter, it is at least the **womb** <note>original: "fecundina"; literally "the afterbirth" or "fertile matter"</note> of metals, congenital to any metals whatsoever. This salt, being free from foreign mixture, is acid and pleasing to our body in the proper quantity, because it thoroughly cleanses and consumes all non-vital moisture and **tartar** <term>Tartarum: stony mineral deposits that Paracelsus believed caused diseases like gout and stones in the body</term>. 
<margin>11.</margin> There is truly a twofold excrement in us. One is our own, which [leads] to putrefaction and...

### THIRD PARADOX.
# 692

<margin>10.</margin> ...is subject to stench: but there is another class of things, which a traitor completes his tragedy with a hostile coagulation, and is called by the general etymology, **tartar** <note>original: "tartarum"; refers to stony precipitates or deposits found in wine or the body</note>. Thus **acetous salt** <note>original: "sal acetosum"; a sharp, vinegar-like salt</note>, like an embryo, is considered in the order of
<margin>11.</margin> metals: not infrequently also as a solitary individual, but not yet
<margin>12.</margin> completed in its destination. I shall explain the matter by the example of **vitriol** <term>vitriol: also known as chalcantum, these are metallic sulfate crystals (like copper sulfate) highly valued by alchemists for their transformative properties</term>. For the best artificial vitriol for medicine is made from copper, in imitation of nature: it is therefore by far the best when it is forged from copper alone, without earthy filth or the mixture of foreign materials—which, however, are not unable to flow together in the wombs of nature. It is made in this way: Sulfur is cast upon melted copper until the flame has consumed it all; then immediately the molten copper is poured into rainwater, from which it turns green. This is repeated until all the copper has migrated into the water. Finally, once the water has evaporated, you have vitriol. For what was previously copper has now additionally acquired a salt from the sulfur.
<margin>13.</margin> Secondly, the most excellent vitriol grows naturally in mines where nature has brought forth that **hungry salt** <term>sal esurinum: a sharp, "hungry" mineral spirit capable of "eating" or dissolving metals</term>, corroding a fertile vein of copper, and dissolved by the liquor of a licking spring, which they later boil in vats into vitriol. The Cyprian, Hungarian, and Roman varieties are praised, and generally any which contributes the most copper in its examination.
<margin>14.</margin> But that vitriolic juice was thought to change iron into copper—the miners barely recognizing the delusion: namely, that as it consumes the place of the iron, the succeeding atoms of copper fill it. Nor did they notice that just as copper makes dissolved silver (otherwise invisible in **parting-acid** <note>original: "chrysulca"; a strong acid used to separate gold and silver</note>) visible and corporeal, so it is the property of iron to manifest the copper dissolved in vitriol by seizing it to itself, while simultaneously by that same act, the iron itself is dissolved and vanishes into the spring. Let the springs be my witnesses. Indeed, vitriolated waters become much poorer in copper themselves after the iron has received the benefit of the recovered copper.

<column-break/>

For that reason, clearly, outside the spring (where and whenever a continuous flow of new copper from the depths is lacking), the otherwise deceptive **transmutation** <note>The author is explaining a chemical displacement reaction, where copper replaces iron, which 17th-century observers often mistook for the literal alchemical transformation of one metal into another</note> of iron does not occur.
<margin>15.</margin> Thirdly and finally, vitriol is made by art from **pyrite** or **brassy marcasite** <note>pyrite and marcasite are iron sulfide minerals often called "fool's gold"</note> impregnated with sulfur. Indeed, once the sulfur is abstracted from it, the remaining brassy body is exposed to the air; over a number of days, it gradually resolves its marrow into an acid salt, which by that same sharpness of resolution dissolves something of the brass into itself; and from there, drawn out with the help of water and soon boiled, it becomes vitriol. And so, whatever resisted the gnawing of the hungry salt the first time, after repeated burning of sulfur, finally yields entirely and turns into vitriol. 
<margin>16.</margin> Fourthly, finally, the hungry salt is born together, congealed in the pyrite, which by burning and resolution carries something of the brass away with it and becomes vitriol. From which it becomes manifest:
<margin>17.</margin> First, that hungry salt, although acid, differs greatly from any other acidity—as much as vitriol differs from **verdigris** <note>original: "aerugo"; the green pigment or rust formed on copper by vinegar</note>, which is made by the vapor of vinegar, and thus by the salt of vinegar conceived within.
<margin>18.</margin> Secondly, that although sulfur is entirely fatty and **combustible** <note>original: φλογιστὸν (phlogiston); the ancient Greek term for the principle of inflammability</note>, it nevertheless leaves behind a certain semi-fixed acid salt during the penetration of copper (which otherwise flies away during burning and is collected into a juice by a bell-shaped vessel).
<margin>19.</margin> Thirdly, the acid salt and hungry salt of springs, having arisen in the bowels of the earth, is the embryonic salt of some sulfur: 
<margin>20.</margin> yet it is more noble than the artificial salt sought from sulfur, because it is closer to the **prime matter** <note>original: "primo enti"; the "first being" or fundamental essence of a substance</note> and to the seeds of the **Iliadus** <term>Iliadus: a Paracelsian term for the first matter of the universe or the "inner sun" of a substance</term>. As is read above. Therefore, you will recognize that those who estimate the virtues of the **waters of Spa** <note>original: "Spadanorum"; referring to the famous mineral springs in Spa, Belgium</note> from the properties of the contained minerals (as if they had already progressed into their final matter) wander far from the truth. For it is evident from the above that the hungry salts of sulfur differ very widely from the property of sulfur; indeed, that...

### FOURTH PARADOX.
# 693

What is more, the artificial **hungry salt of sulfur** <note>original: "sal esurinum sulfuris"; an acidic, reactive mineral essence</note> is as far removed from the natural variety as this **embryonated** <note>meaning in its early, unrefined mineral state</note> form is closer to its root in the first seeds. They are, I say, completely mistaken who compare the hungry salts of lead with lead itself, from which it is immensely distinct. For there is a very foreign similarity between the perfect salts—such as **alum** <note>a mineral salt used as an astringent</note>, **nitre** <note>saltpeter</note>, and **vitriol** <term>vitriol: metallic sulfate crystals</term>—and those same salts when they are not yet perfected. This is clear by example: for the hungry salt of alum is sweeter than any sugar (it is called the **manna of alum**) and knows no astringency, being similar to its **first being** <note>the pure, essential state of a substance before it takes physical form</note>.

<margin>22.</margin> Fourthly: Since therefore the most excellent

<column-break/>

**vitriol** is materially nothing other than the hungry salt of **embryonated sulfur** which has eroded some part of copper, whereas the salt of cheaper vitriol is drawn from perfected sulfur; led by the analogy of things, we have therefore adopted the same name for vitriol for all similar dissolutions of metals. I find this has not yet been noted by others writing about the waters of **Spa** <note>original: "de Spadanis"; referring to the famous mineral springs in Belgium</note>. For indeed, <margin>23.</margin> in the progress of both art and nature, vitriol (except for gold) is made daily from any metal. Specifically, insofar as from a metal and the marriage of a certain hungry salt, a metallic liquor—I mean a **coagulable vitriol**—is produced.

### FOURTH PARADOX.
# 694

**vitriol** <note>original: "chalcantum"; also known as copperas</note> of a most acidic taste. Elsewhere, following **Dioscorides** <note>a 1st-century Greek physician and pharmacologist</note>, they find more of an unpleasant and earthy astringency in vitriol than acidity. Finally, just as the most acidic **oil of vitriol** is drawn out only by the extreme torture of fire (specifically, from a hungry and sulfurous salt, lifting up the airy spirits), they believe the springs become acidic from this and no other way: namely, that a heat of this kind in the earth stirs up the acidic spirits of vitriol toward the surface of the earth, which, being compressed there by the cold and changed into an acid, are mixed with a nearby spring. This position is accompanied by many anxieties. 

<margin>2.</margin> First, because there is no such **spontaneous distillation** in the Universe. Secondly, because the interior parts of the earth are cold in summer, according to **Hippocrates** <note>the ancient Greek physician</note>, which is precisely when the **Spa waters** <note>original: "Spadana"</note> are at their best. Thirdly, because the spirit of vitriol cannot help but erode the earth or rocks it touches, and therefore would cast off all its acidity, making its dedication to the springs in vain. Fourthly, because in summer, the cold of the earth is not only on the surface—which would be for condensing spirits more than the interior parts—from which they imagine the spirits are driven away by the force of heat. Fifthly, because the spirits of vitriol, when mixed with water (even if carelessly observed), neither lose their acidity nor are they stained with a reddish color: yet this is entirely common to spring waters. Thus far the opinion of others has led me astray. I will confess my own blindness. 

<margin>3.</margin> *I once seriously distilled the **Savinière** and **Pouhon** springs:* <note>original: "Savenirium, & Pouhontium"; two famous mineral springs at Spa, Belgium</note> *and indeed, I found in them not just a catalog of minerals—no, I found nothing at all in them except spring water and **vitriol of iron**, which had been neglected by other writers before me.* 

It is well known that the vitriol of Mars <term>vitriol of Mars: iron sulfate crystals</term> is made from a hungry salt of **embryonated sulfur** <note>sulfur in its early, unrefined mineral state</note> and a **vein of iron** <note>iron ore</note> (not the metal iron itself), which the hungry salt, while still volatile, has eroded by "licking" it. <margin>4.</margin> In this act of erosion, a certain dissolution of the vein itself occurs, along with a coagulation or fixation of the volatile salt. The salt, I say, as long as it is volatile—that is, suited to fly away when pressed by fire—is counted among the **spirits**. <margin>5.</margin> But bodies do not erode bodies insofar as they are 

<column-break/>

such, nor do fixed things act upon each other: but only insofar as one of them is volatile, that is, a spirit, whether it be solid or liquid. Finally, in every solution <margin>6.</margin> (as can be seen in the activity of **aqua fortis** <note>nitric acid</note>, distilled vinegar, etc.), certain exhalations are excited which were previously quiet; these, like **wild spirits** <note>original: "sylvestres"; Helmont's term for 'gas'</note>, do not obey coagulation again, and therefore necessarily fly out of the water or break the vessels if they are confined. 

Furthermore, <margin>7.</margin> this is also notable: that as much of the spirits as completed the dissolution of the body, just as much has also assumed "corporality" within the dissolved body. From this, the reason is clear why the **Spa waters**, in such great clarity, hide the opaque body of the iron vein within themselves. Finally, why, in the activity <margin>8.</margin> of the hungry salt, they smell of sulfur, even though corporal sulfur is absent. At last, <margin>9.</margin> it is also obvious why toward the end of their activity (for that festive state of dissolution lasts for more or less time in different springs), the waters lose their acidity, and the vein, previously transparent, then appears reddish. <margin>10.</margin> For when the spirits have now partly been driven away, or when they have been weakened and coagulated at the end of their activity, the absorbed vein settles and is made manifest, which had previously stood hidden: while the waters, in the meantime, recover their original simplicity. 

Furthermore, it is not without reason that I denied that iron <margin>11.</margin> or iron filings are in the Spa waters, but rather the **iron vein**. For in the vein, more virtue occurs than in the iron—specifically those subtle parts which the furnace stole away during smelting. Therefore, the juice, spirit, <margin>12.</margin> or **hungry salt** (call it what you will) does not grow inside the iron vein so that there is an equal melting of both in the waters; far from it—the salt has found other wombs in the earth, from which the passing wave dissolves it and carries it away like a close kinsman, the former son of another wave. If, therefore, it is held for a longer time in a significant cavity around <margin>13.</margin> the vein, it absorbs more of the vein into itself, as the **Pouhon** spring does, and this even more so...

...more so than the Geronster spring. The **Tonnelet**, however, is richer in **hungry salt** <note>original: "sale esurino"; van Helmont’s term for a sharp, acidic mineral solvent</note> than the previous two, yet it is poorer in the **vein of iron** <note>iron ore</note>. For this reason, it is colder and more troublesome to the stomach. Therefore, whichever spring moves the bowels more effectively is richer in the vein of iron. Indeed, this was not unknown to the Ancients, who used **iron scales** <margin>14.</margin> to clear the belly. Young women, too, when taking **stomoma** <note>original: "stomoma"; a term for steel or the "edge" of iron</note> or iron-water, are also accustomed to vomit in the first few days. <column-break/>

and the vein more quickly, and the medicinal wave dies out sooner. For this same reason, it passes through the stomach most easily, is digested, and penetrates more quickly. Therefore, the presence of the <margin>16.</margin> **acting spirits** within the vein dilates the pores in the water and makes the spring water lighter in the balance. Furthermore, it should be noted that just as a fermenting boiling occurs in wines and **verjuice** <note>original: "omphacio"; juice of unripened grapes</note>, so does the action of the hungry salt occur. And it does not only act upon the <margin>17.</margin> vein while it gnaws and permeates it, but it also operates for a time upon that same vein once it has been carried away with it. The **Pouhon** <note>original: "Pouhontius"</note>, I say, acts far longer than the Sauvenière, etc., until the activities of the spirits are exhausted, and both the agent and the patient—the dissolver, I say, as well as the dissolvable—faint away by the same process.

Therefore, the Spa waters, when drunk, are suitable for absolutely all diseases that arise from the enemy **tartar** <note>original: "tartaro"; internal stony or crusty deposits believed to cause disease</note>, which has been received and coagulated within against nature—provided that the **root of life** remains sufficient, that is, if they are drunk early enough. On account of which, <margin>4.</margin> for those affections that are genuine **idiopathies** <note>diseases arising from the organ itself, not from a secondary cause</note> of those parts, the Spa waters only help "by accident" <note>indirectly</note>. The reason is this: since they are mineral, they are entirely unfit for nourishment; they are banished from the body in the urine along with the final excrement of the salts, the commerce of which...

### FIFTH PARADOX.

...the more vigorous blood does not allow it any further. Therefore, if they [the waters] seem to bring any relief to the head, heart, or lungs, it must be thought that this happens entirely by removing the underlying condition, which had caused a **dyscrasia** <note>an imbalance of the bodily fluids or "humors"</note> in those parts through **deuteropathy** <note>original: "deuteropathiam"; a secondary disease or symptom caused by an original ailment elsewhere</note> and **sympathy** <note>the medical concept of "consensus," where one organ affects another through a shared connection</note>. Furthermore, the Spa waters are not much help in epidemic, endemic, or **astral diseases** <note>illnesses believed to be caused by the influence of the stars or heavens</note>, such as the Plague, pleurisy, **prunella** <note>a feverish throat infection, often called "the sloe"</note>, and so on; nor do they contribute much to cases involving poison, whether swallowed, generated within, or shared by contagion. They are also ineffective in "tincture" diseases, such as leprosy, the **Venereal pox** <note>syphilis</note>, morphea <note>a skin condition causing localized hardening</note>, cancer, epilepsy, and the like. Therefore, we do not agree with those who recommend the Spa waters for every single disease without distinction. They even extol them to the point of blasphemy. They say, for instance: *“There is no reason to be amazed by the ancient miracles of waters—the pool of Siloam or the Jordan healing Naaman—now that we have the Spa; for here we see those suffering from the 'astonished disease' <note>original: "attonito morbo"; a term for apoplexy or sudden seizure</note>, convulsions, paralysis, and even lepers being cured.”* 

<margin>5.</margin> Away with this! Miracles are the work of an inimitable Finger <note>referring to the "Finger of God"</note>; moreover, one must properly distinguish between **accidental effects** and those caused directly by a thing’s own nature. For example, if a young woman suffers from suffocation, epilepsy, or a paralytic condition due to a **stoppage of her menses**, and then, after drinking the Spa water, her menses return and she is freed from the related illness, there is no reason to claim that apoplexy, asthma, epilepsy, or true paralysis should be treated by the Spa springs. 

<margin>6.</margin> For diseases arising from the womb belong to an entirely different **monarchy** <note>a Paracelsian term meaning a distinct category or realm of disease governance</note> and grow from a different root than those which erupt from the general condition of the **microcosm** <note>the human body viewed as a miniature version of the universe</note>, in both men and women. If someone does not distinguish between these, they will be laughed at by more discerning people. 

<margin>7.</margin> We have already discussed how much the **hungry salt** <note>original: "sal esurinum"; van Helmont’s term for a sharp, acidic mineral solvent</note> achieves in the springs; now we must speak of what the corroded and dissolved **ore of iron** does. It clearly acts as an **astringent** <note>something that shrinks or constricts tissues</note> first and foremost, and therefore strengthens the stomach and all neighboring parts. 

<column-break/>

Therefore, the Spa waters are suitable for "loose" and "dissolved" diseases, such as **lientery** <note>a type of diarrhea where food passes undigested</note>, diarrhea, **celiac flux**, dysentery, and so on. 

<margin>8.</margin> I expect people to object that since anything containing iron is said to provoke menses and clear blockages of the liver and spleen, it would be more logical to say that the Spa waters **open** <note>clear blockages in the vessels</note> rather than constrict. 

<margin>9.</margin> I respond according to the **Adepts** <note>alchemical philosophers or masters of medicine</note>. Within us, there often wanders a certain dissolved mineral salt, which is purely waste matter—I call it **resolved tartar** <note>solid, stony deposits formed from metabolic waste or undigested matter</note>—existing either in its first or final state. Whether its "mine" is the womb, liver, spleen, kidneys, pancreas, mesentery, or stomach, we judge the same: so long as it is clear that it causes great distress to the sufferer. When **stomoma** <note>original: "stomate"; steel or processed iron</note>, that is, steel or iron in powder form, is swallowed, that harmful salt (which does not obey the commands of laxatives) rushes headlong to the iron and clings to it in order to dissolve it and exert its power; thus it coagulates around it and leaves the body along with the iron. But if the iron or "edge" <note>steel</note> is drunk already dissolved in a sharp liquid that is not hostile to us (like the Spa waters), then nature, once these liquids are consumed and admitted deep inside, soon separates the iron (as it is unfit for nourishment) from the mixture and sends it out through the intestines. This can be seen in the **blackness of the stools** after drinking Spa water. 

<margin>11.</margin> In this separation of the iron, there is an immediate, spontaneous gathering of mineral salts, just as when copper is added to **chrysulca** <note>original: "chrysulca"; literally "gold-washer," a term for nitric acid or a strong solvent</note> containing silver, and the dissolved copper flies to the iron. Thus, the swallowed iron frees the body from obstruction and "opens" it **accidentally**—that is, by carrying the defeated obstructing matter away with it. This does not mean, however, that the iron ceases to be **constrictive** in its own nature. 

<margin>12.</margin> It "opens," I say, by a **specific and appropriated power**, but it "constricts" by a **secondary quality**. Furthermore, since it has increased the spirit and hope of the miserable, especially...

### FIRST PARADOX <note>Continued from previous page.</note>

<margin>13.</margin> Regarding those suffering from **calculi** <term>kidney or bladder stones</term>, I shall give my judgment on the drinking of the water. It is certain that the Spa waters flush the urinary region, both because they pass through easily and because they are drunk in great abundance. Being mineral-rich, their **hungry salt** <term>original: "sal esurinum"; a sharp, acidic salt believed by Helmont to have transformative chemical powers</term> prevents the **spirit of urine** (the sole architect of stones) from petrifying anything by its own innate property. Indeed, another more powerful salt brings that spirit under its own control, as if it were bound.

<margin>14.</margin> However, because this is merely a palliative care—even if existing stones and sand are expelled as if by the scouring of flowing water—it only prevents
<margin>15.</margin> new gatherings of stones for as long as the water is being drunk. If the stones grow back soon after, we consider these remedies unreliable for those with the stone. In fact, a stone hastens to grow all the more readily when that "womb"—the other parent of the stone—has been made cleaner. For will not urine more easily glue a stone to a clean chamber pot than to one smeared with oil? This is perhaps why the kidneys of many beasts
<margin>16.</margin> abound in fat. We know, therefore, that the perfect cure for the stone and the long-awaited relief is something else entirely: a process in which smaller stones are gently driven out (which is the least of it), while larger ones return to their original liquid state through a backward **analysis** <note>a chemical breaking down</note> of their solid form. Yet even that would not be enough unless the **petrifying inclination** <note>the body's tendency to create stones</note> is removed. By harvesting a few specific remedies that restore the body, anyone can hope for total health—longed for no less than after a fever. We have written of these elsewhere and provided the remedies. For the power of healing stands upright under any weight; that is, all diseases are of equal value to it, and its power cannot be diminished by any ailment. What is lacking are only the nobler powers of

<column-break/>

remedies, which cry out to the Creator in heaven that they have come in vain, as there is almost no one to release their bonds. But one must soon refrain from complaints in this "ulcerous" age.

<margin>17.</margin> Therefore, as far as the **primary qualities** <note>the traditional Aristotelian qualities: Hot, Cold, Moist, Dry</note> of the Spa waters are concerned: although we are very little concerned with them (since they are fleeting and lack a vital anatomy), so long as they are not infamously harmful, we judge the **hungry salt** to be in the first degree of heat and dryness. However, the dissolved vein of iron we judge to have reached the second degree of coldness and dryness.

<margin>18.</margin> As for the water itself, we follow the indulgence of Aristotle in deeming it supremely moist but only mildly cold, as was shown in the deductions above. But because those qualities—of the water as well as the minerals—are **relative** <unclear>relolleae</unclear>,

<margin>19.</margin> they possess no power of healing. Instead, they arrive at the established condition of the body inappropriately, like mere colors. Therefore, we leave the speculation of such things to others, contenting ourselves with the mastery of the **cherionic quality** <term>original: "qualitatis cherioniae"; a term used to describe a potent, penetrating, or "surgical" healing property that can manage difficult or "ulcerous" conditions</term>.

<margin>20.</margin> Finally, an objection must be answered: Why is the Tonnelet spring, despite its abundance of hungry and hot salt, said to be colder and more troublesome to the stomach? I shall satisfy this.

<margin>21.</margin> Even if the **hungry salt** is hot in its primary qualities, it acts just like oil of vitriol, sulfur, or *aqua fortis* <note>nitric acid</note>: it nevertheless chills the body through its third and proper **cherionic** quality. Specifically, it weakens our natural heat through its excess; most importantly, its acidity dissolves the "secondary humor" (the immediate nourishment of the stomach) and makes it unfit for feeding. It is no wonder if the stomach, lacking this vital liquid, suffers in its own inherent and borrowed heat.

### THE SIXTH PARADOX

<margin>1.</margin> Regarding the **diet** and the manner of using the **Spa waters**, I will now subjoin a few points. In the study of diet, with experience as my guide, we have established this above all: the quality of foods, as such, never brings harm unless a weak <margin>2.</margin> and defective remedy is present. (For God saw that everything He had made was good, and consequently, everything He ordained as food is good food); only the **quantity**, however, can be harmful. For eat whatever foods you wish—for instance, even if you are wounded—as long as you do not exceed the proper amount and you have suitable balms and wound-healing potions, you will feel no pressure from the foods and no harm, just as if you were nourished by the most delicate selection of foods. <margin>3.</margin> Soldiers and the poor will testify to this: the Judge of things would have seemed harsh to them if they were required to eat pheasants, partridges, and other culinary trickery <note>original: "mangonio"; refers to the "doctoring" or deceptive preparation of food</note> while sick. Nature scorns the rules of fussy curiosity, protected by that aid which would look in vain for help and defense against disease from a remedy that is unable to satisfy the prevention of defects caused by even a small quantity of food. For whatever is meant to engage in single combat with a disease must, by an even greater right, turn away symptoms arising from food; I mean that which is offered or established to ward off injuries. <margin>4.</margin> Therefore, the necessity of a strict diet is believed to have been introduced by a lack of higher medicines, not by the allure of the foods themselves. <margin>5.</margin> I advise the one drinking the Spa waters to observe this one precept of diet: strive for sobriety, and eat <margin>6.</margin> sparingly like the local inhabitants. For what benefit would there be in praising the health of the locals from the Spa waters if we ourselves live more sumptuously and too luxuriously? Therefore, let the supreme defense of a long life be **sobriety** (even if it seems cruel to those unaccustomed to it). Things that taste good in other circumstances nourish best. And a hungry person will easily digest those things which <margin>7.</margin> taste the best. By this rule of diet alone, the waters will pass through safely,

quickly, and pleasantly. Likewise, the Pouhon water, in a moderate quantity, will intentionally open the urinary passages <note>original: "vimarios meatus"; likely a reference to the branching vessels</note> beforehand. The quantity should be increased daily, up to the point of tolerance, so that each person may be his own judge. This will be easily determined from there. Otherwise, the delay makes the natural heat vanish and the action is frustrated. <margin>12.</margin> Returning to the village from the spring, let him walk slowly so that not sweat, but **urine** (which is desired), is provoked. <margin>13.</margin> Let the hour of lunch be when the stomach has been cleared of the waters, lest the residue of the water, nearly "processed," prematurely carry raw juice into the veins. <margin>14.</margin> Whether the Spa water mixed with pure wine is appropriate has been doubted. **Q**uince the monster of **lithiasis** <note>the formation of stones in the body</note> is so frequent in man, and calls so many to the **Springs of Spa** <note>Spadacrenas</note> with the hope of a perfect cure, it will certainly help to explain this paragraph more liberally, lest brevity breed obscurity. We must therefore discuss what the Ancients, and what the more modern disciples of the **Hermetic school** <note>followers of chemical medicine and alchemy</note>, think about the origin and cure of stones.

<margin>1.</margin> First, they blamed the material of the stone on phlegm, **pituitary** <note>mucus</note>, and mucilage—or human excrement. But for the **efficient cause** <note>the active force that creates the thing</note>, they blamed actual heat, and heat that is excessive in the organ.

<margin>2.</margin> Why not? they say, since from a kidney afflicted by stones much sediment is stirred up, and from a bladder beset by stones, a continuous mucus is driven out headlong? ...where it is not properly separated in the vessels dedicated to excreting waste, it creeps inside, mixed with the genial and vital juices. <margin>16.</margin> All of this will be made clear by a single, common example. It is obvious that every one of us, even when in the best of health, passes healthy, golden, clear urine, free of sediment or mucus. If this is kept for several hours, even in a clear glass vessel,

Those who claim the stone arises from muddy or mucous phlegm are mistaken; because they cannot see the juice equipped with stone-forming power in clear and transparent waters, they remain ignorant. Truly, such a view is no wiser than the knowledge of a common peasant. 

<margin>22.</margin> Therefore, we must turn to **Analysis by Fire** <term>Analysis by Fire</term><note>An early chemical method using distillation or heat to break a substance down into its fundamental components to reveal its true nature.</note>, which places the release of bodies and their certain composition before our eyes. # SUPPLEMENTS
## ON THE CAUSES OF STONES

<margin>25.</margin> ...though it is quite readily expedited, yet sticking bit by bit like a small stone to the vertebrae <note>original: "spondylibus"</note>. To recognize such a material cause is hindered by the identical nature of tartars in the macrocosm <note>the universe or external world</note>, as well as the similar offspring of stones. <margin>26.</margin> But what if we say that heat does not dry out the mucus while it fashions the stone, but rather compels or coagulates it? Not indeed by a drying property, but by a heating one, or *concoction* <note>original: "pepasmo," a Greek medical term for the "ripening" of humors</note>. By the command of this alone, the restrained matter might put on the power of an internal coagulant, stirred up through heat. <margin>27.</margin> And yet, this is to say something in our favor, and is granted to us of its own accord. Specifically, to recognize in the matter a property assigned to coagulation, whether it was meanwhile viscous or clear and transparent. <margin>28.</margin> Otherwise, indeed, gemstones would protest, as they did not require the viscosity of matter to assume such strength and brilliance. <margin>29.</margin> However, you will not escape the reefs <note>difficulties in the argument</note> on that account. For indeed, no actual heat congealed the stone in the *chamber pot* <note>original: "matula"</note>; rather, it happened long after the *urine* <note>original: "lotium"</note> had grown cold. Finally, since in a stone of the bladder, the hateful sensation of heat is absent—even where the stone is generally harder than in the kidneys—it follows entirely that the necessary efficient cause of the stone is not heat. <margin>30.</margin> Or otherwise, a more powerful heat would preside over the manufacture of the stone in the bladder. Therefore, the studies of more modern thinkers decree that heat in the kidneys is by no means the parent of stones, but a symptom—an effect following the positioning of the hateful guest, the stone, within the organ. <margin>31.</margin> Just as a thorn <note>original: "spina"</note> fixed in a finger is neither hot, nor hardened by heat, nor thrust into the flesh because of heat, yet heat follows the injury as a companion: so too, one must seriously observe that heat supervenes upon the injury of the organ caused and continuously fostered by the existing stone. For where there is pain, there is the disease according to Hippocrates, and heat flows thither as something that comes after. <margin>32.</margin> Moreover, that which happens in the injured tissue of the kidney does not likewise occur in the bladder, which behaves like a receptacle and a sewer for the urine, which merely glides through the kidney without delay.

<column-break/>

If, however, both the <margin>33.</margin> kidneys and the bladder, each according to its own nature, should excrete something mucus-like when a stone is present, cease to wonder. For the part besieged by the enemy, depressed in its vegetative power, continuously loses some of its own nourishment and, as it were, "weeps" its alimentary fluid (just like an eye besieged by hostile dust). <margin>34.</margin> For individual parts within us feel what is agreeable and what is hateful and execrable, and they express no obscure signs of that sensation everywhere. Otherwise, indeed, once a bladder stone was cut out, the continuous flow of mucus would not yet cease—if, that is, the mucus were the cause, rather than the effect, of the stones. <margin>35.</margin> Regarding the cure, however, it must be diligently noted that it has necessarily been incomplete until now among those to whom the true causes of the stone were not known: if, naturally, the morbid disposition ought to depart only upon the removal of the causes, and not otherwise. <margin>36.</margin> I admit, first of all, that intestines emptied by enemas <note>original: "enematibus"</note>, which press upon the ureters, will provide an altogether easier exit for a stone about to emerge. Similarly, I promise that poultices, ointments, and baths will be very beneficial. For just as our body is a single unit in the consensus of all its parts, so according to Hippocrates: *it is a whole that breathes together and breathes out, both inside and out. Likewise, inside and out, above and below, day and night, fire and water, they make three circuits within us, and thus permeate here and there, and vice versa.* <margin>37.</margin> But in truth, these exterior aids are not direct <note>original: "perpendicularia"</note>; they are only oblique <note>indirect</note> supports. <margin>38.</margin> Finally, since nothing touches the stone directly except that which laps the kidney by way of the urine, it is certain that moistening, viscous, and mucilaginous things (such as *mallow, marshmallow, psyllium,* etc.) have stripped off those bodily qualities in the first workshops of digestion; they are clearly unsuited to urinary qualities. <margin>39.</margin> In the meantime, we concede they help stone-sufferers insofar as they soothe and temper the sharpness of the urine with a sweeter juice; or, having driven out the mucus of the former life deep in the root, they preserve something cleansing or dissolving <margin>40.</margin> (which alone we admit as an *aperient* <term>aperitivum</term><note>A medicine used to "open" the body's channels or bowels.</note>), which is effective for use...

He also discusses the role of mucus as an effect of the stone's presence and evaluates various treatments like enemas and herbal poultices.</summary>

# A NUMEROCRITICAL PARADOX.

...as follows. Just as in the juice of lemons, quinces, chickpeas, pellitory-of-the-wall, etc. But surely, on both sides, the power of these things is only weak and lazy against such a great enemy. <margin>41.</margin> Finally, we do not sufficiently understand what is promised. In what way could almond oil be able to enlarge or distend the ureters <note>The tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder.</note>, when hardly a drop of it ever reaches the ureters—and then only through an error of the secretory system? This is the reality. Indeed, the ureters consist of a moist membrane, which nothing enters deeply except that which is its own nourishment. Thus, even if the oil flowed there in its entirety, it would not perform on a living membrane what it otherwise does on dry and dead parchment. It is far from the case that the ureters, already occupied and moistened by their own nourishment and urine, would take up something oily. For the combination of oil with water is not easy, and the too-rapid passage of the oil would happen too slowly for the dilation of the ureters. Therefore, let us dismiss these dreams. Indeed, the ureters are never enlarged or distended except by a thicker mass of the body <note>meaning the physical presence of a stone</note>; it was not the task of oil or liquid. Clearly, the ureter is naturally loose and soft, and being content with its own urine, it further <margin>42.</margin> rejects other liquids. Therefore, it is dilated only by a stone—that is, by a morbid cause—and once enlarged, it does not collapse again. As can be seen, stones that have grown gradually are more easily expelled <margin>43.</margin> than those that were previously very small. But they will say that the wretched are sometimes helped after drinking relaxants—that is, things that distend the ureters—and therefore, <margin>44.</margin> dilations of the ureters do happen. I hope that anyone who thinks facts in Philosophy should be noted based on the outcome is without success; Philosophy is not accustomed to attributing effects to accidental causes. For perhaps some sweeter liquid has influenced the urine and, by its mixture, rendered it more diluted; these things will indeed be a delight and a solace in suppressing the ferocity of the symptoms. But it is not permitted to infer from this that, by drinking a sweeter juice, the stomach, veins, or ureters have either been enlarged or at least made more <margin>45.</margin> fit for enlargement. For if anything drunk were to render the ureters more widely distensible, it would surely dissolve and enlarge the stomach,

<column-break/>

because the stomach, assigned to sustaining a greater weight of food, would suffer extension in every direction. This would be even more true because, during the precipice of an impending stone, much vomiting excessively plagues the stomach and therefore pulls it apart even to the point of tearing. Hitherto, nothing of remedies has been heard of in such great calamity. Therefore, approaching more closely to a judgment of those things which, by a slight wiping away or even by some specific property, have hitherto seemed to exterminate the stone: we shall speak frankly, with your permission. <margin>46.</margin> For although powders of herbs, seeds, fruits, liquids, and waters, as well as stones and fossils, may have finally brought out the stone and sand once the cruelty of the symptoms was soothed: what, I ask, was achieved there more narrowly than to have cured the present paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or violent expression of a disease.</note>? Surely we have done nothing different than one who has soothed an epileptic fit. We have, I say, merely plucked a single fruit of the disease on both sides, while the tree remains untouched by the axe and the root remains safe. Therefore, whatever things we especially hope will benefit those suffering from stones, we shall teach in two chapters. <margin>47.</margin> The first: That the goal should not be the expulsion of the stone (for something less cruel befits a Physician than that which nature herself, almost fainting under the weight and driven by the rack <note>original: "equuleo," a Roman torture device</note> of symptoms, busies herself with spontaneously), but rather a unique resolution. By "resolution," I mean that once the barriers of the coagulum are dissolved, the stone must be reduced into liquid by a backward conversion—namely, into the matter from which it grew through *synthesis* <note>the process of putting together</note>, it must be reduced through *analysis* <note>the process of breaking down</note>. Let the second be even more noble: That the petrifying inclination <note>the body's tendency to turn fluids into stone</note> be removed. For while this still persists, nothing worthy of thanks has been achieved. <margin>48.</margin> Indeed, it is established by the aforementioned example of urine that every human being has a "potential stone" in their urine (for the fate of the microcosm <note>the human body viewed as a miniature version of the universe</note> required this, if it were to express a greater reality in every way); but only that man is wretched whose latent power of petrifying in the urine is unfolded into action within his own skin. <margin>49.</margin> Therefore, it is absolutely necessary that in the powers of that wretched man's things, some impression—the seal-mark of the Gorgon <note>A reference to Medusa, whose gaze turned men to stone; here used as a metaphor for the "petrifying power" within the body</note>, I say—must be present...

He proposes that true healing requires "resolving" the stone back into liquid and removing the internal "Gorgon's seal" or petrifying tendency of the body.</summary>

# SUPPLEMENT TO THE NUMEROCRITICAL PARADOX.

...to be present, by reason of which these very powers—too exactly, exquisitely, hesitantly, and scrutinizingly—apply themselves to the secretion and examination of the urine <note>original: *lotii*, referring here to the "wash" or liquid waste of the body</note>. It is from this, then, in that internal workshop, that there occurs the activation of <margin>50.</margin> **tartar** <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "tartar" refers to the stony sediment or metabolic waste that precipitates within the body to form stones or gouty deposits.</note>, which previously moved like a watery substance throughout the whole urine. But since these "sealing marks" and the impressions of diseases belong not to the species but only to individuals, we must by no means despair; for when a stronger and more benign impression is brought in, the occupying tyranny may yield its lodging as if defeated. Therefore, the inclination toward the **stone** <note>original: *calculum*</note> will be entirely removed if that power itself no longer pours in the actual secretion of tartar from the urine.

<margin>51.</margin> That secretory force, which is far too exquisite, must therefore be put to sleep. And this should in no way be done by inducing the sluggishness, negligence, and rest of an opium-induced stupor or similar narcotics. <margin>52.</margin> Far from it. Rather, the power lies in a **planetary remedy**, possessing the specific property of **chaste Venus** <note>In alchemy, Venus represents copper. A "remedy of Venus" usually implies a preparation involving copper, believed to have specific effects on the kidneys and reproductive system.</note>, which so restrains the entire elaboration of urine in the kidneys that thereafter, the kidneys—occupied by a sweet leisure as if by sleep—remain at rest, indulging only in their own nourishment. This "golden peace" within us is like that in Politics, which commands each person to attend only to their own duties, and not to be intent on the affairs of others, so that peace may be achieved. It should be noted here: this is an action not of bodies, but of powers upon powers, and a permanent operation, if the victor so overcomes the vanquished that the latter thereafter surrenders itself to the victor’s army. Under this side-point, it is obvious enough that the highest "essences" <note>original: *crases*, referring to the constitutional temperament or mixture</note> of medicines reside only in the most purified liquids, since the "seminal" and primary constituent parts have no commerce at all with the thicker framework of physical bodies. Furthermore, to attain that longed-for peace in the kidneys, we have so far successfully used and possessed the <margin>53.</margin> medicine ***Aroph*** <note>Aroph (Aroma Philosophorum) is a term used by Paracelsus for a specific preparation, often involving saffron or bloodstone, intended to dissolve stones and ease pain.</note>, described by **Paracelsus** in his books on the *Virtues of the Organs*.

<margin>54.</margin> I hear some whispering here—those who are accustomed to swallowing only what has been pre-chewed for them—complaining about the ominous obscurity of my words. These "coal-burners" <note>A common derogatory term for unrefined alchemists who worked only with fire and soot without philosophical understanding.</note>, they say, should set their medicines before us plainly and 

<column-break/>

provide us with ocular demonstrations. <margin>55.</margin> Truly, this is a new standard for learning **Pythagorean Philosophy**! Let them buy coals and glass vessels, and let them first learn what nights spent in orderly watchfulness and the expenditure of money have given to us. The gods sell the arts for sweat, not for readings alone. Therefore, I have not even dared to reveal **Diana** stripped of her clothing; the example of **Actaeon** deters me <note>In mythology, Actaeon was turned into a stag and torn apart by his dogs after seeing the goddess Diana bathing; the author uses this to explain why he keeps alchemical secrets "clothed" in metaphor.</note>. He who can grasp it, let him grasp it. Depart from yourself, then, and leave behind your usual ways—you who presume to investigate the inner chambers of nature through an easy shortcut of readings.

Moreover, so that the first point regarding full <margin>56.</margin> healing may be satisfied, there remained the investigation of a medicine for the complete, safe, and secure dissolution of the stone.
1. It must be fit to be changed into urine, so that it may reach the affected place.
2. It must have within itself the power to loosen the "bars" of the stone. For this is a gift of God, which art does not create, but only separates and draws out.
3. It must possess this in a **specific and appropriated property**; not in "secondary qualities" <note>Secondary qualities refer to simple heat, cold, moisture, or dryness. The author argues these are too crude to work.</note>, which are usually fleeting, failing during preparation, or infamous for the violence of their qualities.
4. It must be subtle, so that it may go in every direction and be able to demolish its object from afar.
5. It must be a friend to nature, so that it does not pervert everything. For not just any messenger approaches the stone quarries; but only he who, freed from bonds, knows the ways, is prepared for the journey, is a friend to the places, and has strength.

Accordingly, those who prescribe this **single combat** <note>original: *monomachiam*</note> using only corrosives are in error. Trusting too much in secondary qualities, they sleep in a state of poor security; and by neglecting specific properties and disregarding the "appropriated" means, they focus only on the physical object and walk into the dark. <margin>57.</margin> For it is not by a quality of corrosion that the **Ostrich** <note>original: *Struthio*. It was a common medieval belief that ostriches could digest iron and stones.</note> grinds iron, or small birds grind flints, pearls, and pebbles. It is a virtue of loosening the bars and the "tartaric" obstacles. It is fitting to meditate upon this and to imitate it. I have spoken.

-># ADAMIC UNDERSTANDING.<-

[Decorative woodcut initial 'A' featuring a seated figure surrounded by foliage and scrolls.]

ADAM gave the fitting names to all animals: and therefore he possessed an intimate, or intuitive, knowledge of them, which is called the **Mastery of Nature** <note>original: *Adeptum naturae*; a term used in alchemy and natural philosophy to describe a deep, divinely-granted understanding of the physical world</note>. Perhaps he similarly possessed the fullest cognition of herbs, minerals, and even the stars. Indeed, when an object previously unseen was presented to him, he knew its innermost properties. From this, most people conclude that the same cognition was given to us as a natural inheritance <note>original: *proprietate vernacula*</note>, as to his descendants and heirs: but that it was obscured through sin. Others, however, contend that it was entirely taken away by the eating of the fruit of the knowledge of good and evil. Having long been wrongly persuaded of these things, I also believed them—alas! For what did I leave untried so that I might reach the promised labor of **Wisdom** <note>original: *Sophiae*</note>, the **Paradise of long life**, through Adamic knowledge? But at last I observed many things which would subvert those principles. For first, I could hardly persuade myself that Adam in the state of innocence knew those things; and even more, that he would afterward *not* know them through the eating of the knowledge of good and evil. That would indeed be the case if he had eaten a fruit of forgetfulness, of sleep, or of ignorance. But not when he had eaten the fruit of *knowledge*. But if in original sin, he himself—the original transgressor and the defiler of human nature—still knew what he knew before: how then, through a newly acquired knowledge of a different character, deposited as if in the forbidden fruit, would he have taken all knowledge away from his descendants? Indeed, why would he himself—who by creation possessed all knowledge except that which is called by the divine spirit the "knowledge of good and evil" through a hidden paraphrase and wordplay <note>original: *peronomasia*</note>—at least not have passed this on to his descendants? For if by the eating of the fruit his eyes were opened—which at least indicates that they were somehow closed before—and he was made knowing of good and evil, and saw that he was naked: why was there at least not as much knowledge in his seed as there was in the fruit? Why, if sin is transmitted through his seed, is shame not also trans-

<column-break/>

mitted, so that Indians <note>Here referring to indigenous peoples encountered in the Americas or East Indies</note> would naturally be ashamed of their nakedness? Or so that a three-year-old child would at least be ashamed of its nakedness? No differently than Adam was immediately after chewing the fruit. Finally, if knowing the natures, societies, and properties of animals had been implanted in him from creation, and thus was essentially within his marrow: how would God, who loves us so much, have taken away the essential intellectual and natural gifts <note>original: *vernacula dona*</note> by which He wishes to be adored in the spirit of man, yet left the natural ones to the **evil demon** <note>original: *cacodaemoni*</note>, the most vile, despised, and worst of creatures? Would He have so greatly impoverished our spirit and favored the devil more than the children of men, with whom He says His delights reside? Indeed, after I conceived in my soul the knowledge of long life and the causes of death, I knew that as long as Adam was immortal, his mind immediately vivified and ruled his body: and even to that extent he perfectly understood whatever things are read to be "subjected under his feet" <note>A reference to Psalm 8:6 regarding man's dominion over the earth</note>. But after the **sensitive soul** <note>original: *anima sensitiva*; the aspect of the soul that governs physical senses and biological urges</note> was introduced as a feminine medium <note>In this philosophical framework, the "feminine" implies a material or passive channel through which life is mediated</note> between the mind and the body, Adam thereafter lived in the soul and in a "middle life"—that is, in the modern manner. And his mind, for the sustenance of the sensitive soul, merely scattered a dark light from itself through the mists of the flesh, over the life of a new and impure generation. However, the former sciences, which he had before the fall, were deposited in the sensitive life through reminiscence; yet they were darkened by the shadowy and wretched discourse of reason. Since he had now generated in the manner of Brutes, and had transmitted the "middle life" in a feminine way, then all his knowledge—both the former and the subsequent (namely, of good and evil)—and the memory of those same things were obliterated in the seed: and man born from there is a **blank slate** <note>original: *inanis tabula*</note>. Indeed, from then on, the sensitive power arose in his descendants, or that same "middle life" which was in Adam. Which, when it had grown to proper maturity in the seed, at last into the true light, the vi-

<meta>This page continues the author’s exploration of the "Adamic Intellect." Having previously discussed Adam’s intuitive knowledge before the Fall, the author now examines the structural relationship between the immortal Mind and the mortal, sensitive Soul in the wake of original sin, and how grace restores our connection to divine light.</meta>

-># ADAMIC UNDERSTANDING.<-

...and the same form was brought forth by the creator. Into which the human **Mind** then transmitted its vicariate <note>original: *vicariatum*; the status of being a deputy or representative, meaning the Mind acts as God's representative within the body</note>. However, the mind remained, as if retracted into its own depth, shuddering at the impurities of nature, and no longer able (unless through grace) to diffuse itself immediately into the sensitive animal soul: God so disposing for his own pleasure; as will be said later. In man, therefore, there is actually something of a natural and formal act, which is the **soul**, or sensitive life, which is very much distinct from the mind. For just as the seed of a dog tends toward a living dog, which reasons obscurely: human seed certainly does not tend toward a corpse, but at least aspires toward a vital soul; and it flows, namely, into the sensitive and discursive <note>the ability to reason step-by-step, rather than through immediate intuition</note> soul, in a far more perfect way than in a dog, a fox, etc.

And so that I might more firmly grasp this real distinction in us between the sensitive soul and the mind, I imagined a young man desperately in love with a girl. For here, with the full sense and consent of the soul, he wishes to be able to be freed from this tiresome love: and likewise he would wish not to love so, and to be freed from love. It is not indeed that he intensely wants now one thing, and then the other by turns: but simultaneously, and with the same motion and impetus, he wishes, and does not wish, to be freed from that love: he declares himself happy and unhappy because of this one love. And he suffers many such contradictory things at the same time. 

Since these contradictions cannot dwell together in the same subject and respect, I hesitated for a long time as to how such things happened everywhere in a single man, until at last the **Apostle** <note>Referring to St. Paul in Romans 7:23</note> solved this knot for me. He spoke of "seeing another law in our members, opposed to the law of the mind." He understands these laws to be supported not only by inclination and desire, but even by reasoning and consent. Then I clearly saw that some affections belong to the sensitive soul, and others to the mind: but these latter are languid, because the operation of the mind is almost darkened by the disturbances of the sensitive soul. 

In this sense, namely, the Apostle calls anger, envy, quarrels, the worship of idols, etc., the **works of the flesh** <note>original: *opera carnis*; Galatians 5:19-21</note>. For although they seem like spiritual concepts, yet because they are operations of the sensitive soul—which itself is raised in nature from the will of the flesh and blood through the seed—they are therefore mere works of the flesh. We are therefore incessantly affected by the troublesome allurements of this "social soul" <note>the part of the soul that interacts with the body and the physical world</note>, because having afterward become degenerate from sin, we lost our immortality. 

For this reason, God now requires only a few things from us so that we may enter into life. Specifically, that a baptized person believe the whole history of the **Creed**, and that he keep the commandments of God by means of His grace. But whoever aspires to a higher degree of **charity** <note>original: *charitatis*; here meaning divine love</note>, let him strive, as much as his talent allows, through loving acts to reach toward those abstract things believed through faith, until through the grace of constant exercise he feels the mind flooded with **supernatural light**, continuing in all humility and charity. 

Indeed, the meditation on natural forms helps much at the threshold for understanding the **quiddity** <note>original: *quidditatem*; the "what-ness" or essential nature of a thing</note> of the sensitive soul. Since all forms besides the mind are vital lights destined to return to nothingness, I have certainly learned that the mind stands at a very great distance from the sensitive soul. 

Inasmuch as the mind is immortal, it is retracted into itself so that it is not defiled by its marriage to the transient social soul: yet it presides over all acts, insofar as it sits nearby and inheres, whole, in the whole sensitive soul. And thus it operates with the soul in a "deaf" <note>original: *surdo modo*; meaning silently, or without being consciously perceived by the senses</note> manner. 

I gathered that this order of the Almighty has been this way since the fall of Adam; first, because He created some people blind, and also some insane, not because of their own or their parents' sin, but by His good pleasure and for His glory. For He did all things as He willed, and by far for the best. Next, because He wished to be worshiped in spirit. And finally, because in His house there are "many mansions" <note>John 14:2</note>, which would be pointless now if every man, being equal in the grace of the soul, were also equal in life. From this I gathered that there must be a diversity of spirits among men, and worshipers of divinity who differ in their degree of charity. Since He created the Angels, so that...

<meta>Continuing from the previous page, which described the conflict between the rational mind and the sensory soul, the author now explains how this internal struggle serves a divine purpose in the refinement of the human spirit toward a state of "Adamic Understanding."</meta>

# THE ADAMIC UNDERSTANDING.

...without the disturbances of physical bodies, that they might adore Him in the spirit of understanding. But man He made a little lower than the Angels <note>A reference to Psalm 8:5</note>: yet primarily for His own glory and adoration, He chose him as the image of divinity, and as adopted sons. Nevertheless, man is subject to an unhappy and calamitous way of life; for being now submerged within a body, he hardly understands that he understands, almost forgotten of his own immortality and subjected to the tyrannical demands of diseases. Thus, the immortal intellect in the insane and the rabid appears almost extinct. For it pleased the Almighty that those diverse mansions of the soul should be inhabited as if by a ladder of merits, and that men—raised up by the mark of grace—might arrive at higher dignities of understanding. This leads toward that promise: *the learned shall shine as the Sun.* <note>Daniel 12:3</note>

The first step, therefore, is to have lived in the simplicity of "operative faith" <note>faith expressed through actions</note>, abstaining from evils and doing good. Next, that they adore God in the spirit of naked truth, and through operative faith proceed by the attainment <note>original: "Adeptum"</note> of paternal love. With the help of merits found in charity—even when we are not consciously striving—we become more and more enlightened in our intellect. 

And so, at last, the mind is released from this dark prison of blood; it looks upon itself intellectually and, with humility, marvels at a light never seen before. It then walks without difficulty toward the more abstract contemplations of the "kiss" <note>A mystical term for the intimate union between the soul and God</note>, led through unknown paths. There, in truth, justice, and the union of virtues, under the light of the abstract spirit, the happy soul adores God as if rising from a deep sleep. For although God may desire different kinds of recognition from a man than He does from an Angel, man should not therefore rejoice any less in the divine good pleasure. Instead, he should continue by praising in humble adoration, in which all understanding of wisdom and the clarity of all spirits are absorbed, as if into a living Center.

<column-break/>

Therefore, by the merit of these degrees, after the Fall, the Ineffable One crowned man with glory and honor—though he was degenerate—and placed all other things under his feet. For before the Fall, man would never have aspired to such heights. Therefore, it was necessary for man to possess neither the full knowledge that Adam had in the beginning, nor even knowledge of himself, if there was to be any "merit" in his life. For a crown presupposes a struggle, merit, and victory. Indeed, it is only from the battle that we can carry back an increase of grace in exchange for victory.

I conclude, therefore, that we who are placed in this "middle" and sensory life know, have, are, and can do nothing of ourselves; we exist only by grace, with our own merit cooperating. To establish this, God required that these stages of progress in the adoring intellect be presupposed. Therefore, let the one who is innocent in hands and pure in heart adore God in the truth of the spirit. 

The state of such a mortal man is far happier than the state of the immortal Adam was before the Fall. For that "poverty of spirit" <note>Matthew 5:3</note> knows wisely in truth, recognizes knowingly, believes confidently, feels truly, and humbly confesses itself to be a mere subject of all defects—that is, a "useless and wicked servant." By this journey, the ineffable Kingdom of God meets man: an ocean of light that gives a clarity of understanding that was not even asked for, and things much more majestic than even the prayers of Angels might desire. These things surpass the philosophy of the heathens and of modern atheists. So it is. Such is the nature of Understanding and Truth, in which our Philosophy places its *Alpha* <note>The beginning or fundamental principle</note>. Unless it does so, a long life is useless—ignored for so many centuries, neglected by so many geniuses, and until the end of the age, known only to the "Adepts" <note>Those who have reached the highest state of spiritual or alchemical knowledge</note>.
