# V I T A L  A U R A.
->(Aura Vitalis)<-

...of the heart. I say that the substantial transformation of crude blood <note>original: *cruoris*; the darker, venous blood</note> into arterial blood <note>original: *sanguinem*</note>, and of arterial blood into spirit, occurs throughout the whole, without any residue or separation of different parts: because the waste products have already been removed. The heart's substance is restless, constantly occupied with this duty of transformation, so that it may ceaselessly produce arterial blood from crude blood, and vital spirit from that blood. Thus, no "natural spirit" exists beforehand in the crude blood as a material from which the vital spirit is made. Rather, the entire crude blood itself, if necessary, becomes arterial blood, and from there, vital spirit. 

Therefore, the making of crude blood in the liver <term>cruorificatio: the hepatic process of turning nutrients into venous blood</term> and the making of blood in the heart <term>sanguificatio: the refinement of blood in the heart</term> differ. For one is a true transformation of chyle <note>milky fluid from digested food</note> into crude blood and the generation of a new being. The other is the thinning of crude blood into volatile blood and into a vital aura. For crude blood is made through its own thickening and the separation of liquid waste without urine. 

But the vital spirit is made through the melting of what was thickened and through aerial thinning, for which the blood provides the step or medium. I admit, indeed, that the **spirit of wine** <note>original: *spiritum vini*; high-proof alcohol</note> is snatched up as a spirit into the arteries, as something simple and similar, already prepared to easily cross over into the vital spirit: but from this, the **Schools** <note>The traditional Scholastic and Galenic medical authorities of the university</note> prove nothing for their liver theory. Therefore, let the crude blood itself be the "hepatic spirit" coagulated, and the pre-existing material of the vital spirits. This spirit certainly has the nature of a body, with the potential to be spiritualized. Thus, just as by the **ferment** <term>a catalytic agent that triggers chemical change</term> of the heart, crude blood becomes arterial blood and volatile spirit: so in the arteries, acting as the heart's stomach and having taken up the heart's ferment, the blood itself passes into the "republic of spirits." 

Indeed, even the secondary humors, or the immediate nourishment of the solid parts, gradually become volatile, so that they leave no residue behind: but through their total transpiration, they make their exit. The heart therefore fashions blood from crude blood by its ferment, which by the same work it prepares and thins

<column-break/>

so that further, in the arteries as if in its own stomach, just as much vital spirit is made from the arterial blood as the thickness of the blood and its resisting substance allows to be made in the short time it is agitated in the arteries. It is almost a single action as crude blood passes into arterial blood, and blood into spirit. For they do not differ in the "workshops" or in the stages of digestion, thinning, and refinement. For just as much blood is born from crude blood, and just as much vital spirit is fashioned from the blood by that same ferment of the heart, as is necessary for each. And the powers of making it are strong. 

Nor is it enough yet to know that crude blood ascends into arterial blood; that blood partly migrates into vital spirit, and partly goes toward the nourishment of the solid parts. From the vital spirit, finally, the **animal spirit** <term>the subtle fluid believed to travel through nerves to cause sensation and movement</term> is made, which receives its ultimate determination in its own nerves. In such a way that the "visual spirit" is made in the optic nerves, but if it wanders from there and is carried to the tongue, it would be plainly useless for taste: just as the animal spirits responsible for touch are unequal to fear, and vice versa. 

Because, moreover, one must know the "marrow" <note>the essential core</note> of the vital spirit. Truly, from the acid chyle, part becomes crude blood, and part becomes urine and sweat. That wasteful saltiness of urine is a volatile and salty spirit, which, when fermented together with earth, finally forms **saltpetre** <note>original: *sal petræ*; potassium nitrate, used in gunpowder but here discussed as a biological salt</note>: for this reason, that salty spirit is a waste product. 

Crude blood, however, through distillation, also shows us a saline spirit, plainly volatile, and in no way distinguishable by smell or taste from the spirit of urine. Yet it is essentially different in this: that the "spirit of blood salt" cures **epilepsy**, but the "spirit of urine salt" does not. From this at least it is clear that in crude blood there is a salty and volatile spirit. But how the entire crude blood is transformed homogeneously by the heart's ferment cannot be explained in words. Because the natures themselves...

# V I T A L  A U R A.
->(Aura Vitalis)<-

they themselves cannot be demonstrated *a priori* <note>original: *à priori*; reasoning from cause to effect</note>. For the essential operations of **ferments** <term>fermentum: a hidden power or "leaven" that directs the transformation of matter</term> are for the transmutation of things, rather than the accidental spreading of traits merely to create certain conditions. Therefore, the **vital spirit** is clearly salty; thus it is balsamic <note>meaning it preserves against decay</note> and a guardian against corruption. Although **spirit of wine** <note>original: *aqua vitæ*; high-proof alcohol</note> easily migrates into the vital spirit, the spirit is not oily or flammable like alcohol. Instead, by the mere touch of a ferment, the spirit of wine is easily and entirely changed into a salty spirit, and immediately loses its flammable nature. Just as I taught in my book regarding *Duelech* <term>Duelech: Van Helmont’s term for the stony material that forms in the bladder or kidneys</term>, how through the **spirit of urine**, alcohol is coagulated in a single instant into a fine mass <note>original: *offam*; likely referring to *Offa Alba*, a chemical phenomenon Van Helmont used to explain physiological processes</note>. One may argue this even more clearly concerning the volatile salt of the blood and the effective ferment of the heart.

For this reason, those who endure heart palpitations for some time, even if they have drunk a great deal of pure wine, do not easily become intoxicated. This is because, due to urgent necessity, the spirit of wine is very quickly drawn into the heart and the arteries—which are impoverished of spirits—and is suddenly formed into vital spirit. It restores strength, I say, yet does not then intoxicate: because it is no longer a stranger, but having easily become a "domestic," it is drawn into the heart and then dispensed through the arteries in every direction. It does not argue to the contrary that the **spirit of saltpeter** <note>original: *salis petræ*; nitric acid</note> is acidic, and that therefore the vital spirit ought to be acidic. For the spirit from which saltpeter was made in the earth was not acidic then. Thus, the vital spirit is salty, and closer in nature to the spirit of urine than to saltpeter—which, because of burning and extraction, is always a new creation of its own compound. Therefore, the foundation that was laid by the ferment of the gallbladder <note>original: *fellis*; bile</note>, by making things volatile and salty, is afterward perfected in the workshop of the heart. Indeed, the previous digestions are so many preparations for vital functions and necessities. For if sensation returns to a limb that was once numbed,

<column-break/>

it certainly happens with perceptible stings and prickling, which are signs of true saltiness. Moreover, that the whole of the blood <note>original: *cruor*; the darker, venous blood</note> is mere salt can be deduced from nowhere more clearly than from the fact that, through a very easy degeneration, the whole of it is changed homogeneously into a salty **ichor** <note>original: *ichor*; a thin, watery discharge</note> in cases of dropsy <note>original: *ascite*; an accumulation of fluid in the abdomen</note> and in ulcers. It was appropriate for the vital spirit to have a salty, sharp quality and a subtle matter, if it was to suffice for preserving the limbs.

The redness of the blood also takes on a yellowish hue when the blood becomes arterial, because through the sharpness of the salt, red becomes yellowish in its dissolution. Yet the blood does not lose all redness, since a part of it must remain for the nourishment of the solid limbs. Everything I have said so far is a "dead" description: that the vital spirit is a salty outflow <note>original: *aporrhœa*; a flowing off or emission</note>, sharp, and made from blood through the ferments of its vital organs. Now, therefore, I shall speak of the *life* of the spirit.

For since it had to perform the duties of life, it was not required that it be in the form of a salty liquid, or blood, or that it should mock us under the image of a salty vapor; but because it was primarily intended to live and receive life, it was necessary for it to be **illuminated**. Certainly not with a burning, flaming, or fiery light, but with a simple, vital light, belonging to the nature of the forms of living things, of life, and of the sensitive soul—and indeed of the human species. Imagine, for the understanding of this, the worms called **glow-worms** <note>original: *nitedulas*; fireflies</note>, which have a light in their bellies at night that does not merely shine like the eyes of a cat, but pours out a thin light all around. That light is extinguished with the life of the glow-worm. Imagine a similar light that illuminates the vital spirit; as long as it lives, it shines, and it is propagated into newly made spirit that has been properly processed. And the more impure and less processed it is, the darker that light will be. This light is extinguished in us, while the matter of the spirit remains, in cases of plague, poisons, etc., just as the light is extinguished and the spirit vanishes through fainting <note>original: *syncopen*</note> and palpitations. At the point of death...

# V I T A L   A U R A.
->(Aura Vitalis)<-

...likewise, the membrane of the eye is destitute of manifest light, at least of the clearly visible sort. Yet, the essence of that light in **fireflies** <note>original: *nitedulis*</note> is not equal to that which is in us, so that they differ from us only by degree. Rather, there are as many species of these lights as there are living creatures. This is an indication to us of Divine generosity: that of the lights, which we understand under a single concept, there are so many species and vital differences. Indeed, these lights are the very lives and forms of the living beings themselves. Thus, the thrice-glorious **Father of Lights** <note>A biblical reference to God as the source of all illumination</note> plays with an abundance of generic lights with no less prodigality than he has fashioned nearly as many varieties in the single human countenance as there are men. For there is, within His power, a certain **Republic of vital lights** and a cohort of innumerable citizens: a certain likeness of which He expresses in living creatures through life and form—that is, through the **vital light**.

The **vital spirit** <term>spiritus vitalis: the refined, airy substance that carries the life force through the body</term> is, therefore, blood which has been resolved into a phantom aura <note>original: *auram falsam*; likely meaning an airy, vaporous, or insubstantial state</note>, vitally illuminated by the power of the **ferment** and the motion of the heart. In us, this light is warm; however, in a **fish**, it is actually so cold that as long as it lives and remains, it can never aspire to the power of heat. Therefore, our heat is not the consumer of the "primigenial moisture" <note>the fundamental fluid believed by ancients to sustain life</note>; for likewise, fish do not escape death thus far by a defect of heat, even though their moisture is not carried off into exhalation—least of all in the icy sea.

Nor will our **Capuchin friar** <note>Van Helmont often uses the Capuchins, who wore simple sandals, as examples of people exposed to the cold</note>, who for the greatest part of the year is freezing from his feet up to his belly—hardly feeling that he has feet—therefore fail to tolerate the daily transpiration of his nourishing moisture, or refuse the restoration of food. Otherwise, the Capuchin would have to have changed into a fish in those parts; which would indeed be necessary if heat were the primary foundation of life, rather than merely an adjacent and accompanying trait. Far be it from us to be ignorant that there is one kind of consumption of moisture caused by heat, but quite another which is promoted by a **thinning ferment**. This latter kind

<column-break/>

indeed leaves no dross or any residue behind it. The former (heat), however, leaves behind stone or charcoal. Thus, the first (heat) tends toward thickening, while the latter (ferment) tends toward thinning.

If, however, a huge heat should sometimes arise in us—which might scorch the limbs like a burning coal or **Persian fire** <note>original: *igne persico*; a historical term for shingles or erysipelas, a painful skin infection</note>, causing them to gangrene, move toward a crusty scab, and then erode the flesh like a dormouse—these are surely the works of **corrosive salts**, acts of lawless degenerations proscribed from the **vital Republic**. In the same way, through laxative poisons, the entire gore of the blood is resolved into rot. For these errors are to be ascribed to the violences of "alien seeds" <term>alienigenorum seminum: Helmont's term for external disease-causing agents that "plant" themselves in the body</term>, under which the vital light degenerates, just as the compression of hay excites a fire.

Furthermore, the **vital spirit** climbs into the head through the **aorta** arteries. In the center of the **brain**, however, there is a single sinus <note>a cavity or channel</note> which, when inspected from above, appears double; but when the "chamber" is raised upward, it shows its unity. In this sinus, the artery ends in a **wrinkled vessel** <note>likely the choroid plexus, a network of blood vessels in the brain</note> of a different texture than the rest of the arterial structure. Through this, the vital spirit flows out into the sinus of the brain, for the service of the **Imagination**, **memory**, and the attendant spiritual faculties. All of these are equally founded upon the **innate spirit**, the inhabitant of the brain. 

From here, if the inflowing spirit proceeds into the openings of the nerves beginning from the brain or cerebellum, it acquires properties suited to the destined functions of those parts. I have said elsewhere that this does not essentially differ from the vital spirit; rather, in the breadth of its essence, it is capable of many properties, according to the breadth of the **Ideas** impressed upon it. For that which flows down to the tongue effects **taste**; yet the same spirit does not taste when in the finger. This is because it takes on the particular determination of the organ without a transmutation of its own nature; otherwise, there would have to be as many subdivisions of the **animal spirit** as there are ministries divided by a plurality of duties. In the meantime, call the thing what you will.

# MULTIPLE LIVES WITHIN MAN.
<note>original: *Vita Multiplex in Homine*</note>

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'O' with floral and scrollwork designs.</image-desc>

I have shown elsewhere that there is a monarchy within the womb, and thus a singular life: which, for instance, still strives to bring forth offspring even after the woman's death. <note>Van Helmont refers to "coffin birth" or post-mortem contraction, which he interprets as the organ having its own independent life force.</note> I have also seen a woman who was never seized by the **falling sickness** <note>epilepsy</note> except when the pains of labor were pressing; nor did it cease except after the birth. I have shown, too, that a certain spleen-shaped flesh <note>likely the placenta</note> lives, born between the **afterbirth** <term>secundinas: the fetal membranes and placenta delivered after the baby</term> and the **sockets of the womb** <note>original: *acetabula uteri*</note>: and its life is proper to itself, such that it does not live by the life of the mother or the fetus. Rather, it lives by a certain shared life—not indeed a sensing life, though it is nourished by a certain **vital power**; yet not by the favor of some "herbaceous" or vegetative soul. Finally, I have shown that a life of its own remains in the veins even after a man's death, by which, for many days after the person's passing, it preserves the blood held within itself from clotting, and to this extent illuminates it with a certain life. Wherefore, in the veins,

<column-break/>

there is another life, by which they not only live, but also preserve the blood itself in a living state. Lastly, I have also demonstrated that a certain peculiar life resides in the muscles, with faculties of sensing and moving, through which they all stretch themselves in a fearful spasm at the sensation of death. This is evident in **tetanus**, in rigors, and in convulsions, in which the muscles are moved against the will, both in the living and after death, even after the extinction of life. And although these "lives" are distinguished by their various locations and are manifested by a diversity of duties, they all nevertheless originate from the **seed** <note>the *semen* or formative biological spark</note>, they are irrational, they are implanted in their respective subjects, and they exist within the integral life as the "forms of the parts" exist within the whole. For this reason, they are not to be considered in a treatise on "long life." This is because they perish without hope of fuel, or at least soon after the death of the man. Nevertheless, they are memorable in the variations of diseases and in curative indications.

# THE FLOW TOWARD GENERATION.
<note>original: *Fluxus ad Generationem*</note>

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'G' with floral and scrollwork designs.</image-desc>

I saw the beginnings of our generation as if in a dream, and I shall describe them with my pen as much as words allow. First, I saw the womb, contracted in its folds with inimitable artifice, expanding itself for conception through its own **magnetic Blas** <term>Blas: Van Helmont’s term for a motive or formative power, in this case acting like a magnetic attraction</term>: and this occurs exactly according to the extension of the seed. This drawing apart or opening of the folds causes a suction and an attraction of the seed by reason of a vacuum. And in this, the **rhombus of conception** <note>The "rhombus" likely refers to the geometric shape or specific anatomical space within the womb</note> lies for the female sex. Indeed, it contains the immediate cause of the pleasure and the attraction of the seed into the womb. For at no other time during sexual unions, however pleasurable, does any expansion of the folded womb ever occur, except at the very instant of conception: hence comes the almost infallible conception of brute animals. Indeed, there is no voluntary drawing apart of the womb,

<column-break/>

nor is it subject to any human arts. Rather, in a way that surpasses nature, it displays God as the President of human generation, continued for the future according to the word of the blessed propagation: **"Be fruitful and multiply"** <note>original: *Crescite, & multiplicamini*</note>. It is surely the **finger of God** which draws apart these chambers without any organic means. As it is said in the Holy Scriptures: **"God opened the womb of Sarah"** <note>original: *Deus aperuit uterum Sarai*</note>. Truly, the whole history of generation would seem to exceed nature, were it not that by the law of acquired propagation and its continued frequency, it had been accepted within the bounds of nature. Whoever, therefore, meditates on the expectation of children should not look for lustful desire, nor an abundance of seed, nor even health: but entirely and primarily for the aforementioned **magnetism of the womb**. and on the part of the male sex, a seed defiled by no contagion. For otherwise, the womb, once receiving seed that is badly imbued, rejects it, nor [does it conceive]...

...subsequently opens itself, so that it might drive the man’s seed into the life of that womb. For often, in fruitful marriages, a womb conceives that was sterile in its first marriage bed. Therefore, the expansion of the womb must be proportioned to the seed to avoid a vacuum. Next, everything foreign is a hostile impediment to generation. Then finally, after the male seed is joined to the female seed, the flux of that "magnet" <note>Van Helmont uses magnetic metaphors to describe the biological attraction between the sexes and the womb's pull on the seed.</note> immediately ceases in the aforementioned hollow of the womb, and the door of the womb closes near its neck. The womb, however, embraces what is contained on all sides and adequately, with all air excluded, by its benevolent favor; and a more exact joining of both begins, because of a hidden **sacred marriage** <term>syngamiam: from the Greek *syngamia*, a union or marriage of seeds</term>, unfolded on both sides within the seeds. Soon after, although the conceived seed is initially a turbid and opaque liquid: yet two days later, it takes on the likeness of transparent egg-white. But on the sixth day (and not before), the inhabitant of the seeds appeared to me, the **Archeus** <term>Archeus: the internal "master workman" or life-force that Van Helmont believed directed all biological growth and healing</term>, like a cloudy vapor, which afterwards, on the thirteenth day, was endowed with the figure of a man in shadow-form, with some clarifying of its thickness. For then the seed had perhaps grown by a tenth part of itself, and had wedded to itself the primary nourishing liquid. Meanwhile, I marveled at the begun **self-love** <term>philautiam: from the Greek *philautia*, an instinct for self-preservation</term> of the "I-ness" <note>original: *egoitatis*; the sense of individual identity or selfhood</note>, which even in the seeds would soon begin to contemplate its own growth. For just as warm milk immediately coats itself with a skin: so too the seed, after three days, clothes itself in a skin, which nevertheless gradually becomes more manifest. Yet in this, both "cloaks" differ: milk covers itself with a skin at least against the air, but the seed does so on all sides. For the skin is not stretched over the milk by a formative spirit, but by heat, separating the different parts of the milk. From this it happens that the more viscous, fattier, and always closer parts of the milk are selected for the skin-making, through separation from the rest; once these are consumed, the skinning of the milk ceases. Therefore, in milk tending toward corruption, there arise

<column-break/>

disparities of matter. This does not happen in seeds collected and arranged for generation. Furthermore, although a "breeze" <note>original: *aura*; a subtle, spiritual substance or vital breath</note> could be seen in the figure of a man: yet I could not yet note any sexual character. (A few days after this vision, I came upon the passage of the Apostle: *There will be neither Greek nor Hebrew, neither male nor female: but all are one in Christ.*) <note>Galatians 3:28</note> Around the 17th day, I saw that this figured aura submerged itself and was plainly "betrothed" within the egg-white, and as if slept for three whole days and about 12 hours. There was again a certain opaque chaos in the seed. In this interval, it drew over itself the visible **afterbirth** <note>here referring to the fetal membranes or placenta</note>; and it had made for itself a hardness of membrane, which it did not find in the material, through its formative and transmutative power. To be sure, this formative aura, while it sculpts the body, does not use separation, nor does it therefore have need of diversity of matter, by which it might fabricate the variations of organs proposed in its blueprint. When those three days had passed, then for the first time appeared that formative spirit, marked with the signature of the sexes, yet no longer wandering indistinctly through the whole mass of the seeds: but under a certain confusion proper to those three days, this whole aura had grown together in every individual part (though not yet apparent). For it was no longer as if one part was wandering and fluctuating in that mass. But a single, indwelling spirit, continuous with itself through the rudiments of the parts, completed the whole distribution of generation. And this labor of his was tireless, yet without toil and weariness. And although it did not grow weary in its work, it nevertheless took a "deputy" to itself. For more and more the distinction of parts is unfolded, and the growth of the whole occurs from the maternal and purer blood, and it forms for itself the **radical moisture** <term>humidum radicale: the fundamental fluid thought to sustain life and innate heat in the body</term>, which constitutes the solid parts. Wherefore it also draws growth and nourishment from the vital spirit of the maternal blood, which it soon assimilates to itself in most perfect union. Truly, the spirit in the seeds is nourished and grows...

It is false, therefore, that nature is everywhere circular.

<column-break/>

Since she everywhere wished to satisfy her own ends, which are put on by the glorious Creator of nature, and not by nature herself. For otherwise, a recurved reflection is not instilled into the upright seminal spirit by the generator; but it proceeds from the finger of Him who disposes all things sweetly from end to end. And so, immediately upon the seed being conceived, the womb closed its lower door, lest anything foreign rush in that might disturb the conception. Finally, the uterine vessels, subject to command, are also closed from above, as if a doorkeeper were added: because then a new **republic** <note>Van Helmont uses political metaphors like "republic" and "economy" to describe the self-governing systems of the body</note> arises in the womb, a new economy of the future fetus: and therefore, a singular kitchen is erected in the neighboring vessels. To such an extent that the embryo is not nourished from the thick blood of the liver: but from pure and clean arterial blood. Soon after, as this kitchen is prepared for the embryo (which is to live in its own world), the womb prepares the thick blood to offer to the embryo, and whatever is found to be less useful is swept away. So much so that during that whole movement, the mother usually feels unwell. Indeed, since the filth can no longer be purged through the drain of the womb, nor can it wait for the maturity of birth: the filth turns back into the good [vessels], takes on the condition of excrement, and is thrust out through vomiting and other sewers. This does not happen equally in brute animals, since they lack the menses and do not admit untimely intercourse. Finally, the conception of humans was not from the Creator's first intention, in the manner in which we are conceived in sins. Finally, also, because for brutes, blood of equal purity would not be required for nourishment. Therefore, the pregnant woman alone, by a dire expiation of many punishments for the pleasure of a single encounter, pays more than the brutes. Therefore, the embryo is first nourished by arterial blood prepared in the kitchens near the womb, until after the first forty-day period, having obtained a living soul, it becomes its own master. And this happens again within the fetus itself before those nutrients can increase its size. However, once the infant is born, before it is capable of enduring harder foods, it grows accustomed to gentler ones. Often, indeed, I have held back a threatened and beginning miscarriage; but sometimes, I could not. I recognized that I had succeeded as often as the miscarriage was caused by a symptomatic **thymosis** <term>thymosi: a state of excitation or "rage" in an organ, here referring to the uterus</term> without a premature expulsive force—that is, when the uterus was merely wandering from its place. The remedy worked by restraining, numbing, soothing, and calming the aforementioned furies of the uterus. But I could not prevent a miscarriage whenever there was a fall by the mother from a height, or a great disturbance of terror, grief, anger, or other disordered passions. Likewise, if the fetus had a notable monstrosity, which adds a swift spur to expulsion. Or if the fetus should die, or waste away or fail from significant weakness.

In this way, a half-living conception often results in a **mole** <term>mola: a non-viable, shapeless mass of tissue in the uterus, sometimes called a "false conception"</term> or a foolish sprout that tends to miscarry. But this hardly ever happens due to a defect in the father’s seed: because a sterile or "foolish" seed is either not drawn in (and thus not conceived), or if it is drawn in, it soon falls out again through the foolish lust of the uterus and irritates the conception. 

However, the seed degenerates into a mole because of external accidents happening to the seed; regarding these, **Hippocrates** says women are "led where they do not wish." A mole therefore occurs while the spirit is submerged in the body of the woman and is stripped of its human shape, yet retains its original vegetative life. Thus, submersion alone can seize the shape from the forming spirit, if it is lulled to sleep within for too long. However, a dream-vision—although it lasted scarcely seven or eight minutes <note>original: *semiquadrantem horæ*; literally half a quarter of an hour</note>—nevertheless represented all the successive periods of generation together, as if in a mirror. The moments, surely—the flows, movements, appearances, alterations, and at the same time the errors—stood collected into a unity. 

But having woken up, alas, how much I groaned at the similarity of our modern propagation with that of the animals! And so, not undeservedly, **Adam** mourned the death of **Abel** for a century. Grieving for a time that hateful animal-like generation, he did not know his wife for that entire century. He weighed deeply that nature, already defiled in its root, was destined to suffer original and necessarily lasting hardships.

For in the first place, the moon does not accumulate or expel this blood: although

# THE LUNAR TRIBUTE

The purging of the uterus coincides with the course of the moon. However, this coincidence between the two cycles is merely accidental <note>original: *per accidens*; a philosophical term meaning something that happens by chance or side-effect rather than by essential nature</note>. For otherwise, if this female purging were caused by the moon itself, all women—at least those living in the same climate—would surely menstruate on the same day. Or at the very least, all young women would suffer the same thing simultaneously with the new moon. This is clearly false. Indeed, if several ships follow a lead ship or a flagship in the dark of night, and that lead ship carries a lantern as a signal, the lantern provides only the sign for the following; but the wind, the helm, and the pilots are the immediate efficient causes of the pursuit. Thus, the moon, like a torch, completes its allotted circuit in four weeks and six hours; and the woman does the same for reasons to be added shortly. For a woman was required to increase and nourish the conceived offspring from her own substance until the fetus reached its proper size, and then to feed the born infant with her own blood turned into milk. Therefore, it was necessary for her to have a more copious supply of blood, so that, while it was not being absorbed for those purposes, it would become superfluous and, consequently, be excreted. Indeed, although a woman eats and drinks much less than a man, she nevertheless abounds with more blood. That is, the "blood-workshop" <note>referring to the liver or the body's metabolic functions</note> produces more blood in a woman than in men, even from a more meager amount of food and drink. From this, it necessarily follows that more of what she eats is turned into useful nourishment in a woman, whereas in a man, more is changed into waste. But so that everyone may know what kind of blood this surplus is, let it be known that human blood must be renewed in the same span of days in which the moon measures its individual courses through the zodiac. This is precisely the span of time in which the blood is preserved by its own internal **balsam** <term>balsam: in early medicine, a vital, life-preserving substance within the body that prevents decay</term>; if it is kept longer, it spoils. Indeed, whoever abounds in blood must either consume it by nourishing the "family of life," or must transform it into fat, watery phlegm, other dregs, sweat, or morbid wastes. For a woman has tiny pores, and her fleshy membrane beneath the skin is rich in much fat; therefore, she cannot consume in nourishment

<column-break/>

the amount of overabundant blood she produces daily. Once the goal of the blood's course is reached, all the surplus becomes spent <note>original: *effetus*</note>. Nature then strives to eject it, sequestering it toward the veins of the uterus as if to a designated drain <note>original: *emunctoria*; an organ or canal that carries off waste</note>. The blood recedes to those specific places, and no others, because for the reasons already stated, the menstrual flow is a superfluity of female blood alone. It becomes burdensome by the very fact that it is superfluous, and even more so because it then loses its vital spirit. It is not unlike certain wines which, after a year has passed, become stale <note>original: *vappa*; flat or spoiled wine</note>. In these ways and for these purposes, the blood becomes an excrement, then a poison <note>original: *virus*</note>, and it acquires worse powers as it goes along. Finally, it assumes the horrid properties of a fresh corpse. This is why the menstrual discharge of the first few days is more infected than that which flows on the subsequent days. For although the expulsion of the menses is the specific task of the veins, nevertheless its collection, renewal, and sequestration belong to the **monarchal Archeus** of the uterus <term>Archeus: the "internal chemist" or governing vital force that directs the functions of a specific organ</term>. Therefore, because it is most hateful to the body, it is ejected more quickly the sooner it has separated from the good blood; and thus, having been detained longer around the veins of the uterus, it becomes all the more virulent. Finally, even if this poison mimics the appearance of blood, having lost the favor of its vital balsam, it ascends by degrees to the malignancy of a cadaverous liquid; it assumes the nature of a venom and has degenerated from the original nature and properties of blood. Mechanical proof confirms this. Indeed, if a cloth stained with menstrual blood is plunged into boiling water, it contracts a stain that is hereafter indelible; and by at least the third washing, it falls out of the cloth in holes, just as if it had been corroded by the acidic spirit of sulfur <note>original: *spiritu sulfuris acido*; sulfuric acid</note>. This property is entirely foreign to human blood in any other case—whether it flows from the nose, wounds, hemorrhoids, or dysentery, or even if it falls from ulcers like a dark, clotted mass. From this, it is also clear that the menstrual flow possesses a dyeing property similar to alum <note>original: *aluminosam tinctoriam*; alum was used as a mordant to fix dyes</note>.

From the weight of what has been said, it is clear that pregnant women, nursing mothers, the infirm, the bloodless, the emaciated, the prepubescent, and old women lack the menses because they also lack the superfluity.

It is also false that all menstrual blood is indiscriminately poisonous, or that it is entirely harmless. Likewise, it is false that we are nourished in the womb or grow from the menstrual flow. For womanly blood does not take on the condition of the "menstruum" until, being unfit for nutrition and exhausted of life, it is bound and led to the sewer <note>original: *cloacam*; a metaphor for the body's excretory systems</note>. For he who drinks wine does not drink vinegar, even if the latter is made from the former. Just as he who eats food does not feed on excrement. Indeed, there is more: the blood which is excreted during or shortly after birth is not menstrual blood, because it lacks the necessary condition—namely, that it is not a superfluity from the preceding course of the moon. Furthermore, because it is not gathered, fleshy, or aluminous <note>original: *aluminosus*; likely referring to a styptic or astringent quality</note>, does not stain linens, is not segregated from the whole, nor is it proscribed to the uterine sites for expulsion. blood; yet it is not the mother’s menstrual flow. For this reason, that blood took on a different property than that of the mother, and different than that of the menstruum. For that guest blood indeed has the appearance of menstrual blood; yet it is an adoptee of a foreign family, and having become exotic to the mother, it must be seriously expelled, no differently than the afterbirth itself. If neglected and left behind, it corrupts and brings death. Furthermore, since there is no menstrual flow at all in a pregnant woman, it follows that the fetus is not nourished by it: but rather by the pure blood of the mother, and then by pure blood previously purified in its own "kitchens."

Therefore, the Schools <note>The "Schools" refers to the established university authorities of the time who followed traditional Galenic and Aristotelian medicine</note> are mistaken when they teach that rashes, measles, or smallpox <note>original: *exanthemata, morbillos, seu variolos*</note> are owed to almost every mortal because of the "tribute" of menstrual nourishment consumed in the womb. But in all these things, lacking true knowledge of the facts, they have simply agreed with one another and fallen into fables and conjectures. For first of all, they did not consider that it would be almost impossible for anyone to be immune to that disease if everyone were nourished by the menstruum indifferently. Secondly, they would be afflicted at a certain, single, and fixed term, as if by a crisis.

1. The first is when that blood is superfluous from the previous cycle of the moon. 
2. The second occurs as soon as it is separated from the rest of the blood. 
3. The third is when it resides, set apart, around the vessels of the womb. 
4. The fourth is when it has clung there for a while and has entered the "path of death" <note>the process of decay or fermentation</note>. 
5. The final stage is when it is already like a corpse and has vanished into the air. 

Error is therefore committed by the Schools <note>the established medical universities of the 17th century</note> through bloodletting <term>bloodletting: Latin 'venae sectiones' or 'phlebotomia,' the common medical practice of draining blood to balance the humors</term>, when they busily attempt to aid virgins who feel heart palpitations on account of the menses, without making any distinction between these stages. This is because I have observed that when the veins of the arm or the backs of the knees are emptied, the menstrual blood is drawn backward from the neighborhood of the uterus into the main veins. Since these veins do not remain empty but are filled again by the connection of the vessels: thus, after immense palpitations and intermittent pulses, or following acute pains in the sides originating from the uterus (doubtless because of the alum-like poison <term>alum-like poison: 'virus aluminosum,' referring to a sharp, astringent, or corrosive chemical quality</term> of the third degree), I have seen virgins suddenly expire because of bloodletting performed against my will. In the first degree, the abundance of blood is indeed removed. But it is a lesser evil even if a part of the produced blood is left behind. I would certainly prefer to help nature in its sequestration <note>the process of separating or setting aside waste</note> and expulsion rather than to have weakened nature by draining blood indiscriminately. This is also noteworthy: that although I have distinguished diseases by...

This is because the menses is neither digested nor is it a waste product <note>original: recrementum</note> of digestion, and thus it is of a different condition. For first it errs by a "good" abundance, then it becomes an oppressive superfluity; soon it is deprived of life and becomes a poison. Yet it heals pigs bordering on leprosy, as it also immediately heals horses who have fallen ill from drinking at the wrong time, if they are given a tiny bit of menstrual blood to drink. Likewise, the virulent and true menses of another woman, given in a few drops, immediately strangled a woman suffering from a flow <note>likely a uterine hemorrhage</note>. However, the blood which is finally excreted copiously in such flows, if drunk in a few drops, stops the flows <note>Helmont describes a "like cures like" or sympathetic effect here</note>. 

Furthermore, the fact that only woman (with the possible exception of the ape) suffers the menses—and although the menses may only indicate abundance—nevertheless, a cow whose udder has dried up does not suffer menses, though otherwise she overflows with much milk. This denotes that the abundance of blood is indeed the material cause, but not the "final cause" <note>the ultimate purpose or reason for being</note>, which I have therefore not classified among the natural laws. This is because the Almighty alone encloses all the causal ends of all things within Himself, He who disposes all things sweetly according to the inscrutable abyss of His judgments. 

But if one wishes to inquire into the cause of this, it is certain that Eve, after eating the forbidden fruit, made herself subject to the itch of lust, and excited and admitted her husband to intercourse. From this, human nature was conceived as corrupted and has since persisted as degenerate. Because of this corruption, her descendants are deprived of incomparable purity. Hence there is room for conjecture: that Eve, through the member by which she became subject to many miseries, might bear witness to her descendants of the successive guilt of her fall and the bloody defilement in nature. For indeed, the part in which the image of God was to be conceived by the Holy Spirit has become a sewer of filth, witnessing to the abuse and the guilt of indelible sin; and therefore woman endures it. Because "in pain you shall bring forth children" like the beasts, because henceforth you shall conceive in the manner of beasts. For in this way that curse entered into nature...

## LIFE.

<image-desc>Decorative initial S</image-desc>
If I must finally philosophize regarding a long life, I must first look into what life is; then, what the life of man is, what is immortal and Adamic <note>referring to the state of Adam before the Fall</note>, what is thereafter sensory and short, what is diseased, what is healthy, what is the life of the world, and what is eternal life. To this end, it is appropriate to repeat several lessons from my previous premises. First, therefore, life is a light and a formal beginning <term>formal beginning: Latin 'initium formale,' the organizing principle or 'soul' that gives a thing its specific nature</term> by which a thing acts as it has been commanded to act. This light, however, is given by the Creator, infused into things in a single instant, just as fire is struck from a flint; it is enclosed within the identity and unity of the form, and is distinct throughout genera and species. However, it is not a fiery light, nor combustible, nor is it a consumer of the radical moisture <term>radical moisture: Latin 'humidi radicalis,' a medieval medical concept of a life-sustaining fluid innate to all living things that acts as fuel for the body's natural heat</term>. It is as vital in a fish as it is in a lion; as much in a poppy as in pepper. Nor does the heat within us fail because of the consumption of radical moisture, nor conversely does the moisture fail due to a lack of heat: but only because of the lessening and extinction of the vital powers, and thus of the light itself. Fire, light, life, forms, the *magnale* <note>original: "magnale," a term used by Paracelsus and Van Helmont to describe a great mystery or a vital medium through which forces act</note>, place, and so on, are "neutral creatures," not substances, nor are they included in the catalog of accidents. Therefore, I do not distinguish the "form" in living things from "life" itself, except in both cases for the human mind. To be sure, a certain kind of life is "mute" and scarcely appears, such as that which occurs in minerals; which nevertheless declare that they live and die through their own signs and the emblems of their vital powers. A second kind is then a little more unfolded, such as that in the seeds of things tending toward the period of their own species. A third kind is finally seen in plants, which increase themselves and prolificate through successive multiplication.

<column-break/>

—and consequently, she was never subject to the monthly flow, just as she suffered no female inconveniences. For she deservedly has the moon, and the properties of the moon, spread under her feet by divine decree <note>original: "luna... pedibus substratam," an allusion to the Woman of the Apocalypse in Revelation 12:1</note>. To whom, after God, be honor and praise.

The fourth kind of life is manifest in beasts through motion, sense, and the choice of will, along with a certain discourse of the imagination. The last kind, finally, is in the immortal mind, which is a substance that is now obscured and is explained to some extent through the "sensitive soul" <term>sensitive soul: Latin 'animam sensitivam,' the part of the soul responsible for sensory perception and movement, shared with animals</term> which acts as its deputy. Life, therefore, is not a balsam, nor a "mummy" <note>original: "mumia," a vital essence or spiritualized substance often discussed in iatrochemistry</note>, nor finally the spirit of the blood, although the latter is the preserver of the body. This is because life is not matter, nor even a substance, but the very form of the thing itself.

Furthermore, being about to speak of the immortal life of men, I shall follow the text. For truly, because the penalty for the broken commandment was death—for death did not come from God, but arrived from the condition of the Law—I say the Almighty did not make death, nor did He create a "medicine of destruction" <note>a reference to the Wisdom of Solomon 1:13-14: "For God made not death... neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living."</note> upon the earth. And that is to be understood strictly in respect to humans. For the entire nature and condition of the universe did not have to be defiled because of the sin of Adam, to such an extent that beasts were made subject to death by the transgression of our race. Indeed, even before the fall of sin, beasts had to die, since the Lord of things had substituted some of them as meat and fodder for others. For they had to die naturally—all those things whose life and form were one and the same annihilable thing. That is, it was necessary for those forms to perish which, through the physical union of seeds, obtain their first preceding and subsequent dispositions. Therefore, the death of beasts was not worthy of the name "death," since it included the extinction and annihilation of the light, rather than the separation of that light with the preservation of the separated part. It pleased the Immense One, therefore, that he should fashion man in—

into a living likeness of the divine majesty, not subject to death. Therefore, God is said not to have made death. It is believed, therefore, that Adam, before his transgression, was immortal through the goodness of the creator. Thus I have understood that Adam was indeed immortal before the breaking of the law; yet this immortality was not natural to him from the "root of life" <note>the innate biological principle of life</note> but rather by virtue of the Tree of Life. For otherwise, the planting of this tree in Paradise would have been in vain if man could not have suffered the changes of ages and calamities. Therefore, the tree was created for the powers and necessities of renewal, rejuvenation, and indeed for the prevention of old age. For even if the body from its creation were not vulnerable nor subject to diseases, it would nonetheless have felt the successions of ages little by little, unless vigor had been sustained by the Tree of Life. For it is not believable that the Lord of things, the Savior of the world, was of a worse constitution than the **First-Formed** <term>Protoplasto: the "first-formed" man, Adam</term>. But as for the fact that the Redeemer of the world died, and felt the calamities of age so much that in his 32nd year he was reckoned as fifty <note>original: "census sit quinquagenarius," a reference to John 8:57, suggesting Christ looked older due to his suffering</note>, this did not happen from his own nature, nor from the root of his life. For death, as well as the decay of years, had no right over him. But out of his infinite goodness, by which he had made himself a guarantor for our sins, he willed to subject himself to hardships and even death in his most glorious birth, in which the Lord took the form of a servant. How far he withdrew from the original and genuine dignity of his human nature, in which he was conceived in the womb, he himself showed. Indeed, he who came forth into the world from the closed womb of the Virgin, having scorned the barriers of physical dimensions, immediately subjected himself to the condition of destined death and willingly felt every necessity of a servant’s nature. Doubtless both Adams were immortal in their beginning. The first was to be preserved by the Tree of Life. The second, however, contained the Tree of Life entirely within himself. Doubtless both chose to be able to die rather than to live: the first from a fault, the second from charity. The Tree of Life, therefore, and the healthfulness of the place of Eden,

<column-break/>

would have protected Adam in his original vigor from death, until, the number of years being completed, he would have departed, translated happily to the homeland of glory without death. Furthermore, it is a matter of faith that Adam never tasted of the Tree of Life; and lest he should eat of it, he was cast out of paradise, he who now had to face death. Indeed, he was of such perfect constitution—having been formed immediately by the hand of the Almighty without the commerce of nature—that even when banished from the garden of pleasure, he lived for some nine hundred years, and would have far exceeded the age of **Methuselah** <note>The oldest man in the Bible, said to have lived 969 years</note> by the power of his own nature, had he not cut short the thread of his very long life through a century of continuous grief and sorrow. Therefore, the death of Adam is not to be lamented (as **Paracelsus** <note>Theophrastus Paracelsus, a famous Renaissance physician and alchemist</note> wrongly persuaded himself), on the grounds that the vital spirit and the science of long life collapsed together with him. For they contradict this view, noting that a long life is obtained through science; likewise, that through the formation by the hands of God and the support of the Tree of Life, he was immortal; even after sin, he retained the gift of long life due to the most perfect and noble constitution of his life and body. From this, finally, the spirit of a flourishing and exuberant life was passed to his descendants; as vigor gradually declined through the transmission of generations, it manifested the injuries of life and diseases, and the decay of years, with the curse cooperating as it must on a great scale; which, once it entered the vitals of mortals, soon took possession of them. For those whose life was previously without destruction through the tree, soon also without it, languished within a brief prescribed limit, and underwent increase, status, decline, and fall, in the manner of other things. Thus indeed death established its empire at the devil's persuasion. For poisons that were harmless under the Tree of Life were then supported as a medicine of extermination. For I believe the properties and presence of the Tree of Life were hidden from **Adam**. Otherwise, he would have stretched out his hand to this sooner than to the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. And although the tree...

However, I do not mean that life which is read to be implanted in the Paradise of Pleasure <note>original: "Paradiso voluptatis," referring to the Garden of Eden</note>, which no mortal will ever reach. Rather, ours is a shadowy life, a substitute for the other. It possesses nothing extraordinary or majestic unless, through the retention of its properties by art <note>referring to alchemy or medical chemistry</note>, it is reduced into a juice of such a kind that it can mingle itself with the solid parts of the body through the smallest particles. Nor indeed does our life (of which I first treat) contain impassibility <note>the state of being unable to suffer or feel pain</note>, freedom from diseases, or the incapacity for death, as the other life does. On the contrary, even if the Tree of Life from Paradise were available to us today, it would not cause immortality. This is because the condition of the receiver has changed. For man has been made of a different generation, of a corrupt nature, and constructed with the bond of a different, long life. In this state, the immortal mind no longer immediately sustains all the actions of life within itself; instead, it is succeeded by the perishable sensitive soul <note>the part of the soul responsible for sensation and movement, which humans share with animals</note>, which acts as a substitute for the mind and provides for the necessities of life. This soul itself is like a flame, failing and extinguishable by the hour.

## A SHORT LIFE.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap initial 'A' with foliate and floral motifs.</image-desc>The **formative aura** <term>Aura formatrix: a vital spirit or "breath" that directs the development of an organism</term>, in the seed, gradually ascending to its own maturity, finally conceives the light of its species or its essential form. This form comes immediately from the **Father of Lights** <note>original: "Patre luminum," a biblical reference to God (James 1:17)</note> and is life properly named. For as many species as there are of things wrapped in darkness, there must also be as many species of forms beneath that light. For if a thing is what it is because of its form, in its difference from all others, and if the form of living things (except for the mind) and "life" are synonyms, then there must be as many lives as there are vital forms. Therefore, the light of life is simple in itself everywhere and specific to each kind; it is not, however, fiery, because it is vital, formal, and essential. The fact that the light of life may be hot or cold denotes that life is only accidentally joined to heat or cold. Thus, heat or cold comes from life, but life does not come from heat or cold. Life, therefore, cannot be understood otherwise than under the concept of light. Neither can life be demonstrated from prior causes any more than the forms of things themselves can, or whatever flows immediately from the bosom of the Almighty. Therefore, this vital light, though varied by species, lacks a specific name of its own. We can indeed create fiery light, which is given to us for our great needs, but it is not within the power of the **artist** <note>here meaning a physician or alchemist</note> to produce vital light from himself or immediately. As the **Chemists** <note>original: "Chymici"</note> say, the artist cannot introduce a substantial form. The progenitor is indeed the performer and producer of the vital aura, insofar as he contributes matter toward something like himself and prepares its dispositions in order for life; however, he can in no way produce life, or the **ultimate entelechy** <term>entelechiam: a Greek philosophical term for the full realization or "completion" of a potential</term>. Even in diseases, the light of life sometimes rises to the degree of fire; because the **Archeus** <term>Archeus: the internal "master worker" or vital force that governs the body's functions and healing</term>, when the distinction of the body is threatened, strikes out a fiery light. This is not because the Archeus produces this fire as something like itself, but rather, through fury, the Archeus compresses "damp hay" and it catches fire—which does not happen to dry hay. In another way, wood through constriction and iron through friction conceive fire which they did not previously possess. Indeed, identical effects in a species cannot come from things that are entirely different in kind, except by accident or an equivocal action. In this way, the sensitive spirit, due to pain, or the Archeus, through poisons, catches fire accidentally through its own burning anger, contrary to its nature. For the **Blas** <term>Blas: a term coined by Van Helmont for a motive power or "pulse" of the stars or the human body</term> has that by which, receding from the vital light, it leans toward the other extreme of destruction. In this state, the rays of its light, as if from a flint, strike out fire from corruptible matter, where both lights—that of the Archeus and that of the corrupting thing...

...perishable, they penetrate one another, are united, and are advanced into a fiery light. For fire is the death of a thing in both respects, arising from its own effect of deficiency, yet capable of being stirred up in things consisting of some fatty, inflammable substance. Indeed, although there is but one single spirit in the seed—entirely uniform, singular, and the lasting **Architect of the embryo** <note>The "Architect" refers to the Archeus, the internal governing principle that directs the growth of a living being</note> until its exit onto the stage of life—it was nevertheless a defect and the ruin of material nature that this spirit, torn apart by a plurality of duties, gradually turns toward the multiple heterogeneities <note>Differences in kind or nature</note> of individual parts. And this is truly a defect, insofar as it paves the way toward **ataxia** <note>original: "ataxiam," meaning disorder or lack of coordination</note>. For otherwise, since the spirit must serve the necessities of its goals, it was certainly a noble thing for it to be distributed into a number of tasks. Indeed, necessity itself created its own servant organs, and for that reason, it established many and diverse organs for itself, and has hitherto brought itself under that same law of necessity.

It has, in fact, imitated a **monarchical state**, in which there is some independent prince, the moderator of laws and government. For this reason, it fashioned a certain solar, emanating life for the **Heart**, as if depending on it from elsewhere, and established the fountain of radical life in that very place. But because a republic cannot long subsist unless it is nourished, after the Kings, the first are the **Farmers** and **Fishermen**, who provide us with grains, herds, flocks, fish, wool, flax, wine, wood, honey, oil, and hides. For even before Kings were thought of, happy shepherds and farmers already had their flocks. For that reason, **Saturn** is imagined as the parent of the lesser gods; the pagans handed down that he holds the necessity of nutrition in us through the **Spleen**, providing a splendid life of vegetation through a shifting, gliding ferment. Finally, those who would prepare grains into bread, and also wool, flax, and hides into clothing, support the farmers. Soon **Jupiter**, substituted in the father's place, succeeded by craft and force; and therefore another disposer of nourishment, establishing his home in the **Liver**, was joined to the nutritive life; he corresponds adequately to a necessary place in the monarchy. Finally, **Mars**, removing the dissenting remains from the prior digestions—

<column-break/>

—acting as a reserve in the **Gallbladder**, conforms to the **Soldier**. Only these three seemed necessary and sufficient—namely, the **Sun**, **Saturn**, and **Jupiter**—so long as each individual part harmonized in concert. But then the **Martial** life <note>referring to the gallbladder/bile</note> was added, not so that there might simply be a republic and a state, but so that each part might preserve peace and mutual duties toward one another, lest the unity be destroyed as a crowd of impurities grows.

Furthermore, to grow follows upon being present. For a thing exists before it grows. Indeed, since a thing cannot be fattened unless it is nourished, being nourished precedes growing. For the **Moon**, the last of the wanderers <note>The "wanderers" or "errones" are the planets</note>, is nearest to the earth in respect to those things that are fattened. Therefore, its immediate and inexcusable necessity dedicated this economy to the **Brain**, which is sacred to the **Judge** in the monarchy. To be sure, one lives from the **Heart**, but sustenance comes from the **Spleen** and **Liver**; the correction of digestion comes from the **Gallbladder**; but the power of growth <note>original: "accretrix"</note> is from the **Brain**. Thus, "to vegetate" and "to grow" differ in their origins as well as their organs. And this is surely not by accident, or because of the stubbornness of parts that subsequently refuse to grow, but because of the singular gifts of the **Internal Organs** <term>Viscera</term>.

Indeed, what I have said is seen even in the rising of the embryo. Since the power of growth flows from the brain (which no one has thought before this), the head of the embryo, and of the fetus itself, is proportionally much larger than the other members. For if a hand is dislocated, it not only ceases to grow, but furthermore, it even decreases, even in adults. **Hunchbacks** <note>original: "Gibbosi"</note> also stop growing, although the gradually distorted vertebrae protrude greatly outward or to the side; it is certainly not because the sense of feeling is taken away or diminished in hunchbacks, for they feel no less than any others. Therefore, the defect of growth does not depend on any dislocation of nerves, veins, or arteries, but solely by regard of the crookedness in the **spinal cord** <term>medulla</term>, through which the straight influence of the brain is poorly "enfleshed." Nor is this flow a humoral one <note>A flow of the four bodily fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note>, namely through the veins and arteries (since in the twisted branches of trees, as well as in curved legs, a defect of growth is not perceived)—

In the elderly, teeth not infrequently grow in anew. And all of this occurs because the **accretive power** <note>The force responsible for growth and tissue repair</note> obeys the brain. Astrologers attribute the power of growth to the moon, yet no one attributes it to the brain. The bones of old animals (as I have said), by a singular secret, contain more marrow than those of younger ones. This is because the moon works toward transmutation, rest, destruction, and reduction into primary matter. Therefore, the moon is very powerful in the elderly and does not prevent the marrow from being increased. Furthermore, since every being desires to grow and meditates on its own propagation from the very beginning, Nature is concerned with nothing more than sex—so much so that she has marked even the insects, which she rouses from corrupt waste, with the distinction of sexes. There was also a need for **Venus** <note>A metaphorical term for sexual desire or reproductive function</note>. The **Schools** <note>The traditional academic authorities of the time, often Aristotelian</note> think the kidneys serve this purpose. I disagree, however, because I have observed those with stones in both kidneys to be more lustful than is right. Nor, otherwise, could I believe that if the fundamental organ of Venus were damaged, lustfulness could persist. This is because the necessity of the parts is such that if they are damaged in their own organ, their function is also necessarily cut off. I have spoken elsewhere of the "Venus of the Spleen." At least let it suffice here that the female sex is primarily necessary and highly useful for the subsistence of the **Republic** <note>The body viewed as a self-governing state</note>, according to divine praise. But finally, since not every land bears every fruit, the custom of mortals has introduced linked provinces and mercantile alliances for the purpose of living well and comfortably. Thus, utility has made the **Lungs** into **Mercury** <note>The Roman god of trade and messengers, here symbolizing the lungs' role in exchange and communication with the "external" air</note>, conforming to trade with external things. This was so that after the fetus had grown, it might have the vital vigor of respiration and voice. I speak of a life that is participative and distributive throughout the whole, which can be breathed out in a steady breeze...

...without which, surely, all the blood would thicken into a stone-like crust through nutrition, and the body would soon either grow into a massive monster or be suffocated from the start—as I have discussed elsewhere regarding the human <term>Blas</term> <note>A term coined by the author to describe the vital, pulsating motion or influence within living things</note>. Yet, although this republic and harmony are thus compared to the "errors" of the stars, I would not want the **Architect** to beg for these things from the celestial stars elsewhere like a stranger. For He who made the stars from nothing with a little word, established within the inner chambers of seeds the similar power of the Word ("increase and multiply") to last through the ages. Therefore, by a free gift, the seed has drawn into itself the ability to stir up and imitate the analogies of the stars in its own **Blas**. Thus it happens that more fortunate imitations of the stars follow at fixed periods, because they are more powerful and clearer impressions. Yet, meanwhile, there is no power from the stars that presides over the formation of mortals, their morals, health, vocation, or fortunes. For He who is all in all, and created all things for an immediate end—His own glory—did not want His image to be subject to the stars, lest men excuse themselves of a crime through the troublesome revolutions of the planets. But it is well. There is in the seminal being an analogue that corresponds to some extent to the stars and the whole universe. Therefore, first in man, the seed clothes itself with membranes, then it exerts itself in its own "economy," and finally, it meditates on the aforementioned Republic, arranges individual parts in various ways, and constrains them with "municipal" laws. Then, indeed, it also contemplates a kingdom and empires. Finally, it considers the whole earth, and lastly the heavens. And so, by the power of the Word, it shadows the entire universe within itself, insofar as it is the <term>Imago Dei</term> <note>The Image of God</note>. For He put under his feet the birds of the air, the fish of the sea, sheep, oxen, and the beasts of the field. Because He established him over the works of His hands. ...in a way to reflect the heavens in the image of the **Archetype** <note>The original divine model or blueprint of creation</note>. However, that command, since it is now planted in nature, will be a person’s own innate greatness from the very egg <note>original: "ab ovo"; meaning from the moment of conception</note>: but not from the Stars substituted for himself. Since, however, the **Schools** <note>The traditional academic authorities</note> and the common folk have considered the defects found in deformities and faulty formations more than those arising from erroneous faculties, they have given **Astrologers** <note>Those who believe human fate is governed by the stars</note> the opportunity to pull everything toward their celestial dances as they please. But after the diversity of functions was recognized by more discerning minds, they began to involve the **heterogeneity** <note>The state of being composed of diverse or unlike parts</note> of faculties and organs; consequently, they began to trace this difference, number, and deformity back to the stars, and refer them to the directions of the seeds. Indeed, under a nature already fundamentally corrupted for a long time, lucky seeds could neither be kept under a single unity, nor could the distinct duties of so many organs be fulfilled through it, without a disparity of strength creeping into the internal organs almost from the beginning; indeed, an inequality of strength would even creep into individual parts and be sealed into their locations. From this, finally, comes the breaking of the thread, dissolution, an offspring of infirmities, and many a plague. All of which the celestial diviners—with the Schools not resisting but standing amazed—have attributed with impunity to their own dances of the constellations. Therefore, as if a lead goat were grabbed by the beard, the entire subsequent crowd of posterity followed in admiration. For there is such great heterogeneity in the heart of matter that scarcely...

<column-break/>

...a golden thread could be made that does not become weaker in some part of itself and snap more quickly. Therefore, it is no wonder that in such a distraction of members and functions, an unequal strength grows into the limbs. On this account, entire families perish from consumption or **dropsy** <note>original: "hydrope"; a condition of swelling caused by excess fluid</note>. In some, the ability to walk fails by the age of fifty, while their sight persists until eighty. In others, truly, the sight grows dull from forty, while their gait promises longevity. Indeed, from the simple and universal spirit of the seed, the governors <note>original: "rectores"; the internal guiding forces of specific organs</note> of the individual organs grow. These rectors, certainly, either by the fault of those receiving them or by an error in distribution, not infrequently depart from their goal, having become alienated. For the spirit, which distinguished and formed the parts from one another, soon took up all the determinations within those very parts. For in the eye, the optical spirit sees, and in the tongue, it tastes: because the flowing spirit is determined by the spirit implanted there. Just as, furthermore, there is a certain initiating life in the Spleen, another in the muscles, and finally another in the woman's womb, as I have often demonstrated elsewhere. Each of these is as separated from the common life of the man as those things which have different existences. Since, therefore, plurality includes a certain duality, it is no wonder that a life driven by many different governors easily falls into dissolution, once the immortal mind has allowed the reins of governing life to slip onto the neck of the **sensitive life** <note>The part of the soul or vital force responsible for physical sensations and instincts, as opposed to the rational mind</note>.

The **Gospel** <note>original: "Euangelium"</note> promises mortals not only that the Son of God was incarnated and suffered for human salvation, but that these two mysteries are applicable to individuals, who otherwise would exist as if in vain. Now, I have considered that application in this way. Truly, through sin, man broke God's intent no less than His decree; hence human nature was corrupted in its root, because a different generation followed, almost beast-like, incapable of eternal life by itself. For this reason...

<column-break/>

...the Gospel had to include the abolition of **original sin** <note>The fallen state of humanity inherited from the first man</note> and all other sins flowing from the corruption of nature. Therefore, since man from then on should no longer be born naturally from God, but only from the blood of the sexes, from the will of the flesh, and from the will of man: and yet his body could not rise again to its former dignity by any power of its own, much less cease to be so that it might begin to be again in a different way. For this reason, the glad tidings were brought to us: that one baptism was given for the remission of sins, through which man is so...

# ETERNAL LIFE.

...one should be born again of water and the Holy Spirit <note>original: "ex aqua & Spiritu ſancto"; a reference to the Gospel of John 3:5</note>, so that his soul, as if by a new birth, should be reborn and become a partaker of the pure humanity of Christ the Savior, which was fashioned by the Holy Spirit. This rebirth restores the soul to its former state of innocence, while simultaneously removing sin. And we believe this to be entirely real in its nature: we do not embrace these things as mere allegories or metaphors for the truth. Rather, these things truly and actually happen to the baptized in such a way that God allows a testimony of that actual grace, conferred through baptism, to be physically transmitted into the body. 

It is in this respect, certainly, that the **Mohammedans** <note>A historical term for Muslims</note> receive baptism, insofar as it removes an innate stench that would otherwise last their whole lives—a scent which we otherwise observe today in all **Hebrews** <note>The author is referencing a common, though prejudiced, medieval and early modern theological myth called the *foetor judaicus*, or "Jewish odor," which was claimed to be miraculously removed by Christian baptism</note>. Thus, the internal effect of baptism also shines forth outwardly. Indeed, this confirms that the effect of a single baptism is perpetual and indelible. 

Yet, this rebirth does not remove death; instead, it leaves Christians burdened with a corrupt body, generated by the will of man. To this extent, it nonetheless leaves the soul subject to the vices of the corrupt body. Therefore, baptism was not sufficient for adults, even though it may be abundantly enough for younger ones as long as they remain innocent. Consequently, another privilege was proclaimed through which adults can possess eternal life: that whoever shall eat the body of the Lord <term>Dominicum corpus; the consecrated bread of the Eucharist</term> worthily, Christ will raise him up to life on the last day. If, however, he does not eat, he shall not have life in himself. For this mystery has been given to us for the life of the world. There is, to be sure, the **Adam-like life** <note>The fallen, mortal life inherited from the biblical Adam</note> of the world, which is fleeting and almost animalistic. In exchange for this, we are given a pledge, as well as an actual and real participation in eternal life. 

The merits of the Lord’s passion are therefore communicated to us through participation in the pure virginity of Christ the Lord. For the communion of His most pure and most chaste body unites us to Him and actually regenerates us within Him; and thus He

<column-break/>

gives us a life conformed to Himself. The body of the Lord is given for the life of the world. And although the human body, conceived from blood, does not perish immediately, by that very act by which we are united with the body of the Lord and His humanity, He makes us partakers of His incomprehensible incarnation. He restores us to the former integrity of human nature, insofar as we acquire, through participation, that most pure virginity of Christ in which we must be saved. Moreover, because of this loving union with Him, participation in the merits of His passion is granted to us. Therefore, the most principal effect of the sacrosanct Eucharist is participation in the purity and the uncorrupted virginal nature of the Lord Jesus. For this reason, it is preached with its own specific phrase: *the wine that produces virgins* <note>original: "vinum germinans virgines"; a mystical reading of Zechariah 9:17</note>.

Furthermore, the Apostle <note>Saint Paul</note> teaches that this mystery of ineffable divine love works the aforementioned real effects of regeneration in human nature. He says: *We shall all indeed rise again, but we shall not all be changed* <note>1 Corinthians 15:51</note>. It is as if he were saying: All mortals will at some point rise from death. The damned will indeed rise, but they will be in no way changed; they will remain in the former Adam-like body—heavy, non-penetrating <note>In scholastic theology, "penetration" or "subtlety" was the ability of a glorified body to pass through physical objects</note>, etc.—with only the "necessity of death" (which they might otherwise wish for) taken away from them. 

Children, however, reborn only by the washing of baptism, will rise in a body that is to some extent glorified, but they will be less perfect to the degree that they were distant from such great happiness <note>The author suggests children who die after baptism but without the Eucharist occupy a different state of glory</note>. But those who were united in the communion of the Lord’s body will rise entirely glorious throughout their whole nature, because they were most perfectly regenerated in life. Although visible signs of this regeneration did not appear then, they were nonetheless truly present within; for these qualities are not made anew in the resurrection unless they had previously existed in this world through a complete regeneration. Our faith is not about non-entities, but about real things that are not visible, because God wishes us to earn our reward through faith. Therefore, however much this symbol of love and union with God may be utterly inscrutable, just as its effects are currently invisible:

...nevertheless, the aforementioned mystical and real rebirth is still considered earthly according to the understanding of Nicodemus <note>A reference to the Pharisee who questioned Jesus about being "born again" in John 3</note>, and under that title, I have transferred the discussion here.
